paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: Let (y in Y) -> (x in X) be a finite morphism that is etale in codimension one. Do the Frobenius volume and Hilbert-Kunz Frobenius volume satisfy the finite-degree formulas Fvol(y, Y) = deg(f) Fvol(x, X) and Fvol_HN(y, Y) = deg(f) Fvol_HN(x, X)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p>0$, and let $(x \in X)$ be a normal local singularity of finite type over $k$. For a Cartier (or $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier) setup, let $\mathrm{Fvol}(x,X)$ denote the Frobenius volume of $(x \in X)$, defined via the asymptotic behaviour of $\dim_k H^0$-type invariants under iterations of the Frobenius morphism, and let $\mathrm{Fvol}_{HN}(x,X)$ denote the Hilbert–Kunz Frobenius volume, defined analogously using Hilbert–Kunz type asymptotics.

Suppose 
$$f \colon (y \in Y) \longrightarrow (x \in X)$$
is a finite dominant morphism between normal local singularities that is étale in codimension one (i.e. the ramification locus of $f$ has codimension at least two in $Y$). Let $\deg(f)$ denote the degree of the field extension $K(Y)/K(X)$.

Prove or disprove the following finite-degree (multiplicativity) formulas:
$$\mathrm{Fvol}(y,Y) \;=\; \deg(f)\cdot \mathrm{Fvol}(x,X),$$
$$\mathrm{Fvol}_{HN}(y,Y) \;=\; \deg(f)\cdot \mathrm{Fvol}_{HN}(x,X).$$
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of open problems on K-stability of Fano varieties. While analogous transformation/multiplicativity rules under finite covers étale in codimension one are known for F-signature, Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity, and certain limit-multiplicity invariants (work of Carvajal-Rojas–Smolkin–Tucker and others), no published proof of the stated equalities for the Frobenius volume Fvol and Hilbert–Kunz Frobenius volume Fvol_HN was found. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Develop software to generate benchmark parameterized linear systems that are generally accepted as relevant in practice and suitable for theoretical analysis.
self_contained_problem:
A parameterized linear system is a family of linear systems of the form A(p) x = b(p), where p = (p_1, ..., p_k) ranges over a parameter domain P ⊂ R^k (or C^k), A(p) is an n × n matrix whose entries depend on p, and b(p) is an n-vector whose entries depend on p; the entries are typically given as polynomial, rational, or interval-valued functions of the parameters. Design and implement a software framework that automatically generates benchmark instances of such parameterized linear systems satisfying the following requirements:

(1) The generated families are representative of problems arising in engineering and scientific practice (e.g., from structural analysis, electrical networks, control theory, discretized PDEs with uncertain coefficients, or interval/affine parametric models), so that they are widely accepted as practically relevant test cases.

(2) The generated families are simultaneously suitable for rigorous theoretical analysis, meaning that each instance is accompanied by a precise mathematical specification (parameter domain, dependency functions, structural properties such as symmetry, sparsity pattern, conditioning bounds, solution-set descriptions where applicable) sufficient to permit proofs of correctness and complexity bounds for solvers acting on it.

(3) The generator is parameterized itself (allowing control over dimension n, number of parameters k, type of dependency, conditioning, and structural features) and produces reproducible instances together with reference solutions or solution enclosures.

Provide such a generator and justify that the produced benchmark suite meets criteria (1)–(3).
status_search_result: The task is a software/benchmarking development goal rather than a closed-form mathematical conjecture. No widely accepted, comprehensive benchmark generator for parameterized linear systems meeting both practical relevance and theoretical-analysis suitability appears to have been established; while individual test collections (e.g., interval/parametric examples in INTLAB, examples in the literature on parametric linear systems) exist, a general-purpose generator as described remains an open research/engineering goal.

original_question: Algebraic Multigrid Analysis for Theoretical Computer Scientists: Show that for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices $M$, Algebraic Multigrid runs in time $~O(nnz(M))$ to compute an (implicitly represented) symmetric matrix $Z$, which can be applied in $O(nnz(M))$ time, and satisfies the condition that $ Omega(1) M^-1 Z O(1) M^-1$. In particular, the constants are independent of the problem size $n$.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbf{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be a symmetric weakly column diagonally dominant M-matrix (SWCDDM); i.e., $\mathbf{M}$ is symmetric, all off-diagonal entries are nonpositive, all diagonal entries are positive, and for every column $j$ one has $\mathbf{M}_{jj} \ge \sum_{i \ne j} |\mathbf{M}_{ij}|$. Assume in addition that $\mathbf{M}$ is polynomially bounded, meaning that the ratio of the largest to smallest nonzero magnitudes among the entries of $\mathbf{M}$ is bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(n)$. Let $\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M})$ denote the number of nonzero entries of $\mathbf{M}$. For symmetric positive (semi)definite matrices $\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}$, write $\mathbf{A} \preceq \mathbf{B}$ for the Loewner order, i.e. $\mathbf{B} - \mathbf{A}$ is positive semidefinite. The notation $\widetilde{O}(\cdot)$ hides factors polylogarithmic in $n$.

Problem. Prove that there is an Algebraic Multigrid algorithm that, given any such polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrix $\mathbf{M}$:
(i) runs in time $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$;
(ii) outputs an implicit representation of a symmetric matrix $\mathbf{Z}$ such that, for any vector $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the product $\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{b}$ can be computed in $O(\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$ time;
(iii) produces $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfying the spectral approximation
$$\Omega(1)\,\mathbf{M}^{-1} \;\preceq\; \mathbf{Z} \;\preceq\; O(1)\,\mathbf{M}^{-1},$$
where the hidden constants are absolute and independent of $n$.
status_search_result: No direct evidence was found establishing or refuting an Algebraic Multigrid algorithm with the stated $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$ runtime and $O(1)$-spectral-approximation guarantee for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices, with constants independent of $n$. While nearly-linear-time SDD/Laplacian solvers (Spielman–Teng and successors) and AMG variants such as LAMG are known, the specific theoretical guarantee posed here for general AMG on this matrix class does not appear settled in the search results.

original_question: Can we solve an $(n,k,0,kappa)$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $~ O(k^omega + nnz(A)kappa)$ arithmetic operations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the matrix multiplication exponent, and for a matrix $A$ let $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ denote the number of nonzero entries of $A$. Call a linear system $Ax=b$ an $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ system if $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is invertible, has at most $k$ singular values that exceed the smallest singular value by more than a constant factor (equivalently, $A$ can be written as a well-conditioned matrix plus a perturbation of rank at most $k$), the perturbation has rank exactly $k$ with no additional noise term, and the well-conditioned part has condition number at most $\kappa$.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given such an $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ system $Ax=b$ and a target accuracy $\varepsilon>0$, computes a vector $\widetilde x$ with $\|\widetilde x - A^{-1}b\|\le \varepsilon \|A^{-1}b\|$ using
$$\widetilde O\!\left(k^{\omega} + \mathrm{nnz}(A)\cdot \kappa\right)$$
arithmetic operations, where $\widetilde O(\cdot)$ hides polylogarithmic factors in $n$, $\kappa$, and $1/\varepsilon$?

original_question: What is the complexity of solving $(n,0,l,kappa)$ linear systems, and how is this affected by the model of computation (direct access vs matrix-vector product)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be a non-singular matrix with singular values $\sigma_1 \geq \sigma_2 \geq \cdots \geq \sigma_n > 0$. Fix integers $0 \leq l \leq n$ and a real number $\kappa \geq 1$. Say that $A$ is an $(n, 0, l, \kappa)$ matrix (a system with $l$ small singular outliers and no large outliers) if:
- the top $n - l$ singular values are well-conditioned in the sense that $\sigma_1 / \sigma_{n-l} \leq \kappa$, and
- the bottom $l$ singular values $\sigma_{n-l+1}, \ldots, \sigma_n$ may be arbitrarily small (the "small singular outliers").

For $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and a target accuracy $\varepsilon > 0$, the $(n, 0, l, \kappa)$ linear-system problem is to compute $\widehat{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|\widehat{x} - A^{-1} b\| \leq \varepsilon \|A^{-1} b\|$.

Consider two computational models:
(i) Direct-access model: an algorithm may read individual entries of $A$ and $b$ at unit cost and perform arithmetic operations.
(ii) Matrix–vector product model: an algorithm may, at unit cost per query, choose a vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and receive $A v$ (or $A^\top v$), in addition to arithmetic on the returned vectors.

Determine the asymptotic query/arithmetic complexity, as a function of $n$, $l$, $\kappa$, and $\varepsilon$, of solving $(n, 0, l, \kappa)$ linear systems in each of these two models, and quantify the gap (if any) between the two models.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of open questions from a numerical linear algebra workshop. No published resolution was found in available searches; standard results give an O(√κ log(1/ε)) matrix-vector iteration upper bound for the well-conditioned bulk, but the precise dependence on the number l of small singular outliers and the gap between direct-access and matrix-vector models is not settled.

original_question: What is the bit complexity of solving $(n,k,l,kappa)$ linear systems? In particular, does the $~ O(k^omega + n^2kappa)$ running time for $(n,k,0,kappa)$ systems extend to the Word-RAM model?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the matrix multiplication exponent. Consider the following class of structured linear systems. An $(n, k, \ell, \kappa)$ linear system is a system $A x = b$ where $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is an invertible matrix that admits a decomposition $A = D + U V^{\top}$ in which:
- $D \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is a block-diagonal matrix consisting of blocks of size at most $k \times k$,
- $U, V \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times \ell}$ are low-rank correction factors of rank at most $\ell$,
- $\kappa$ is an upper bound on the condition number of $A$,
- the entries of $A$ and $b$ are rational numbers with bounded bit-length.

Assume that in the Real-RAM (or arithmetic) model of computation one can solve $(n, k, 0, \kappa)$ systems (i.e., the purely block-diagonal case with no low-rank correction) in $\widetilde{O}(k^{\omega} + n^2 \kappa)$ arithmetic operations, where $\widetilde{O}$ hides polylogarithmic factors.

Question. Determine the bit complexity, in the Word-RAM model with logarithmic-size machine words, of solving $(n, k, \ell, \kappa)$ linear systems. In particular, does there exist a Word-RAM algorithm that solves every $(n, k, 0, \kappa)$ linear system using $\widetilde{O}(k^{\omega} + n^2 \kappa)$ bit operations (up to polylogarithmic factors in $n$, $k$, $\kappa$, and the input bit-length)?
status_search_result: No authoritative source could be located confirming or refuting a Word-RAM bit-complexity bound of $\widetilde{O}(k^{\omega} + n^2\kappa)$ for $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ structured linear systems, nor a more general bound for $(n,k,\ell,\kappa)$ systems. The question is posed as an open problem and no resolution was found.

original_question: Several specific open problems that exist in this context are mentioned in~. More generally, try to extend the approach in~ to other types of PDEs or preconditioners.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a partial differential equation (PDE) discretized by a standard numerical method (e.g., finite differences, finite elements, isogeometric analysis) on a sequence of grids of increasing resolution, producing a sequence of large sparse matrices $\{A_n\}$ whose dimensions $d_n \to \infty$. Assume $A_n$ is paired with a preconditioner $P_n$ so that one studies the spectrum of $P_n^{-1} A_n$. A spectral symbol for the sequence $\{P_n^{-1} A_n\}$ is a measurable function $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$ (with $\Omega$ a domain of finite measure) such that, for every continuous compactly supported test function $F$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{d_n} \sum_{j=1}^{d_n} F(\lambda_j(P_n^{-1} A_n)) = \frac{1}{|\Omega|} \int_{\Omega} F(f(x))\, dx.$$
Suppose that for a particular family of PDEs (e.g., constant-coefficient elliptic problems on tensor-product domains) and a particular family of preconditioners (e.g., multigrid, ILU, or Schwarz-type), one has identified explicit spectral symbols $f$ that fully describe the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of $\{P_n^{-1} A_n\}$, including localization of outlier eigenvalues and conditioning estimates.

Problem: Extend this symbol-based spectral analysis to broader classes of PDEs and/or preconditioners. Specifically, identify and rigorously prove explicit spectral symbols $f$ describing the asymptotic eigenvalue distribution of $\{P_n^{-1} A_n\}$ in settings such as: (i) variable-coefficient or non-self-adjoint elliptic operators; (ii) time-dependent (parabolic or hyperbolic) PDEs and their all-at-once or space-time discretizations; (iii) saddle-point or coupled multi-physics systems (e.g., Stokes, Maxwell); and (iv) preconditioners not previously covered by such an analysis, including algebraic multigrid, domain decomposition with inexact subdomain solves, and sparse approximate inverse preconditioners. In each case, determine whether the resulting symbol yields uniform spectral clustering away from zero and dimension-independent convergence rates for standard Krylov iterations.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a general research direction: extending symbol-based (GLT-style) spectral analysis of preconditioned PDE matrices to additional PDE classes and preconditioners. Such extensions are an active area of research with many specific subproblems remaining open; no single comprehensive resolution is known.

original_question: Find an interesting (nonselfdajoint resp. nonsymmetric) model problem, where the theoretical result on the eigenvalue distribution of the preconditioned matrix indeed corresponds to the actual convergence behavior of GMRES (e.g., $M^-1A$ has $m$ eigenvalue clusters and an acceptable approximate solution is obtained by GMRES in $ O(m)$ steps). Determine which particular properties of the problem implied this correspondence.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a nonsingular, non-Hermitian (nonsymmetric) matrix and let $M \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a nonsingular preconditioner. Consider the linear system $Ax = b$ solved by the (left) preconditioned GMRES method applied to $M^{-1}A x = M^{-1}b$, starting from $x_0 = 0$, which at step $k$ produces the iterate $x_k$ minimizing $\|M^{-1}(b - A x_k)\|_2$ over the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_k(M^{-1}A, M^{-1}b)$.

Suppose the spectrum $\sigma(M^{-1}A)$ can be partitioned into $m$ clusters, i.e., there exist $m$ points $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m \in \mathbb{C}$ (bounded away from $0$) and a small radius $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$$\sigma(M^{-1}A) \subset \bigcup_{j=1}^{m} D(\lambda_j, \varepsilon),$$
where $D(\lambda,\varepsilon)$ denotes the closed disk of radius $\varepsilon$ around $\lambda$.

Task: Exhibit a concrete and mathematically interesting non-Hermitian model problem $(A, M)$ — for instance arising from the discretization of a non-self-adjoint partial differential or integral operator together with a natural preconditioner — for which the following correspondence between the spectral clustering of $M^{-1}A$ and the actual convergence behavior of GMRES provably holds: an acceptable approximate solution (i.e., relative residual below a prescribed tolerance independent of $n$) is obtained in $\mathcal{O}(m)$ GMRES iterations, with constants independent of the discretization parameter. Identify and rigorously justify which structural properties of the problem (e.g., normality or near-normality of $M^{-1}A$, bounds on the field of values, departure from normality, conditioning of the eigenvector basis, regularity of the underlying continuous operator, or bounds on pseudospectra) are responsible for ensuring that the eigenvalue clustering translates into the predicted GMRES convergence rate.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open-ended research desideratum asking for example problems where eigenvalue-cluster-based GMRES convergence bounds are sharp, together with identification of the structural properties responsible. The literature (e.g., Greenbaum–Pták–Strakoš 1996 showing that any nonincreasing residual curve can correspond to any spectrum) emphasizes that eigenvalues alone do not determine GMRES convergence in the nonnormal case, and partial answers exist for nearly normal operators or via field-of-values/pseudospectra arguments. No definitive resolution is recorded; the problem appears to remain open as stated.

original_question: Taking the above recurrences to represent the CG or steepest descent algorithm, determine conditions on $A$ that will insure that the norms of the vectors $r_k$ drop below the machine precision in finite precision arithmetic or show some examples where they do not.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Consider the iterates produced by the conjugate gradient (CG) method or the steepest descent method applied to the linear system $Ax = b$, starting from some initial guess $x_0$ with initial residual $r_0 = b - A x_0$. In exact arithmetic these methods generate a sequence of approximate solutions $x_k$ and residual vectors $r_k = b - A x_k$ satisfying the standard recurrences:
- Steepest descent: $\alpha_k = \frac{r_k^T r_k}{r_k^T A r_k}$, $x_{k+1} = x_k + \alpha_k r_k$, $r_{k+1} = r_k - \alpha_k A r_k$.
- CG: with search directions $p_0 = r_0$, $\alpha_k = \frac{r_k^T r_k}{p_k^T A p_k}$, $x_{k+1} = x_k + \alpha_k p_k$, $r_{k+1} = r_k - \alpha_k A p_k$, $\beta_k = \frac{r_{k+1}^T r_{k+1}}{r_k^T r_k}$, $p_{k+1} = r_{k+1} + \beta_k p_k$.

Now suppose these recurrences are executed in finite-precision floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff $u$ (machine precision). The computed residual vectors $\tilde r_k$ may stagnate above $u\,\|b\|$ or below it depending on $A$.

Determine sufficient (and, where possible, necessary) conditions on the matrix $A$ (e.g., on its spectrum, condition number, eigenvalue distribution, or structure) under which the computed residual norms $\|\tilde r_k\|$ eventually fall below the machine precision level (e.g., $\|\tilde r_k\| \le c\, u\, \|b\|$ for a modest constant $c$) as $k$ grows. Alternatively, exhibit explicit examples of symmetric positive definite matrices $A$ for which $\|\tilde r_k\|$ never drops below the machine precision in either CG or steepest descent run in finite precision arithmetic.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this question was located. The behavior of finite-precision residuals in CG and steepest descent has been extensively studied (Greenbaum, Strakoš, Gutknecht, Paige, and others), and it is known that maximum attainable accuracy is governed by the gap between the true and updated residuals, but a complete characterization of matrices $A$ guaranteeing $\|\tilde r_k\|$ below machine precision is not established in the literature surveyed; the question appears to remain open in the general form posed.

original_question: How many bits of precision are necessary to guarantee that CG applied to an $n$ by $n$ SPD linear system $Ax=b$ obtains an approximate solution with normwise backward error at most $epsilon$ in $n$ (or fewer) steps?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be a symmetric positive definite matrix and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Consider the conjugate gradient (CG) method applied to the linear system $Ax = b$, implemented in finite-precision floating-point arithmetic with $t$ bits of precision (unit roundoff $u = 2^{-t}$). Given a tolerance $\varepsilon > 0$, an approximate solution $\tilde{x}$ is said to have normwise backward error at most $\varepsilon$ if there exist a perturbation matrix $\Delta A$ and a perturbation vector $\Delta b$ with
$$\|\Delta A\| \le \varepsilon \|A\|, \qquad \|\Delta b\| \le \varepsilon \|b\|,$$
such that $(A + \Delta A)\tilde{x} = b + \Delta b$ (in some fixed norm, e.g. the 2-norm).

Determine the minimum number of bits of precision $t = t(n,\varepsilon, A, b)$ that suffices to guarantee that CG, run on $A$ and $b$ in floating-point arithmetic with precision $t$, produces in at most $n$ iterations an approximate solution whose normwise backward error is at most $\varepsilon$. Equivalently, find sharp upper and lower bounds on the precision required, as a function of $n$, $\varepsilon$, and (possibly) properties of $A$ such as the condition number $\kappa(A)$, that ensure CG terminates within $n$ steps with normwise backward error $\le \varepsilon$.
category_tag: Numerical linear algebra / finite-precision conjugate gradient
status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., 2024–2025 analyses of finite-precision and mixed-precision (preconditioned) CG) provide partial backward-error bounds of the form $O(u)\kappa(A)^{1/2}$ under various assumptions, but a sharp characterization of the number of bits of precision needed so that CG attains normwise backward error $\le \varepsilon$ within $n$ steps for any SPD system is not established. The question of necessary/sufficient precision for CG to converge in at most $n$ steps to a given backward-error level appears to remain open.

original_question: Extend Paige's analysis of the Lanczos algorithm to the block Lanczos algorithm. The exact analysis will depend on the use of an orthogonalization scheme used within blocks, so either specify certain assumptions on the accuracy of the scheme, or analyze a standard ``good'' algorithm.
status_search_result: A 2025 paper "On finite precision block Lanczos computations" (arXiv:2507.16484, BIT Numerical Mathematics) extends Paige/Greenbaum-type analysis to the block Lanczos algorithm, generalizing the backward-error/continuation interpretation in terms of a nearby larger model matrix and deriving sufficient conditions on the intra-block orthogonalization for the perturbations to remain small. However, the authors note that whereas in the single-vector case these conditions can always be met, in the block case it remains open whether they can always be satisfied, so the program is only partially completed.

original_question: Deterministic Minami Perturbation: Minami showed that if $A$ is $n x n$ Hermitian tridiagonal and $E$ is a random diagonal matrix with independent absolutely continuous entries, then $gap(A+delta E) C(delta/n)^c$ for some constants $C,c$ depending on the distribution of the entries. Give an efficient deterministic algorithm for finding such a perturbation. Here, efficient means faster than the parent algorithm in which it is used, so $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ for diagonalization and, ambitiously, $O(nnz(A) ^c(n/delta))$ or $O(nnz(A) ^c(n)/delta^c)$ for Krylov methods.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Hermitian tridiagonal matrix, and for a diagonal matrix $E=\mathrm{diag}(e_1,\dots,e_n)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and a parameter $\delta>0$, define the perturbed matrix $A+\delta E$. Write $\mathrm{gap}(M):=\min_{i\neq j}|\lambda_i(M)-\lambda_j(M)|$ for the minimum eigenvalue gap of a Hermitian matrix $M$.

A theorem of Minami (1996) asserts that there exist absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that, when the entries $e_1,\dots,e_n$ are independent and absolutely continuous (e.g.\ uniform on $[-1,1]$), the random perturbation satisfies
$$\Pr\!\big[\mathrm{gap}(A+\delta E)\ \ge\ C(\delta/n)^c\big]\ \ge\ 1/2.$$

Problem. Design a deterministic algorithm which, given $A$ and $\delta>0$, outputs a diagonal matrix $E\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ with $\|E\|\le 1$ such that
$$\mathrm{gap}(A+\delta E)\ \ge\ C(\delta/n)^c$$
for some absolute constants $C,c>0$, and which runs in time
$$O\!\big(n^3\,\log^c(n/\delta)\big)$$
(matching the cost of dense Hermitian diagonalization), and, more ambitiously, in time
$$O\!\big(\mathrm{nnz}(A)\,\log^c(n/\delta)\big)\quad\text{or}\quad O\!\big(\mathrm{nnz}(A)\,\log^c(n)/\delta^c\big)$$
suitable for use inside Krylov-subspace eigensolvers, where $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ is the number of nonzero entries of $A$.
category_tag: Numerical linear algebra / spectral gap perturbations
status_search_result: No source located that supplies a deterministic algorithmic version of Minami's eigenvalue-gap perturbation lemma for Hermitian tridiagonal matrices at the requested complexity. Recent work on deterministic Hermitian eigensolvers (e.g., the ICALP 2025 deterministic complexity analysis based on Gu–Eisenstat divide-and-conquer with the FMM) addresses related deterministic eigenproblem questions but does not provide a deterministic Minami perturbation. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For a given $A ^n x n$, let $ V$ denote an approximate invariant subspace of dimension $d$ of $A$, in the sense that there exists some $d$-dimensional invariant subspace $ V$ of $A$ such that $ ( V, V)$ is small. Let $ W$ be some other subspace of dimension $r<n-d$. Suppose the columns of $Q$ form an orthonormal basis for the (generically) $d+r$ dimensional space $ Q = V + W$. Provide conditions that will ensure that $d$ eigenvalues of $Q*AQ$ approximate the $d$ eigenvalues of $A$ associated with the invariant subspace $ V$. Impose assumptions about the eigenvalues of $A$ corresponding to $ V$, as needed.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a $d$-dimensional invariant subspace of $A$, so that $A\mathcal{V}\subseteq\mathcal{V}$. Let $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be another $d$-dimensional subspace which is an approximate invariant subspace, in the sense that the largest principal angle $\angle(\mathcal{V},\widehat{\mathcal{V}})$ is small. Let $\mathcal{W}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a further subspace of dimension $r$ with $r < n-d$, and assume that, generically, $\dim(\widehat{\mathcal{V}}+\mathcal{W})=d+r$. Set $\mathcal{Q}=\widehat{\mathcal{V}}+\mathcal{W}$ and let $Q\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times(d+r)}$ have orthonormal columns spanning $\mathcal{Q}$, so the Rayleigh–Ritz matrix is $H = Q^*AQ\in\mathbb{C}^{(d+r)\times(d+r)}$.
 
Denote by $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ the eigenvalues of $A$ associated with $\mathcal{V}$ (i.e.\ the eigenvalues of $A\big|_{\mathcal{V}}$), and by $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{d+r}$ the eigenvalues of $H$ (the Ritz values of $A$ from $\mathcal{Q}$).
 
Problem. Formulate and prove explicit conditions — including any necessary spectral separation hypotheses on $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ relative to the remaining eigenvalues of $A$, and on the geometric configuration of $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}$, $\mathcal{W}$, and the invariant subspaces of $A$ — under which exactly $d$ of the Ritz values $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{d+r}$ approximate $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$, and provide quantitative bounds on the corresponding errors $|\mu_{i_k}-\lambda_k|$ in terms of $\angle(\mathcal{V},\widehat{\mathcal{V}})$, the spectral gaps, and $\|A\|$.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this exact open problem could be confirmed. Classical Rayleigh–Ritz / Ritz value perturbation theory (Saad, Stewart–Sun, Knyazev, Jia, and others) provides bounds when the trial subspace itself is close to an invariant subspace, but the refined setting where the trial subspace is an enlargement $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}+\mathcal{W}$ with only $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}$ approximating an invariant subspace appears not to have a definitive published answer of the form requested.

original_question: Consider a non-Hermitian $A ^n x n$ and suppose $Q ^n x k$ has orthonormal columns. We know that the Ritz values (eigenvalues of $Q*AQ$) are located in the numerical range, $W(A) = v*Av: |v |_2=1 $, a closed, convex subset of $ $ that contains the eigenvalues of $A$ (and, potentially, points far from these eigenvalues). What can be said (deterministically or probabalistically) about the distribution of the Ritz values across $W(A)$ for $1<k<n$? What if $Q$ is restricted to be a basis for a Krylov subspace? What if $Q$ is the basis for a random subspace?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a (generally non-Hermitian) matrix, and let $Q \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times k}$ have orthonormal columns, with $1 < k < n$. The Ritz values of $A$ with respect to the column space of $Q$ are the eigenvalues of the compression $Q^* A Q \in \mathbb{C}^{k\times k}$. Let
$$W(A) = \{v^* A v : v \in \mathbb{C}^n,\ \|v\|_2 = 1\}$$
denote the numerical range of $A$, a closed convex subset of $\mathbb{C}$ that contains the spectrum of $A$ but may also contain points far from it. It is classical that every Ritz value lies in $W(A)$.

Provide a quantitative description, either deterministic or probabilistic, of how the $k$ Ritz values distribute themselves within $W(A)$. In particular, address the following three settings:

(a) The general case, where $Q$ is an arbitrary $n\times k$ matrix with orthonormal columns.

(b) The Krylov case, where the column space of $Q$ equals the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b) = \mathrm{span}\{b, Ab, A^2 b, \dots, A^{k-1} b\}$ for some starting vector $b \in \mathbb{C}^n$.

(c) The random case, where the column space of $Q$ is a uniformly distributed (Haar-random) $k$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{C}^n$.

Determine, in each setting, what can be proved about the empirical distribution of Ritz values in $W(A)$ as a function of $A$, $k$, and (where applicable) the starting vector $b$.
category_tag: Ritz value distribution for non-Hermitian matrices
status_search_result: The distribution of Ritz values inside the numerical range of a non-Hermitian matrix is broadly recognized as poorly understood beyond basic localization (Ritz values lie in W(A)). Existing work (e.g., Ritz value localization for non-Hermitian matrices by Carden–Embree, and recent work on estimating the numerical range with a Krylov subspace) provides partial bounds and estimates, but a full deterministic or probabilistic description—especially for general orthonormal Q, Krylov subspaces, and Haar-random subspaces—remains open.

original_question: Let $B$ be an $n x n$ (upper) bidiagonal matrix. Is there an algorithm that, in $O(kn)$ operations, can produce $k$ triples $(sigma_i,v_i,u_i)$ such that $sigma_i >= 0$, $v_i, u_i C^n$ are unit vectors, and, for machine precision $epsilon$, $ |Bv_i-sigma_iu_i |_2 = O(epsilon n |B |_2)$; $|v_i^Hv_j|$, $|u_i^Hu_j| = O(epsilon n)$ if $i != j$.
self_contained_problem:
Let $B \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ be an upper bidiagonal matrix (i.e., $B_{ij} = 0$ unless $j = i$ or $j = i+1$), and let $\epsilon > 0$ denote a fixed machine precision. Let $1 \le k \le n$ be an integer. Does there exist an algorithm that, using only $O(kn)$ arithmetic floating-point operations (in a standard model of floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff $\epsilon$), produces $k$ triples $(\sigma_i, v_i, u_i)$ for $i = 1, \ldots, k$ with $\sigma_i \ge 0$ and $v_i, u_i \in \mathbb{C}^n$ unit vectors (in the Euclidean norm) such that the following hold:

1. (Approximate singular triple) For every $i \in \{1,\ldots,k\}$,
$$\|B v_i - \sigma_i u_i\|_2 = O(\epsilon\, n\, \|B\|_2).$$

2. (Numerical orthogonality) For all $i \ne j$ in $\{1,\ldots,k\}$,
$$|v_i^H v_j| = O(\epsilon\, n), \qquad |u_i^H u_j| = O(\epsilon\, n).$$

Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ denotes the spectral (operator $2$-) norm for matrices and the Euclidean norm for vectors, and $v^H$ denotes the conjugate transpose. The implicit constants in the $O(\cdot)$ bounds must be independent of $B$, $n$, $k$, and $\epsilon$.
status_search_result: The MRRR (Multiple Relatively Robust Representations) approach has been proposed to compute k singular triples of a bidiagonal matrix in O(kn) time and storage. However, a fully stable, provably correct version of MRRR for the SVD with the required residual and numerical-orthogonality guarantees is not publicly available in standard libraries such as LAPACK; existing implementations (e.g., BDSVDX, based on an associated tridiagonal eigenproblem) do not achieve the O(kn) complexity together with the stated accuracy guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Prove stronger theoretical bounds for GECP applied to $K$, by exploiting the structure of the kernel $K$.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ be the Lehmann kernel, by which we mean a symmetric positive semidefinite kernel of the form
$$K(x,y)=\min(x,y)\,(1-\max(x,y))$$
(the Green's function for $-d^2/dx^2$ on $[0,1]$ with Dirichlet boundary data), and for any set of nodes $0<x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_n<1$ let $K_n\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be the kernel matrix with entries $(K_n)_{ij}=K(x_i,x_j)$.

Apply Gaussian Elimination with Complete Pivoting (GECP) to $K_n$. Recall that GECP produces, after $n$ steps, a factorization $P K_n Q = L U$ with $L$ unit lower triangular, $|L_{ij}|\le 1$, and $U$ upper triangular; let $K_n^{(k)}$ denote the trailing Schur complement after $k$ elimination steps, and define the growth factor
$$\rho_n(K_n) \;=\; \frac{\max_{k,i,j}\bigl|\bigl(K_n^{(k)}\bigr)_{ij}\bigr|}{\max_{i,j}|(K_n)_{ij}|}.$$
Wilkinson's general bound gives $\rho_n \le n^{1/2}\bigl(2\cdot 3^{1/2}\cdots n^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)^{1/2}$ for an arbitrary $n\times n$ matrix.

Problem. By exploiting the structure of the Lehmann kernel $K$ (its total positivity, smoothness, and Green's-function representation), prove growth-factor bounds for GECP applied to $K_n$ that are strictly stronger than Wilkinson's general bound; in particular, establish whether $\rho_n(K_n)$ can be bounded by a polylogarithmic function of $n$, or even by a constant independent of $n$ and of the choice of nodes $\{x_i\}$, and derive correspondingly improved bounds on the entrywise backward error of the resulting LU factorization.
category_tag: Numerical linear algebra: pivoting growth factors
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate any published result establishing structure-exploiting GECP growth bounds specifically for Lehmann kernel matrices. Recent activity on GECP growth (e.g., Bisain–Edelman–Urschel 2023 improving Wilkinson's bound, and work on butterfly and orthogonal matrices) addresses general or different structured classes, leaving the Lehmann-kernel case unaddressed in the literature found. Status is therefore reported as open based on absence of a matching solution.

original_question: Consider selecting $r = O(k)$ uniformly random row indices $I$ and then choosing column indices $~J$ so that $A(I,:) A(I,~J) ~T$. What are sufficient conditions on $r$ and on the kernel $f$ which guarantee that | _~J A - A |_F <= c(n, m, k) | _J A - A |_F with high probability, where $c(n, m, k)$ grows at most logarithmically in its arguments? In other words, when does column selection on a random subset of the rows perform similarly to column selection on the full matrix?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \{x_1,\dots,x_m\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $Y = \{y_1,\dots,y_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, and let $f : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a (symmetric, positive semidefinite) kernel. Form the kernel matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ with entries $A_{ij} = f(x_i, y_j)$. For any index set $J \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, write $A(:,J)$ for the submatrix of $A$ with columns indexed by $J$, and let $\Pi_J A := A(:,J) A(:,J)^{+} A$ denote the orthogonal projection of the columns of $A$ onto the column span of $A(:,J)$. Fix a target rank $k$ and let $J^\star$ denote a (near-)optimal column index set of size $k$ minimizing $\|\Pi_J A - A\|_F$ over all $|J| = k$.

Now consider the following two-stage random subsampling procedure:
1. Sample $r = \mathcal{O}(k)$ row indices $I \subseteq \{1,\dots,m\}$ uniformly at random (with or without replacement).
2. Choose column indices $\widetilde{J}$ of size $k$ together with a coefficient matrix $\widetilde{T}$ such that $A(I,:) \approx A(I,\widetilde{J})\,\widetilde{T}$ (i.e., perform column subset selection on the sub-row matrix $A(I,:)$ rather than on $A$).

Determine sufficient conditions on the sample size $r$ and on the kernel $f$ which guarantee that, with high probability,
$$\|\Pi_{\widetilde{J}} A - A\|_F \;\le\; c(n,m,k)\, \|\Pi_{J^\star} A - A\|_F,$$
where $c(n,m,k)$ grows at most polylogarithmically in $n$, $m$, and $k$. In other words, characterize the regimes (in $r$ and in properties of $f$) in which column selection performed on a uniformly random subset of the rows is as accurate, up to polylogarithmic factors, as column selection on the full kernel matrix.
category_tag: randomized column subset selection for kernel matrices
status_search_result: Recent work on column and row subset selection (e.g., Cortinovis–Kressner 2020, and follow-ups through 2024–2025 on sublinear-time and randomized-embedding-based CSSP) provides partial results: sublinear-time algorithms based on uniformly random row sampling followed by strong RRQR refinement give approximation factors with polylogarithmic dependence in certain regimes, but a general characterization of sufficient conditions on the sample size $r$ and on the kernel $f$ that yields a polylogarithmic factor $c(n,m,k)$ for kernel matrices does not appear to have been completely established. The problem appears to remain open in the general kernel setting.

original_question: Sketch-and-solve: Let (A R^n x d ) be a full-rank matrix, (B R^n x p ) be a matrix, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $d$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let (~ X = (Omega^ -> p A)^+(Omega^ -> p B) R^d x p ) be the sketch-and-solve approximation to the ordinary least-squares solution $X = A^+B$. (Here, $^+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.) Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A ~ X - B |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) _X R^d x p |AX - B |_ F? ]
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $n,d,p,k$ be positive integers with $d\le n$. Call a (random) matrix $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ an oblivious subspace injection of dimension $d$ with injectivity $1-\varepsilon$ if, for every fixed $d$-dimensional subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with orthonormal basis $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$ the matrix $\Omega^{\top}U\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}$ has full column rank $d$ (equivalently, $\Omega$ is injective when restricted to $V$).

Problem. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be full column rank, let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, and let $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ be an oblivious subspace injection of dimension $d$ with injectivity $1-\varepsilon$. Define the sketch-and-solve approximation
$$\tilde X \;=\; (\Omega^{\top}A)^{+}(\Omega^{\top}B)\in\mathbb R^{d\times p},$$
where $M^{+}$ denotes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. Prove or disprove the following claim: it necessarily holds (with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$, or in expectation under any standard reading consistent with the injection guarantee) that
$$\|A\tilde X-B\|_{F}\;\le\;\bigl(1+\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\bigr)\,\min_{X\in\mathbb R^{d\times p}}\|AX-B\|_{F}.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_{F}$ is the Frobenius norm.
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint titled "Oblivious Subspace Injection Is Not Enough for Relative Error" explicitly disproves the claim: it constructs counterexamples showing that the OSI property alone does not yield $(1+O(\varepsilon))$ relative-error guarantees for sketch-and-solve least squares (nor for randomized SVD in Frobenius norm). The bound is recoverable only under a strengthened injectivity on appropriate augmented subspaces.

original_question: Regression in the $\ell_p$ norm: Consider the $ell_p$ linear regression problem minimize_x R^d |Ax - b |_ell_p for a matrix (A R^n x d ) and a vector (b R^n ). For a sketching matrix (Omega R^n x k ), the sketch-and-solve solution is [~ x argmin_x R^d |(Omega^ -> p Ax)-(Omega^ -> p b) |_ell_p. ] Formulate a generalization of the OSI property to the $ell_p$ regression problem which ensures that this procedure succeeds to constant-factor accuracy [ |A ~ x - b |_ell_p <= const* _x R^d |Ax - b |_ell_p. ]
self_contained_problem:
Let $1 \le p < \infty$. Consider the $\ell_p$ linear regression problem
$$\min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \|Ax - b\|_{\ell_p},$$
where $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ and $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Given a (possibly random) sketching matrix $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$, the sketch-and-solve estimator is
$$\tilde x \in \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \|\Omega^{\top} A x - \Omega^{\top} b\|_{\ell_p}.$$

Recall that, in the $\ell_2$ setting, the Oblivious Subspace Inequality / Embedding (OSI) property of $\Omega$ with respect to a subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ asserts that, with high probability over $\Omega$, the map $v \mapsto \Omega^\top v$ preserves $\ell_2$ norms on $V$ up to constant multiplicative distortion, which suffices to guarantee that the sketch-and-solve solution to $\ell_2$ regression achieves
$$\|A\tilde x - b\|_{\ell_2} \le C \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}\|Ax - b\|_{\ell_2}$$
for an absolute constant $C$.

Task: Formulate an analogous "$\ell_p$-OSI" condition on the sketching matrix $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ (depending only on $\Omega$ and possibly on the column span of $A$ and the residual direction, but not on any a priori bound on the $\ell_p$ norm dilation of $\Omega$) such that, whenever $\Omega$ satisfies this condition, the sketch-and-solve estimator $\tilde x$ above satisfies
$$\|A\tilde x - b\|_{\ell_p} \le C_p \cdot \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}\|Ax - b\|_{\ell_p}$$
for a constant $C_p$ depending only on $p$. Prove that the proposed condition implies this constant-factor approximation guarantee.
category_tag: Sketching and randomized numerical linear algebra
status_search_result: The question asks for a formulation of a generalized OSI-type condition guaranteeing constant-factor sketch-and-solve accuracy for $\ell_p$ regression. While there is a substantial literature on $\ell_p$-subspace embeddings and Lewis-weight sampling (e.g., Sohler–Woodruff, Cohen–Peng, Wang–Woodruff) that gives constant-factor guarantees for $\ell_p$ regression, no single canonical "$\ell_p$-OSI" condition aligned with the framing of this open prompt has been verified. The status as a precise formulation problem is unknown.

original_question: Subspace injection properties of sparse random matrices: Assume the condition $r O(n/ n)$ relating the subspace dimension $r$ and the ambient dimension $n$. Prove or disprove: A SparseStack embedding with parameters $ = O(1)$ and $k = O(r)$ is an oblivious subspace injection with parameter $alpha = const$. More specifically, do parameters $ = 4$ and $k = 2r$ suffice to achieve the OSI property (for all sufficiently large $r$)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $n \geq 1$, $r \geq 1$ with $r \leq C\, n/\log n$ for some absolute constant $C > 0$. For positive integers $k$ and $\zeta$ with $\zeta \leq k$, define a SparseStack random matrix $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$ as follows. Form $\zeta$ independent random matrices $S_1,\dots,S_{\zeta} \in \mathbb{R}^{(k/\zeta) \times n}$, where each $S_i$ is a CountSketch matrix: every column of $S_i$ has exactly one nonzero entry, placed in a uniformly random row and equal to $\pm 1$ with equal probability, all column choices being independent. Set
$$S \;=\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{\zeta}}\begin{bmatrix} S_1 \\ \vdots \\ S_{\zeta} \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}.$$

Definition (Oblivious Subspace Injection). Given a constant $\alpha \in (0,1]$ and a function $r \mapsto k(r)$, a distribution over matrices $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$ is called an oblivious subspace injection (OSI) with parameter $\alpha$ for $r$-dimensional subspaces if, for every fixed $r$-dimensional linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, with probability at least $1 - o(1)$ (as $r \to \infty$),
$$\inf_{x \in V,\, \|x\|_2 = 1} \|S x\|_2 \;\geq\; \alpha.$$

Question. 
(a) Prove or disprove: there exist absolute constants $\zeta = O(1)$, $k = O(r)$, and $\alpha > 0$ such that the SparseStack distribution above is an oblivious subspace injection with parameter $\alpha$ for all $r$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$, whenever $r \leq C\, n/\log n$.

(b) More specifically, do the choices $\zeta = 4$ and $k = 2r$ suffice to yield the OSI property (with some absolute constant $\alpha > 0$) for all sufficiently large $r$?
status_search_result: The question concerns whether SparseStack random matrices with constant column repetition $\zeta=O(1)$ and embedding dimension $k=O(r)$ achieve the oblivious subspace injection (OSI) property, with the specific concrete instance $\zeta=4$, $k=2r$. Recent work introduces the OSI notion and presents SparseStack with strong empirical performance, but a rigorous proof (or disproof) at this constant-sparsity, linear-in-$r$ regime does not appear in the literature; related works on sparse oblivious subspace embeddings (e.g., Chenakkod–Dereziński–Dong, Li–Liu, Nelson–Nguyen) establish sparsity/dimension tradeoffs but do not settle this OSI-specific question. Status appears open.

original_question: Given any choice of $m$-node tree tensor network (e.g., tensor train or Tucker) and choice of ranks (dimensions of edges in the tensor network), let the set of representable tensors in this tensor network be $S R^d_1 x *s x d_n$. Find a polynomial-time algorithm that takes as input any tensor $A R^d_1 x *s x d_n$ and yields an approximation $X S$ such that [ |X-A |_F^2 < (m-1) _Y S |Y-A |_F^2, ] or show that an $(m-1)$-approximation is optimal under complexity-theoretic assumptions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and positive integers $d_1,\dots,d_n$ be given. A tree tensor network with $m$ nodes is specified by a tree $T$ with $m$ vertices, where $n$ of the leaves are labeled by the physical indices $1,\dots,n$ (with attached dimensions $d_1,\dots,d_n$), every internal edge $e$ is assigned a positive integer rank $r_e$, and each vertex $v$ carries a tensor whose modes correspond to the edges incident to $v$ (the dimension of a mode is $d_i$ for a physical leaf and $r_e$ for an internal edge). Contracting all internal edges yields a tensor in $\mathbb{R}^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_n}$. Let 
$$S \subset \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_n}$$
denote the set of all tensors representable by some assignment of node tensors with the prescribed tree structure and ranks. Familiar special cases include tensor trains and (hierarchical) Tucker decompositions.

The question: Either
(a) exhibit a polynomial-time algorithm (running in time polynomial in $\sum_i d_i$, $m$, and $\max_e r_e$) that, on input any tensor $\mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_n}$, outputs $\mathcal{X}\in S$ satisfying
$$\|\mathcal{X}-\mathcal{A}\|_F^2 \;<\; (m-1)\,\min_{\mathcal{Y}\in S}\|\mathcal{Y}-\mathcal{A}\|_F^2,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_F$ denotes the Frobenius norm; or
(b) prove, under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions, that no polynomial-time algorithm can achieve an approximation ratio strictly better than $m-1$ for this problem.
status_search_result: Standard quasi-optimal algorithms (e.g., hierarchical/sequential SVD truncation for tensor trains and hierarchical Tucker) are known to give a $\sqrt{m-1}$-type bound on the error (i.e., factor $m-1$ in squared Frobenius norm), but no polynomial-time algorithm is known to beat this $(m-1)$ ratio, nor is there a complexity-theoretic lower bound proving optimality. Available literature on tree tensor network approximation and contraction-order optimization does not resolve this dichotomy.

paper_title: Pulsars and Millisecond Pulsars I: Advancements, Open Questions and finding Gaps via statistical insights
original_question: What physical processes produce millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in different astrophysical environments, specifically in globular clusters (GCs), which are dense stellar systems with frequent close stellar encounters and binary interactions, and in the Galactic field (GF), where stars are relatively isolated? The question asks which formation channels dominate in each environment and what environmental differences are responsible for the observed MSP populations.
self_contained_problem:
A millisecond pulsar (MSP) is a rotation-powered neutron star with spin period P ≲ 30 ms and small spin-down rate, generally believed to have been spun up ("recycled") through accretion from a binary companion. MSPs are observed in two distinct Galactic environments:

(i) Globular clusters (GCs): gravitationally bound, dense stellar systems (central stellar densities up to ~10^6 stars pc^-3) in which close stellar encounters, tidal captures, exchange interactions, and binary–single and binary–binary scatterings occur frequently over a Hubble time.

(ii) The Galactic field (GF): the disk and bulge population, where stellar densities are low (~0.1 stars pc^-3) and stars and binaries evolve in effective isolation, with negligible probability of dynamical encounters.

Identify and characterize the dominant astrophysical formation channels that produce the observed MSP populations in each of these two environments. In particular:

(a) Specify, for the GF, the sequence of binary stellar-evolution processes (e.g., primordial binary evolution with mass transfer, common-envelope episodes, accretion-induced collapse, low-/intermediate-mass X-ray binary recycling) that lead to a recycled neutron star with spin period in the millisecond range, together with the resulting companion types and orbital characteristics.

(b) Specify, for GCs, the additional dynamical formation channels (e.g., tidal capture of a neutron star by a main-sequence or giant star, exchange encounters placing a neutron star into a pre-existing binary, physical collisions, and the role of mass segregation) that augment or replace the isolated-binary channels.

(c) Quantify which environmental differences (stellar density, encounter rate, binary fraction, metallicity, age, escape velocity retaining natal kicks) are responsible for the observed contrasts between the GC and GF MSP populations, including the per-unit-stellar-mass overabundance of MSPs in GCs.
status_search_result: The question of which formation channels dominate MSP production in globular clusters versus the Galactic field is a long-standing open problem in pulsar astrophysics. While the broad recycling paradigm via low-mass X-ray binaries is well established for the field, and dynamical formation (tidal capture, exchange encounters) is widely accepted as the additional dominant channel in dense clusters, the relative rates, the role of accretion-induced collapse, and quantitative reproduction of observed MSP populations remain unresolved and are an active area of research.

paper_title: Pulsars and Millisecond Pulsars I: Advancements, Open Questions and finding Gaps via statistical insights
original_question: What mechanisms cause the magnetic fields of pulsars to decay or strengthen over timescales from millions to billions of years, and how do those mechanisms differ between pulsars in globular clusters and pulsars in the Galactic field? This asks how dense stellar interactions, binary recycling, and relative isolation change the long-term magnetic-field evolution of neutron stars.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a population of neutron stars observed as pulsars, characterized by a rotation period P, a period derivative dP/dt, and an inferred surface dipolar magnetic field strength B (estimated, e.g., from B ∝ (P dP/dt)^{1/2}). Two sub-populations are distinguished:

(a) Pulsars residing in globular clusters, where stellar number densities are high (~10^3–10^6 pc^{-3}), encounter rates are large, and binary formation/exchange via dynamical interactions (tidal capture, exchange encounters, three-body interactions) is frequent. Many such pulsars undergo episodes of mass transfer from a binary companion ("recycling") that spin them up to millisecond rotation periods.

(b) Pulsars residing in the Galactic field (disk/halo), where stellar densities are low (~0.1 pc^{-3}), dynamical encounters are negligible, and binary evolution proceeds in relative isolation.

Identify and quantitatively characterize the physical mechanisms that govern the long-term evolution (over timescales 10^6–10^{10} years) of the surface magnetic field B(t) of an isolated or binary neutron star, including but not limited to:
  • Ohmic (resistive) decay of currents in the crust and core,
  • Hall drift in the crustal magnetic field,
  • Ambipolar diffusion in the core,
  • Burial / screening of the magnetic field by accreted matter during episodes of mass accretion at rate Ṁ,
  • Possible amplification mechanisms (e.g., thermomagnetic instabilities, dynamo action during proto-neutron-star phases).

Specifically, derive or specify:
  1. An evolution equation for B(t) (or for the magnetic flux distribution within the star) that incorporates the above mechanisms with their characteristic timescales as functions of crustal/core composition, temperature, and accreted mass ΔM_acc.
  2. The dependence of B(t) on the cumulative accreted mass for recycled pulsars, and a quantitative explanation of the typical observed millisecond-pulsar magnetic fields B ~ 10^8–10^9 G versus isolated young pulsar fields B ~ 10^{12}–10^{13} G.
  3. How the rate and outcome of these mechanisms differ statistically between sub-population (a) and sub-population (b), accounting for the enhanced frequency of binary formation, disruption, and exchange encounters in dense cluster environments versus isolated evolution in the Galactic field.

Provide the resulting predicted distributions of B for the two sub-populations and identify which mechanism(s) dominate the differences.
status_search_result: The long-term magnetic-field evolution of neutron stars remains an active and unresolved area of research. paper_title: Pulsars and Millisecond Pulsars I: Advancements, Open Questions and finding Gaps via statistical insights
original_question: How can observations of pulsars be used to constrain the equation of state of nuclear matter inside neutron stars? More specifically, under the extreme conditions present in pulsars—ultra-high density, strong gravity, and rapid rotation—what measurements or inferred properties can reveal the behavior of matter in the dense cores of neutron stars?
self_contained_problem:
A neutron star is modeled as a static or uniformly rotating, self-gravitating fluid configuration in general relativity, whose interior structure is determined (via the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equations in the non-rotating case, or their rotating generalizations) by a one-parameter equation of state P = P(ε) relating pressure P to energy density ε, valid up to several times nuclear saturation density ρ₀ ≈ 2.8 × 10¹⁴ g/cm³. Pulsars are rapidly rotating, magnetized neutron stars whose observable properties include: the gravitational mass M, the circumferential equatorial radius R, the spin frequency ν (and its derivatives), the moment of inertia I, the tidal deformability Λ, the surface redshift, the maximum mass M_max, and parameters of binary orbits (post-Keplerian parameters such as Shapiro delay and orbital decay).

Formulate and address the following inverse problem:

(a) Identify a set of pulsar-related observables — e.g. precise mass measurements from binary timing, simultaneous mass–radius determinations from pulse-profile modeling of hot spots on rotating neutron-star surfaces, the maximum observed neutron-star mass, moment-of-inertia inferences from relativistic spin–orbit coupling in binary pulsars, and limits on spin frequency (Keplerian mass-shedding limit) — and specify, for each observable, the functional dependence on the equation of state P(ε) through the relevant relativistic stellar-structure equations.

(b) Determine, under the constraints imposed by general relativity, causality (sound speed c_s² = dP/dε ≤ c²), thermodynamic stability (dP/dε ≥ 0), and compatibility with low-density nuclear physics, what regions of the function space of admissible equations of state are excluded or favored by such pulsar observations, and in particular how the existence of pulsars with M ≳ 2 M_⊙ and rapid rotation (ν up to ≈ 716 Hz) constrains the stiffness of P(ε) in the supranuclear regime ε ≳ 2ε₀.

(c) Discuss whether the combined set of pulsar observables can in principle uniquely reconstruct P(ε) in the cores of neutron stars, or whether degeneracies persist that allow phenomenologically distinct phases (e.g. purely hadronic matter versus matter containing hyperons, deconfined quark matter, or color-superconducting phases) to remain observationally indistinguishable.
status_search_result: The determination of the dense-matter equation of state from pulsar observations is an active, unresolved problem in nuclear and gravitational astrophysics. Recent NICER mass–radius measurements of PSR J0030+0451 and J0740+6620, heavy-pulsar mass measurements (≈2 M_⊙), and the GW170817 tidal-deformability constraint have narrowed but not fixed the equation of state; significant degeneracies (hadronic vs. quark-matter cores) remain.

original_question: In the planar magnetic billiard model, where a particle moves inside a billiard table along Larmor circles determined by a strong constant magnetic field, is every totally integrable magnetic billiard necessarily the circular billiard?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar magnetic billiard: a charged point particle moves inside a smooth bounded planar domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ under the influence of a uniform constant magnetic field of magnitude $B>0$ perpendicular to the plane. Between collisions with the boundary $\partial\Omega$, the particle travels along Larmor circles of radius $r = 1/B$ (a "strong" magnetic field corresponds to $r$ small relative to the size of $\Omega$, so that Larmor circles fit inside $\Omega$). Upon hitting $\partial\Omega$, the particle reflects according to the standard law of elastic reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection), and then continues along a new Larmor circle of the same radius $1/B$.

The induced magnetic billiard map $T$ acts on the phase space of oriented chords (Larmor arcs) meeting $\partial\Omega$. The billiard is called totally integrable if a neighborhood of the boundary in phase space is foliated by smooth invariant curves of $T$ on which the dynamics is conjugate to a rotation (equivalently, the boundary is accumulated by a family of smooth caustics for the magnetic billiard).

Question: Suppose $\Omega$ is a smooth bounded planar domain such that the magnetic billiard in $\Omega$ with a strong constant magnetic field is totally integrable. Must $\partial\Omega$ be a circle?
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in recent surveys on billiards and symplectic geometry. Partial results exist: total integrability has been established to imply circularity for convex magnetic billiards in weak constant magnetic fields, and algebraic non-integrability results constrain non-circular boundaries; on constant curvature surfaces some integrability-implies-circle results are known. However, the strong-field planar case remains conjectural and is described as an open problem in recent literature (2025).

original_question: Consider Newton's equation u'' = -V'_u(u,t) with V periodic in both u and t. Besides the special case V = V(nu + mt), for which the system is known to be totally integrable near infinity, are there other potential functions V for which the system is totally integrable at infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Newton's equation
    u'' = -∂V/∂u (u, t),
where u: ℝ → ℝ and V: ℝ × ℝ → ℝ is smooth and periodic in both variables u and t (so V is defined on the torus S^1 × S^1). This equation is the Euler–Lagrange equation of the Lagrangian L(u, u̇, t) = (1/2) u̇^2 − V(u, t), and the corresponding Hamiltonian flow, with Hamiltonian H(p, u, t) = (1/2) p^2 + V(u, t), acts on T*S^1 × S^1.

Say that the system is totally integrable at infinity if there exists c > 0 and a smooth function F: {(p, u, t): |p| > c} → ℝ, periodic in u and t, that is a non-trivial integral of motion of the Hamiltonian flow and is functionally independent from H on the region |p| > c.

It is known that:
 (a) The flow is totally integrable on the entire phase space T*S^1 × S^1 if and only if V is independent of u.
 (b) If V(u, t) = W(nu + mt) for some integers n, m with m ≠ 0 and some 1-periodic function W, then there exists an integral of motion that is a polynomial of degree at most 2 in p, and hence the system is totally integrable on the region |p| > c for c sufficiently large.

Question: Do there exist potentials V(u, t), periodic in u and t, that are not of the form V(u, t) = W(nu + mt), for which the associated Hamiltonian flow is totally integrable at infinity?

No source was found classifying all such potentials V or producing examples beyond V(nu + mt). The question appears to remain open.

original_question: Let (N, g) be an orientable closed hyperbolic surface. Is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity of the unit disk cotangent bundle (D^*N, d lambda) finite?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(N,g)$ be an orientable closed hyperbolic surface (a closed orientable smooth surface of genus $\geq 2$ equipped with a Riemannian metric of constant curvature $-1$). Let $T^*N$ denote its cotangent bundle, and let $\lambda$ be the canonical Liouville $1$-form on $T^*N$, so that $\omega = d\lambda$ is the standard symplectic form. Using the metric $g$, define the unit disk cotangent bundle
$$D^*N = \{(q,p)\in T^*N : \|p\|_g \leq 1\},$$
which is a compact symplectic manifold with boundary $(D^*N, d\lambda)$.

The Hofer–Zehnder capacity $c_{HZ}(M,\omega)$ of a symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ is defined as the supremum of $\max H - \min H$ over all smooth, compactly supported (in the interior) Hamiltonians $H:M\to\mathbb{R}$ that are constant near their maximum and minimum and whose Hamiltonian flow has no non-constant periodic orbit of period $\leq 1$.

Question: Is $c_{HZ}(D^*N, d\lambda) < \infty$?

Closed hyperbolic surfaces have $\pi_2=0$, so these criteria do not apply. Recent work (2024) on magnetic disc tangent bundles over constant-curvature surfaces explicitly notes that for hyperbolic surfaces even finiteness of the Hofer–Zehnder capacity remains unknown in the relevant (weak/zero magnetic field) regime, indicating the problem is still open.

original_question: For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a closed symplectic manifold, is it true that either the number of periodic orbits is finite or the number P(T) of primitive periodic orbits of period at most T grows at least quadratically, in the sense that lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $\varphi: M \to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e., the time-one map of a (time-dependent) Hamiltonian flow on $M$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is a finite sequence $(x, \varphi(x), \varphi^2(x), \dots, \varphi^{k-1}(x))$ with $\varphi^k(x) = x$; the orbit is called primitive of period $k$ if $k$ is the smallest such positive integer. For $T > 0$, let
$$P(T) = \#\{\text{primitive periodic orbits of }\varphi\text{ of period at most }T\}.$$
Decide whether the following dichotomy holds for every closed symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ and every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$: either $\varphi$ has only finitely many periodic orbits (counted over all periods), or
$$\liminf_{T \to +\infty} \frac{\log P(T)}{\log T} \;\geq\; 2.$$
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem extending known surface/two-dimensional results (related to the Conley and Hofer–Zehnder conjectures) to arbitrary dimensions. Web searches turn up active recent work on Hamiltonian periodic orbit growth and pseudo-rotations, but no resolution of the quadratic-growth dichotomy in higher dimensions; the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Do there exist nontrivial integrable pensive billiards, meaning pensive billiard systems with a nonzero delay function for which one can exhibit explicit choices of boundary curve and delay that yield integrable dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma$ be a smooth, strictly convex closed curve in the plane bounding a domain $D$, and let $\ell:(0,\pi)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function called the delay function. The pensive billiard map $T_\ell$ associated with $(\gamma,\ell)$ is defined on the space of inward-pointing unit tangent vectors based on $\gamma$ (parametrized by arclength position $s\in\mathbb{R}/L\mathbb{Z}$ and incidence angle $\alpha\in(0,\pi)$) as follows. Given $(s,\alpha)$, draw the oriented chord from $\gamma(s)$ inside $D$ making angle $\alpha$ with the boundary; let $s'$ be the arclength parameter of the chord's other endpoint and $\alpha'$ the angle the chord makes with $\gamma$ at $\gamma(s')$. Then set
$$T_\ell(s,\alpha) \;=\; \bigl(s' + \ell(\alpha'),\ \alpha'\bigr),$$
where the position is shifted along the boundary by the angle-dependent distance $\ell(\alpha')$. The case $\ell\equiv 0$ recovers the classical Birkhoff billiard map.

A pensive billiard is called integrable if the map $T_\ell$ admits a smooth foliation of an open subset of its phase cylinder $(\mathbb{R}/L\mathbb{Z})\times(0,\pi)$ by invariant curves homotopic to the boundary circles, equivalently, if there exists a non-constant smooth first integral $F:(\mathbb{R}/L\mathbb{Z})\times(0,\pi)\to\mathbb{R}$ with $F\circ T_\ell = F$.

Question: Do there exist nontrivial integrable pensive billiards, i.e., explicit pairs $(\gamma,\ell)$ with $\ell\not\equiv 0$ for which $T_\ell$ is integrable in the sense above?
status_search_result: Pensive billiards were introduced recently and are under active study (e.g., Bialy–Drivas–Khesin–Tabachnikov, "Pensive billiards, point vortices, and the silver ratio", arXiv:2408.03279), where variational/symplectic structure, twist conditions, and periodic orbits are investigated, but no construction of nontrivial integrable examples (with nonzero delay) is reported. The question is listed among open problems in current surveys on billiards, and no published resolution was found.

original_question: Characterize which fiber-wise convex domains in T^*S^n arise as billiard domains W_T associated with convex billiard tables T in R^(n+1).
self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 1 and let L = L(R^{n+1}) denote the space of oriented straight lines in R^{n+1}. Equip L with its canonical symplectic structure ω, under which (L, ω) is symplectomorphic to the cotangent bundle (T*S^n, ω_std) of the round n-sphere with its standard Liouville form.

For a smooth, strictly convex, compact domain T ⊂ R^{n+1} (a "convex billiard table"), define the associated billiard domain
   W_T = { ℓ ∈ L : ℓ ∩ T ≠ ∅ } ⊂ L,
endowed with the restricted symplectic form ω_T := ω|_{W_T}. Under the symplectomorphism L ≅ T*S^n, (W_T, ω_T) corresponds to a fiber-wise convex domain in T*S^n (i.e., a domain whose intersection with each cotangent fiber T*_q S^n is a convex body containing the origin), and is diffeomorphic to the unit codisk bundle D*S^n.

Problem. Give an intrinsic characterization of the fiber-wise convex domains W ⊂ T*S^n that arise, up to symplectomorphism, as billiard domains W_T for some smooth strictly convex billiard table T ⊂ R^{n+1}. Equivalently, identify necessary and sufficient symplectic/geometric conditions on a fiber-wise convex domain W ⊂ T*S^n that single out those obtained from convex hypersurfaces in Euclidean space via the line-space construction above.

original_question: Let M be a closed manifold that is not a K(pi,1), and let Sigma be a closed connected hypersurface in T^*M that is a regular energy level of a Hamiltonian H: T^*M -> R. Is there always some epsilon > 0 such that almost all energy levels of H in the interval (c - epsilon, c + epsilon) carry a contractible periodic orbit of H?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold that is not a $K(\pi,1)$ (i.e., its universal cover is not contractible, equivalently some higher homotopy group $\pi_k(M)$ with $k\ge 2$ is nontrivial). Equip the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ with its standard symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the canonical Liouville $1$-form. Given a smooth Hamiltonian $H : T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$, the Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ is defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega = -dH$, and a periodic orbit of $H$ on the energy level $H^{-1}(a)$ is a non-constant solution $\gamma : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to T^*M$ of $\dot\gamma = X_H(\gamma)$ lying in $H^{-1}(a)$. Such an orbit is called contractible if its underlying free loop in $T^*M$ is contractible (equivalently, since $T^*M$ deformation retracts to $M$, its projection to $M$ is contractible).

Suppose $\Sigma \subset T^*M$ is a closed connected hypersurface that arises as a regular energy level $\Sigma = H^{-1}(c)$ of some smooth Hamiltonian $H$ (so $dH$ is non-vanishing on $\Sigma$). 

Question: Does there always exist $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for almost every (in the sense of Lebesgue measure) value $a \in (c-\varepsilon, c+\varepsilon)$, the energy level $H^{-1}(a)$ carries a contractible periodic orbit of $H$?
status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture concerning contractible almost-existence on hypersurfaces in cotangent bundles of closed manifolds that are not aspherical. Related almost-existence theorems are known (e.g., for non-contractible orbits via Macarini–Schlenk, and contractible orbits in symplectically aspherical or low-energy settings), but a search did not produce a resolution of the contractible almost-existence statement in this specific generality (closed M not a K(π,1), arbitrary closed connected regular hypersurface). The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Describe the dynamics of generic trajectories in parallelogram tiling billiards, where the plane is tiled by parallelograms with side vectors a_vec = (a, 0) and b_vec = (b sin alpha, b cos alpha) and the dynamics depends on the parameters alpha in (0, pi) and m = a/b.
self_contained_problem:
Tile the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ by congruent parallelograms whose sides are parallel to the vectors $\vec{a}=(a,0)$ and $\vec{b}=(b\sin\alpha,\,b\cos\alpha)$, where $a,b>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,\pi)$. A tiling billiard trajectory is a piecewise-linear oriented curve in the plane which, upon meeting the interior of an edge between two adjacent tiles, refracts across that edge with refraction coefficient $-1$ (i.e., the trajectory is reflected through the edge so that the angle of incidence equals the angle of refraction on the opposite side of the edge, modeling propagation through a metamaterial of refractive index $-1$); trajectories that hit a vertex are undefined. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle equations of motion dot x = partial_p H + (p dot dot x - H) eta_p_bar and dot p = -partial_x H + f p - (p dot dot x - H) eta_x_bar, is there a physical example realizing this framework, and what is the physical or mechanical meaning of these equations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n$ with local coordinates $x = (x^1,\dots,x^n)$, and let $T^*Q$ denote its cotangent bundle with induced canonical coordinates $(x,p) = (x^1,\dots,x^n,p_1,\dots,p_n)$. Let $\theta = p_i\,dx^i$ be the Liouville one-form and $\omega_0 = -d\theta = dx^i\wedge dp_i$ the canonical symplectic form on $T^*Q$.

A locally conformal symplectic (LCS) structure on $T^*Q$ is a pair $(\Omega,\eta)$ consisting of a non-degenerate two-form $\Omega$ and a closed one-form $\eta$ (the Lee form) satisfying $d\Omega = \eta\wedge\Omega$. Write $\eta = \bar\eta_{x^i}\,dx^i + \bar\eta_{p_i}\,dp_i + f\,dt$-type pieces; concretely, decompose the spatial Lee form on $T^*Q$ as $\bar\eta = \bar\eta_{x^i}\,dx^i + \bar\eta_{p_i}\,dp_i$, and let $f$ be the time-component (conformal factor) coefficient appearing in the time-dependent LCS framework.

Given a smooth Hamiltonian $H : \mathbb{R}\times T^*Q \to \mathbb{R}$, the associated locally conformal symplectic equations of motion for a curve $t\mapsto (x(t),p(t))$ are
$$\dot x^i \;=\; \frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i} \;+\; \bigl(p_j\,\dot x^j - H\bigr)\,\bar\eta_{p_i},$$
$$\dot p_i \;=\; -\frac{\partial H}{\partial x^i} \;+\; f\,p_i \;-\; \bigl(p_j\,\dot x^j - H\bigr)\,\bar\eta_{x^i}.$$

Question: Exhibit a concrete physical or mechanical system whose dynamics is governed by the above system, and provide a physical/mechanical interpretation of the additional terms $(p_j\dot x^j - H)\bar\eta_{p_i}$, $f p_i$, and $-(p_j\dot x^j - H)\bar\eta_{x^i}$ that distinguish these equations from standard Hamilton's equations.
status_search_result: The literature on locally conformal symplectic (LCS) Hamiltonian dynamics develops the geometric formalism on cotangent bundles and discusses dissipative-type extensions of Hamilton's equations, with potential applications via contact pairs and Lie systems (engineering, control, cosmology). However, no source unambiguously identifies a canonical physical example fitting precisely the time-dependent LCS equations stated, nor a definitive physical interpretation; the question is interpretive/open-ended and its status is unclear.

original_question: For a projective billiard, when does the system possess an invariant symplectic form, and when does it admit a variational description?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $
u$ be a smooth field of directions along $\partial\Omega$ that is everywhere transverse to $\partial\Omega$ (a "projective billiard structure"). Define the projective billiard map on the phase space of oriented lines meeting $\partial\Omega$ (equivalently, unit tangent vectors based at $\partial\Omega$ pointing inward) by the following reflection rule at each impact point $p \in \partial\Omega$: decompose the incoming velocity vector into a component tangent to $\partial\Omega$ at $p$ and a component along the transverse direction $
u(p)$; the tangential component is preserved while the transverse (along $
u(p)$) component is reversed. The resulting outgoing direction together with the next impact point on $\partial\Omega$ defines the next state.

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(\partial\Omega,
u)$ under which the projective billiard map admits an invariant symplectic form on its phase space.

(b) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $(\partial\Omega,
u)$ under which the projective billiard map admits a variational (least-action) description, i.e., its orbits arise as critical points of a generating functional analogous to the length functional in the standard billiard.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in recent compilations of open problems in billiards. Partial results are known (e.g., projective billiards on a sphere with an exactness condition on the transverse field admit an invariant symplectic form induced by the hyperbolic Beltrami-Cayley-Klein metric, and recent work studies Hamiltonian projective billiards on convex bodies), but a complete characterization of when an invariant symplectic form or a variational description exists remains open.

original_question: Study the complexity function of polygonal symplectic billiards, where the complexity p(n) counts the number of length-n subwords arising from symbolic codings of billiard trajectories by polygon sides.
self_contained_problem:
Setup (symplectic billiards in a convex polygon). Let P ⊂ R² be a convex polygon with sides s_1, …, s_k (labeled by symbols from an alphabet A = {1, …, k}). The symplectic billiard map T acts on ordered pairs of boundary points (x, y) ∈ ∂P × ∂P (with x ≠ y) by the following rule: T(x, y) = (y, z), where z ∈ ∂P is uniquely determined by the condition that the chord xz is parallel to the tangent line to ∂P at y. (At a vertex of P, "tangent direction" is interpreted via the supporting lines, and the map is defined on the full-measure set where this rule is unambiguous.)

Symbolic coding. Given a bi-infinite orbit (…, x_{-1}, x_0, x_1, …) of T whose points lie in the interiors of sides, assign to it the bi-infinite word w ∈ A^Z whose n-th letter is the index of the side containing x_n. Let L ⊂ A^Z denote the language consisting of all finite words that occur as factors (subwords) of the codings of all such orbits, as P is fixed.

Complexity function. For each integer n ≥ 1, define
   p(n) = #{ u ∈ A^n : u is a factor of some w ∈ L }.

Problem. Determine the asymptotic behavior of the complexity function p(n) of polygonal symplectic billiards. In particular:
(a) Establish general upper and lower bounds on p(n) valid for all convex polygons P (e.g., is p(n) sub-exponential?).
(b) For "rational" polygons (those whose angles are rational multiples of π, or any natural analogue suited to the symplectic setting), determine the precise polynomial growth rate of p(n).
(c) Identify classes of polygons (such as affine-regular polygons or trapezoids, where every orbit is periodic) for which p(n) is bounded, and more generally classify possible growth rates of p(n) in terms of geometric properties of P.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent open-problems collection on billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry. While complexity functions for conventional polygonal billiards (sub-exponential in general, cubic for rational/tiling cases) and for polygonal outer billiards (polynomial) are well studied, the analogous study for polygonal symplectic billiards remains open. Partial information is available: in special polygons (e.g., affine-regular polygons, trapezoids) every symplectic billiard orbit is periodic, so p(n) is bounded; the general asymptotics are not established.
