paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
context_brief: comparison of KSW-narrow and narrow operators
original_question: Is every KSW-narrow operator from L1[0,1] to an arbitrary Banach space X necessarily narrow in the earlier sense of narrow operators on L1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1=L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable functions on $[0,1]$ with the usual norm. Recall the following two notions of "narrowness" for a bounded linear operator $T:L_1\to X$ into a Banach space $X$.

(i) (Narrow operator, Plichko–Popov sense.) $T$ is called narrow if for every measurable set $A\subseteq[0,1]$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a "sign" function $x:[0,1]\to\{-1,0,1\}$ supported on $A$ with $\int_0^1 x\,d\mu=0$ and $|x|=\mathbf{1}_A$ such that $\|T x\|<\varepsilon$.

(ii) (KSW-narrow operator, in the sense of Kadets–Shvydkoy–Werner.) $T$ is called KSW-narrow if for every non-empty relatively weakly open subset $U$ of the unit ball $B_{L_1}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $u,v\in U$ with $\|T(u-v)\|<\varepsilon$ and $\|u-v\|>2-\varepsilon$ (equivalently, on every slice/relatively weakly open set one can find pairs that are nearly antipodal in $L_1$ but whose images under $T$ are nearly equal).

Question: Is it true that for every Banach space $X$, every KSW-narrow operator $T:L_1[0,1]\to X$ is narrow in the sense (i)?

The status therefore appears to remain unresolved in the literature surveyed, but this could not be definitively confirmed.

paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
original_question: Is every Tauberian operator T: L1[0,1] → L1[0,1] a semi-Fredholm operator?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$. A bounded linear operator $T: L_1 \to L_1$ is called Tauberian if its second adjoint $T^{**}: L_1^{**} \to L_1^{**}$ satisfies $(T^{**})^{-1}(L_1) \subseteq L_1$, where $L_1$ is canonically embedded in $L_1^{**}$. The operator $T$ is called semi-Fredholm if its range $T(L_1)$ is closed in $L_1$ and at least one of $\dim \ker T$ or $\operatorname{codim} T(L_1)$ is finite.

Question: Is every Tauberian operator $T: L_1[0,1] \to L_1[0,1]$ a semi-Fredholm operator?
status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Johnson, Nasseri, Schechtman and Tzafriri (Canad. Math. Bull.) construct injective Tauberian operators on $L_1(0,1)$ with dense, nonclosed range. Such an operator cannot be semi-Fredholm (semi-Fredholm operators have closed range), so not every Tauberian operator on $L_1$ is semi-Fredholm.

original_question: For the same quadratic-polynomial linearization problem, does the function α ↦ B(α)+log|U(e^{2πiα})| extend from the Brjuno numbers to a 1/2-Hölder continuous function on R?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and consider the family of quadratic polynomials
$$P_\lambda(z)=\lambda z+z^2,\qquad \lambda\in\overline{\mathbb{D}}.$$
For $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, $P_\lambda$ is said to be linearizable at $0$ if there exists a univalent holomorphic map $h$ defined on a neighborhood of $0$, with $h(0)=0$ and $h'(0)=1$, such that $h^{-1}\circ P_\lambda\circ h(z)=\lambda z$. Let $r_\lambda$ denote the conformal radius of the largest such linearization domain (the Siegel disk), with the convention $r_\lambda=0$ when $P_\lambda$ is not linearizable.

It is known that:
(i) there exists a bounded holomorphic function $U:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that $|U(\lambda)|=r_\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{D}$;
(ii) the Brjuno set $\mathcal{B}\subset\mathbb{R}$ consists of those irrationals $\alpha$ whose continued fraction convergents $p_n/q_n$ satisfy
$$B(\alpha)=\sum_{n\ge 0}\frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}<\infty,$$
and $B:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb{R}$ is the Brjuno function;
(iii) for $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, $P_{e^{2\pi i\alpha}}$ is linearizable iff $\alpha\in\mathcal{B}$.

Question: Does the function
$$\alpha\;\longmapsto\;B(\alpha)+\log\bigl|U(e^{2\pi i\alpha})\bigr|,$$
defined a priori on $\mathcal{B}$, extend to a $\tfrac12$-Hölder continuous function on all of $\mathbb{R}$?
status_search_result: This is the Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz conjecture on the 1/2-Hölder regularity of the function Υ(α)=B(α)+log|U(e^{2πiα})|. Buff and Chéritat proved that the function cannot be α-Hölder for any exponent α>1/2 (sharpness). Cheraghi and Chéritat (2015) proved the 1/2-Hölder continuity for the restriction of Υ to rotation numbers of sufficiently high type, but the conjecture in full generality on all of ℝ remains open as of the most recent literature.

original_question: Fix 0≤s≤r with r≥s for orientation-preserving C^r circle diffeomorphisms of irrational rotation number α. Determine exactly which irrational α have the property that every such C^r diffeomorphism is conjugate to the rotation R_α by a C^s diffeomorphism, and likewise determine the corresponding local class where the diffeomorphism is only assumed to be C^r-close to R_α. Are the global and local arithmetic classes different?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ denote the circle, and for $r\geq 1$ let $\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})$ denote the group of orientation-preserving $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, let $R_\alpha:\mathbb{T}\to\mathbb{T}$, $R_\alpha(x)=x+\alpha\pmod 1$, denote the rigid rotation by $\alpha$. Recall that every $f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})$ has a well-defined rotation number $\rho(f)\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

Fix real numbers $r\geq s\geq 0$. Define two subsets of the irrationals:
\[
\mathcal{C}_{r,s}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}:\text{every }f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})\text{ with }\rho(f)\equiv\alpha\bmod 1\text{ is }C^s\text{-conjugate to }R_\alpha\},
\]
\[
\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}:\exists\,\varepsilon>0\text{ such that every }f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})\text{ with }\rho(f)\equiv\alpha\bmod 1\text{ and }\|f-R_\alpha\|_{C^r}<\varepsilon\text{ is }C^s\text{-conjugate to }R_\alpha\}.
\]
Here "$C^s$-conjugate to $R_\alpha$" means there exists $h\in\mathrm{Diff}^s_+(\mathbb{T})$ with $h\circ f=R_\alpha\circ h$.

Determine the sets $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}$ and $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ explicitly in terms of arithmetic conditions on $\alpha$. Moreover, decide whether $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}=\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ in general, or whether the global and local arithmetic classes differ.
status_search_result: Determining the optimal arithmetic class for $C^s$-linearization of $C^r$ circle diffeomorphisms—both globally and in a neighborhood of rotations—remains an active and incompletely resolved problem. The Herman-Yoccoz theorem and subsequent work by Katznelson-Ornstein, Khanin-Teplinsky, and others yield essentially sharp results in some regularity ranges (e.g., Yoccoz's optimal Diophantine condition for analytic/smooth global conjugacy), but the exact arithmetic characterizations of $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}$ and $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ for all admissible $(r,s)$, and the precise comparison between the global and local classes, are not fully known.

original_question: Let f(z)=Az+O(z^2) be a holomorphic germ of (C^n,0) with distinct eigenvalues satisfying the nonresonance condition λ^k−λ_j≠0 for all |k|≥2. What is the optimal arithmetic condition on the eigenvalues of A that guarantees analytic linearizability of f, and can that optimal condition be proved by a direct majorant-series argument?

Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a holomorphic germ with $f(z)=Az+O(\|z\|^2)$, where $A\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ has distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ satisfying the nonresonance condition
$$\lambda^k-\lambda_j:=\lambda_1^{k_1}\cdots\lambda_n^{k_n}-\lambda_j\neq 0\quad\text{for all } j\in\{1,\dots,n\}\text{ and all } k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb{N}^n\text{ with }|k|=k_1+\cdots+k_n\geq 2.$$
Under this condition, $f$ is formally linearizable: there is a unique formal power series tangent to the identity that conjugates $f$ to its linear part $A$. Say that $f$ is analytically linearizable if this formal conjugacy converges in a neighborhood of $0$.

Determine the optimal arithmetic condition on the eigenvalues $(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ that guarantees the analytic linearizability of every such germ $f$, and decide whether this optimal condition can be obtained via a direct majorant-series argument.

status_search_result: In one complex dimension the optimal arithmetic condition is the Brjuno condition (Brjuno's sufficiency, Yoccoz's necessity for quadratic polynomials). original_question: For commuting k-tuples of circle diffeomorphisms with rotation numbers (α1,…,αk), determine exactly the global and local arithmetic classes C^k_{r,s} and C^{k,loc}_{r,s} for C^r-to-C^s linearization.

$$
C^{k}_{r,s} = \{(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k) \in \mathbb{T}^k : \text{every commuting $k$-tuple } (F_1,\dots,F_k) \in (\mathrm{Diff}^{r}_+(\mathbb{T}))^k$$
$$\text{with } F_i F_j = F_j F_i \text{ and } \rho(F_i) = \alpha_i,\ 1 \le i \le k,\text{ is simultaneously } C^{s}\text{-linearizable}\},

original_question: Let V be a compact C^∞ manifold, f a C^∞ diffeomorphism of V, U a C^∞ neighborhood of the identity, and O_{f,U}={g∘f∘g^{-1}: g∈U}. If O_{f,U} is a finite-codimension manifold, must V be a torus T^n and must f be C^∞-conjugate to a Diophantine translation?

Let $V$ be a compact $C^\infty$ manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ denote the group of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $V$, equipped with its standard $C^\infty$ topology. Fix $f \in \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ and let $U \subset \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V)$ be a $C^\infty$ neighborhood of the identity. Define the local conjugacy class
$$O_{f,U} = \{\, g \circ f \circ g^{-1} : g \in U \,\} \subset \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(V).$$
A translation $T_\alpha$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ is the map $x \mapsto x+\alpha \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^n}$, and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Diophantine if there exist constants $C>0$ and $\tau \geq 0$ such that $|\langle k,\alpha\rangle - m| \geq C|k|^{-\tau}$ for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}^n \setminus \{0\}$ and $m \in \mathbb{Z}$.

original_question: Does there exist a C^3 area-preserving twist map of the annulus with a rotational invariant curve of irrational rotation number that is not topologically transitive? Is the answer the same for every r≥3, or even in the analytic category?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A=\mathbb{T}\times[0,1]$ (or $A=\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}$) be the closed (or infinite) annulus, with universal cover $\widetilde A=\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]$. A diffeomorphism $f:A\to A$ is called an area-preserving twist map if it preserves Lebesgue area, preserves boundary components, and a lift $\widetilde f(x,y)=(X(x,y),Y(x,y))$ to $\widetilde A$ satisfies the twist condition $\partial X/\partial y>0$. A rotational invariant curve for $f$ is an essential simple closed curve $\Gamma\subset A$ (i.e., homotopic to $\mathbb{T}\times\{0\}$) with $f(\Gamma)=\Gamma$; by Birkhoff such a $\Gamma$ is the graph of a Lipschitz function. The rotation number of $f|_\Gamma$ is the Poincaré rotation number of the induced circle homeomorphism. The map $f|_\Gamma$ is topologically transitive if it has a dense orbit in $\Gamma$.

Question: Does there exist a $C^3$ area-preserving twist map of the annulus possessing a rotational invariant curve with irrational rotation number on which the restriction of $f$ is not topologically transitive (equivalently, by Denjoy-type considerations, on which $f$ is conjugate to a Denjoy counterexample rather than to an irrational rotation)? Furthermore, does the same hold for every regularity class $C^r$ with $r\ge 3$, and even in the real-analytic category?
status_search_result: Searches reveal active research on regularity and dynamics of irrational invariant curves of twist maps (e.g. Arnaud's non-hyperbolicity results, Fayad–others on non-differentiable irrational curves for $C^1$ twist maps), but no source found that resolves Mather's question of producing a $C^3$ (or higher, or analytic) area-preserving twist map with a non-topologically-transitive rotational invariant curve of irrational rotation number. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $M$ be a closed (compact, boundaryless) Riemannian manifold of dimension at least $2$, and let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For an integer $r \geq 2$ and a potential $V \in C^r(M \times \mathbb{T})$, consider the time-periodic Lagrangian
$$L_V(x, v, t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g_x(v,v) - V(x, t), \qquad (x,v,t) \in TM \times \mathbb{T},$$
where $g$ is the Riemannian metric on $M$. Let $\Phi^t_V$ denote the associated (time-dependent) Euler–Lagrange flow on $TM \times \mathbb{T}$, and define the kinetic energy along a trajectory $(x(t), \dot x(t))$ by $K(t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g_{x(t)}(\dot x(t), \dot x(t))$.

Question: Does there exist a residual subset $\mathcal{R} \subset C^r(M \times \mathbb{T})$ (in the sense of Baire category) such that for every $V \in \mathcal{R}$ the Euler–Lagrange flow of $L_V$ admits at least one trajectory $(x(t),\dot x(t))$ with
$$K(t) \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as} \quad t \to \infty\,?$$

self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a Hamiltonian partial differential equation written in the form
  u_t = J ∇H(u),
where u(t) belongs to a scale of Hilbert spaces, J is a (possibly unbounded) symplectic operator, and H is a smooth Hamiltonian functional. Assume that this equation possesses a nondegenerate one-parameter family

  {u_λ(t) : λ ∈ I ⊂ ℝ}

of time-periodic solutions with periods T(λ) depending on the parameter λ. Nondegeneracy is to be understood in a suitable Floquet/transversality sense (e.g. T'(λ) ≠ 0 and the linearized period map at u_λ has trivial kernel apart from the directions forced by symmetry).

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation under periodic boundary conditions,
  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x = 0,  x ∈ T = R/Z,
viewed as an integrable infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system. Its phase space (e.g. a Sobolev space H^s(T) of zero-mean functions) is foliated by invariant finite-gap tori, i.e. compact invariant tori obtained from finite-dimensional reductions of the integrable hierarchy.

  u_t + u_{xxx} - 6 u u_x = ε F(u),
where F is a sufficiently regular (say smooth, Hamiltonian) perturbation.

  dist(u(t), T_{ε}) ≤ ε^a   for all 0 ≤ t ≤ T_ε,
where T_ε is some finite-gap torus (possibly depending on the solution) and the time scale satisfies
  T_ε ≥ C_M ε^{-M}.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine the best possible upper bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation of a planar point set. In addition, decide whether one can prove a strictly smaller worst-case upper bound when the input points are in convex position.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (no four points cocircular). The Delaunay triangulation $\mathrm{DT}(P)$ is the planar straight-line graph on vertex set $P$ in which three points $p,q,r \in P$ form a triangular face if and only if the open disk circumscribing $p,q,r$ contains no other point of $P$. For two points $u,v \in P$, let $d_{\mathrm{DT}(P)}(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$ in $\mathrm{DT}(P)$, where each edge is weighted by its Euclidean length, and let $\|u-v\|$ denote the Euclidean distance. The (worst-case) spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation is
$$\rho \;=\; \sup_{P}\;\max_{u\neq v\in P}\;\frac{d_{\mathrm{DT}(P)}(u,v)}{\|u-v\|},$$
where the supremum is over all finite planar point sets $P$ in general position.

(a) Determine the exact value of $\rho$, or prove the best possible upper and lower bounds on $\rho$.

(b) Let $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}}$ denote the analogous quantity where the supremum is restricted to point sets $P$ in convex position (i.e., the points of $P$ are the vertices of a convex polygon). Prove or disprove that $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}} < \rho$, and determine the best possible upper bound on $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}}$.
status_search_result: The exact worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation remains open. The best known upper bound is approximately 1.998 (Xia, 2013), improving the classical 2.42 bound of Keil–Gutwin (1989); the best known lower bound is approximately 1.5846 (disproving the long-standing π/2 conjecture). For points in convex position, the previously known bound 2.33 (Cui–Kanj–Xia, 2009) has been superseded by the general 1.998 bound, and no strictly smaller upper bound specifically for convex position has been established.

self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, a plane geometric graph on $P$ is a straight-line embedded graph with vertex set $P$ whose edges (drawn as Euclidean line segments) pairwise do not cross. For a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$, define its spanning ratio (or stretch factor) by
$$\mathrm{sr}(G)=\max_{u,v\in P,\ u\neq v}\frac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|},$$
where $d_G(u,v)$ is the length of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ (using Euclidean edge lengths) and $\|u-v\|$ is the Euclidean distance.

Define
$$\rho^*=\inf\Bigl\{C\ge 1:\ \text{for every finite }P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\text{ there exists a connected plane geometric graph }G\text{ on }P\text{ with }\mathrm{sr}(G)\le C\Bigr\}.$$

Determine the exact value of $\rho^*$.

self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in general position, a plane spanning tree of $P$ is a straight-line tree $T$ with vertex set $P$ whose edges (drawn as line segments) are pairwise non-crossing and which connects all points of $P$. For a connected straight-line graph $G$ on $P$, the spanning ratio (also called dilation or stretch factor) of $G$ is
$$\operatorname{sr}(G)\;=\;\max_{u
eq v\in P} rac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|_2},$$
where $d_G(u,v)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $u$ and $v$ (with edge weights equal to Euclidean lengths) and $\|u-v\|_2$ is the Euclidean distance.

Consider the following decision problem: given a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{Q}^2$ and a rational number $\delta\geq 1$, decide whether there exists a plane spanning tree $T$ of $P$ with $\operatorname{sr}(T)\leq\delta$. Equivalently, the optimization problem asks to compute a plane spanning tree of $P$ minimizing $\operatorname{sr}(T)$ among all plane spanning trees on $P$.

No proof of NP-hardness or polynomial-time algorithm specifically for the plane (non-crossing) version has been located.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine whether the guaranteed α-value in the α-diamond-property analysis of greedy triangulations can be improved beyond π/6.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Given a finite point set $P$ in the Euclidean plane, the greedy triangulation of $P$ is constructed as follows: order all $\binom{|P|}{2}$ straight-line segments between pairs of points in non-decreasing order of length, and process them in this order, adding a segment to the current edge set whenever it does not properly cross any previously added segment. The resulting plane graph $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ is a triangulation of the convex hull of $P$.

For a real number $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$, an edge $e=uv$ of a plane graph is said to satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property if at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as base and base angles equal to $\alpha$ contains no vertex of the graph (other than $u$ and $v$) in its interior. A plane graph has the $\alpha$-diamond property if every edge does. Whenever a plane triangulation has the $\alpha$-diamond property, it is a $t$-spanner of the complete Euclidean graph on its vertex set, with stretch factor $t$ bounded by an explicit function of $\alpha$ that decreases as $\alpha$ increases.

It is known that, for every finite point set $P$, the greedy triangulation $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property for $\alpha=\pi/6$.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: For β-skeletons with parameter β in the interval [1, 2], determine whether one can prove a stronger lower bound on the spanning ratio that depends explicitly on β.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. For a real parameter $\beta \geq 1$, the β-skeleton of $P$ (in the circle-based / "lune-based" definition) is the undirected graph on vertex set $P$ in which two points $p, q \in P$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open region $L_\beta(p,q)$ — defined, for $\beta \geq 1$, as the intersection of the two open disks of radius $\beta\,|pq|/2$ whose centers lie on the line through $p$ and $q$ at distance $(\beta/2 - 1/2)|pq|$ from the midpoint of $pq$ on opposite sides — contains no point of $P \setminus \{p,q\}$. (At $\beta = 1$ this is the Gabriel graph; at $\beta = 2$ this is the relative neighborhood graph.)

The spanning ratio (stretch factor) of a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is
$$\mathrm{sr}(G) \;=\; \max_{p \neq q \in P} \frac{d_G(p,q)}{|pq|},$$
where $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ (with edges weighted by Euclidean length), and $|pq|$ denotes the Euclidean distance.

For each $\beta \in [1,2]$, let
$$f(\beta, n) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\mathrm{sr}(\beta\text{-skeleton of } P) \;:\; P \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P| = n\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $f(1,n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$ (Gabriel graphs) and that $f(2,n)$ can be as large as $\Omega(n)$ (relative neighborhood graphs). Determine whether one can establish, for $\beta$ ranging over the interval $[1,2]$, a worst-case lower bound on $f(\beta,n)$ as a function of $n$ that depends explicitly and non-trivially on $\beta$ (i.e., a lower bound that strengthens monotonically as $\beta$ increases from $1$ toward $2$, interpolating between the $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ bound at $\beta=1$ and the $\Omega(n)$ bound at $\beta=2$).
status_search_result: Existing results (Bose–Devroye–Evans–Kirkpatrick and related work) establish that the β-skeleton has spanning ratio $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ for $\beta = 1$ (Gabriel graph) and $\Omega(n)$ in the worst case for $\beta = 2$ (relative neighborhood graph), with a uniform $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ lower bound for $\beta \in [1,2)$. We did not find a published result giving a sharper β-dependent lower bound that interpolates between these extremes for the full range $[1,2]$, so the explicit β-dependent lower bound problem appears to remain open.

self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in general position in the Euclidean plane. For a parameter $\beta\in[0,1]$, the $\beta$-skeleton $\mathrm{BSKEL}_\beta(P)$ is the graph on vertex set $P$ in which two points $p,q\in P$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open lune $L_\beta(p,q)$, defined as the intersection of the two open disks of radius $|pq|/\beta$ passing through both $p$ and $q$ and having centers on the line through $p$ and $q$ (with the convention that for $\beta=0$ the lune degenerates to the open segment $pq$, and for $\beta=1$ it is the open disk with diameter $pq$), contains no point of $P$. Let $\mathrm{DT}(P)$ denote the Delaunay triangulation of $P$. Define the relaxed Gabriel graph
$$\mathrm{RGG}_\beta(P) \;=\; \mathrm{BSKEL}_\beta(P)\,\cap\,\mathrm{DT}(P).$$
For a connected geometric graph $G$ on $P$, its spanning ratio (stretch factor) is
$$t(G) \;=\; \max_{p\neq q\in P}\frac{d_G(p,q)}{|pq|},$$
where $d_G$ denotes the shortest-path distance in $G$ with Euclidean edge weights. Let
$$f(n,\beta) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{t(\mathrm{RGG}_\beta(P)) : |P|=n,\ P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\text{ in general position}\bigr\}.$$
For each fixed $\beta\in[0,1]$, determine whether the currently known asymptotic upper and lower bounds on $f(n,\beta)$ as $n\to\infty$ are tight, i.e., whether they match up to constants (and if not, establish improved matching upper and lower bounds).

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine the smallest possible maximum degree that always suffices to construct a plane spanner on an arbitrary finite planar point set.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in the plane, a geometric graph on $P$ is a graph whose vertex set is $P$ and whose edges are straight-line segments between pairs of points of $P$, with edge weights equal to the Euclidean lengths of the segments. Such a graph is called plane if no two of its edges cross. For a real number $t\geq 1$, a geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is a $t$-spanner of $P$ if for every pair $p,q\in P$ the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ is at most $t\cdot\|p-q\|$. The maximum degree of $G$ is $\Delta(G)=\max_{v\in P}\deg_G(v)$.

Determine the smallest integer $\Delta^\ast$ with the following property: there exists a constant $t\geq 1$ (independent of $P$) such that for every finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ there exists a plane $t$-spanner $G$ on $P$ with $\Delta(G)\leq \Delta^\ast$.
status_search_result: It is known that 3 is a lower bound on the maximum degree of any plane spanner. Bonichon, Kanj, Perković, and Ravelomanana (2014) proved that maximum degree 4 always suffices, with stretch factor improved by Kanj, Perković, and Türkoğlu (SoCG 2016) to 20. Whether maximum degree 3 suffices for arbitrary point sets remains open; for points in convex position degree 3 is known to be tight.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine whether the known bounds for constructing plane spanners that simultaneously have low total weight and bounded maximum degree are tight.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane. A geometric graph on $P$ is a straight-line graph whose vertex set is $P$, with edge weights equal to the Euclidean lengths of the corresponding segments. A geometric graph $G$ is called a plane $t$-spanner of $P$ (for some real constant $t \geq 1$, called the stretch factor) if (i) no two edges of $G$ cross, and (ii) for every pair of points $p, q \in P$, the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ is at most $t \cdot \|pq\|$, where $\|pq\|$ is the Euclidean distance.

The total weight $w(G)$ of $G$ is the sum of its edge weights, and $w(\mathrm{MST}(P))$ denotes the weight of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$. The maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ is the largest number of edges incident to any vertex.

It is known that for every finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ one can construct, in $O(n \log n)$ time, a plane $t$-spanner $G$ of $P$ satisfying simultaneously
\[
\Delta(G) \leq D, \qquad t \leq T, \qquad w(G) \leq C \cdot w(\mathrm{MST}(P)),
\]
for certain absolute constants $D$, $T$, and $C$ achieved by existing constructions.

Question: Are the currently known constants $D$, $T$, and $C$ for the simultaneous bounded-degree, bounded-stretch, low-weight plane spanner problem tight? More precisely, determine matching lower bounds (or improved upper bounds) on the achievable triples $(D, T, C)$ such that every $n$-point set in the plane admits a plane $t$-spanner with maximum degree at most $D$, stretch factor at most $T$, and total weight at most $C \cdot w(\mathrm{MST}(P))$.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., experimental and algorithmic studies through the early 2020s) continues to refine the constants for degree, stretch, and weight in plane spanner constructions, with at least 11 known algorithms offering different tradeoffs. No publication establishes that the simultaneous bounds on degree, stretch factor, and weight-to-MST ratio are tight; the constants in known proofs are widely regarded as worst-case artifacts. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Determine the smallest real number t such that every finite planar point set has dilation at most t when dilation is defined as the infimum, over all plane graphs with only finitely many added Steiner vertices, of the graph’s spanning ratio on all points of the set.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set S of points in the Euclidean plane, define the dilation of S as follows. Consider all plane (i.e., crossing-free) straight-line graphs G whose vertex set consists of S together with finitely many additional Steiner points in the plane. For such a graph G, let
  d_G(p,q) = (length of a shortest path in G from p to q),
and define the spanning ratio of G on S by
  sr_S(G) = sup_{p ≠ q ∈ S}  d_G(p,q) / |pq|,
where |pq| denotes Euclidean distance. The dilation of S is then
  Δ(S) = inf_G sr_S(G),
where the infimum is taken over all such plane graphs G with finitely many Steiner points.

Determine the smallest real number t such that Δ(S) ≤ t for every finite set S of points in the plane. Equivalently, compute
  t* = sup_S Δ(S),
where the supremum is over all finite planar point sets S. (It is known that 1.00157 ≤ t* ≤ 1.1247; close the gap.)
status_search_result: The question of the optimal universal dilation constant for finite planar point sets (with finitely many Steiner points allowed) is a long-standing open problem in the geometric spanners literature. Known bounds remain roughly 1.00157 ≤ t* ≤ 1.1247, with works on related geometric-dilation variants (e.g., Dumitrescu–Gärtner–Rote; Ebbers-Baumann et al.; Mulzer; Klein) refining lower bounds slightly above π/2 in the related geometric-dilation setting, but no published resolution closing the gap for the graph-theoretic spanning-ratio version has been found.

original_question: Determine the smallest real number t such that every finite planar point set has geometric dilation at most t, where geometric dilation takes the supremum over all pairs of points lying on the graph’s edges or vertices rather than only over original input vertices.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and a connected planar embedded graph $G$ whose vertex set contains $P$ (edges are rectifiable Jordan arcs in the plane), define the geometric dilation of $G$ by
$$\delta(G)=\sup_{p\neq q}\frac{d_G(p,q)}{\|p-q\|},$$
where the supremum is taken over all pairs of distinct points $p,q$ that lie on the vertices or edges of $G$ (not only on the vertices of $G$), $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $p$ and $q$ measured along the embedded edges, and $\|p-q\|$ denotes the Euclidean distance. Define the geometric dilation of the point set $P$ by
$$\delta(P)=\inf_{G\supseteq P}\delta(G),$$
where the infimum ranges over all such planar graphs $G$ containing $P$ among its vertices.

Determine the exact value of
$$t^* = \sup\{\delta(P) : P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\text{ finite}\},$$
i.e. the smallest real number $t$ such that every finite planar point set admits an embedding into a planar graph of geometric dilation at most $t$. It is known that
$$\left(1+10^{-11}\right)\frac{\pi}{2}\le t^*\le 1.678.$$

paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: For a connected unit-disk graph UDG(P) modeling a wireless ad hoc network on a planar point set P, reduce the total number of broadcast messages needed by a local distributed algorithm to compute a plane local spanner of UDG(P).
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane. The unit-disk graph UDG(P) is the graph with vertex set P in which two points are adjacent if and only if their Euclidean distance is at most 1; assume UDG(P) is connected. A subgraph H of UDG(P) is called a plane spanner if H is planar (its straight-line embedding has no crossing edges) and there exists a constant t ≥ 1 such that for every pair u,v ∈ P, the length of a shortest path from u to v in H (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) is at most t times the length of a shortest path between u and v in UDG(P).

Consider the distributed model in which each node of UDG(P) is an autonomous processor that knows only its own coordinates and can communicate by local broadcast to all neighbors within unit distance. A distributed algorithm is called local if every node decides which of its incident edges belong to H using only information gathered from a constant-size neighborhood (e.g., its k-hop neighborhood for some constant k). The message complexity is the total number of broadcast messages exchanged during the execution of the algorithm.

Problem: Design a local distributed algorithm that, given a connected UDG(P) on n nodes, computes a plane spanner of UDG(P) using strictly fewer total broadcast messages than the previously known bound (e.g., better than the current best known O(n)-broadcast algorithms with their explicit constants), and determine the minimum achievable message complexity for this task.
status_search_result: Recent work has continued to reduce the message complexity of distributed plane spanner construction in unit-disk graphs (e.g., algorithms achieving on the order of 5n broadcasts), and further improvements ("Improved Local Algorithms for Spanner Construction") have been published. However, no tight lower bound matches the upper bounds, and the question of the minimum message complexity for computing a plane local spanner of UDG(P) appears to remain open.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: What are the proper minimal assumptions on the inter-arrival-time and service-time distributions under which the critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue satisfies the conjectured BRAVO asymptotic γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)? In particular, which tail or moment conditions are actually needed, since the paper's exponential-moment light-tail assumption appears stronger than necessary and the author does not know the correct minimal condition.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite buffer of size K (a GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2; service times are i.i.d., independent of the arrivals, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. Customers arriving to a full system (K customers present, including the one in service) are lost. The queue is taken to be critically loaded, meaning λ = μ. Let D(t) denote the number of service completions (departures) in [0, t] in steady state, and define the asymptotic variance rate

   V_K := lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

and the normalized quantity γ*_K := V_K / (the corresponding service rate). The BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Output) conjecture for this model asserts that, as K → ∞,

   γ*_K = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).

This conjecture has been formulated under the assumption that the inter-arrival and service distributions possess finite exponential moments (light-tail condition). Determine the minimal moment / tail conditions on the inter-arrival and service-time distributions under which the above asymptotic formula γ*_K = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) holds. In particular, identify a sharp moment hypothesis (e.g., a finite p-th moment for some specific p) replacing the exponential-moment assumption.
status_search_result: Recent work (2022–2024) on BRAVO for critical GI/G/1 and GI/G/1/K queues has progressively weakened moment assumptions—e.g., establishing busy-period regular variation under finite second moments and reducing the uniform-integrability hypothesis from fourth to lower moments—but a sharp minimal-condition characterization for the γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) asymptotic in GI/G/1/K is not reported as established. The problem of identifying the proper minimal tail/moment condition appears still open.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: Give a complete intuitive explanation for the BRAVO phenomenon in these queueing models, especially the appearance of the factor 2/3 (equivalently 1/3 in the variability parameter formula) for finite-capacity critical queues. The question asks for a conceptual account of why balancing arrival and service rates reduces the asymptotic departure variance in this way, rather than only a formal proof of the GI/G/1/K conjecture.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue of type GI/G/1/K with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ and finite variance, i.i.d. service times having mean 1/μ and finite variance, a single server, and a finite buffer of capacity K (so that arrivals finding K customers in the system are lost). Let D(t) denote the number of customers that have departed (completed service) by time t. Under stability and standard regularity assumptions, the asymptotic variance rate

  V(λ, μ, K) := lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t))/t

is well defined. It is known that for the M/M/1/K queue with λ = μ (the critical case), as K → ∞,

  V(λ, λ, K) → (2/3) λ,

whereas for λ ≠ μ the limit equals min(λ, μ) times a different constant; equivalently, the asymptotic variability parameter (the squared coefficient of variation of D) at criticality picks up a factor of 1/3 instead of 1. This sharp drop at the balanced point λ = μ is the BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs) phenomenon.

Problem. Provide a complete conceptual/intuitive explanation of the BRAVO phenomenon for finite-capacity critical queues. Specifically, give a transparent probabilistic mechanism that explains:

(a) why balancing the arrival and service rates (λ = μ) causes the asymptotic variance rate of the departure process to be strictly smaller than min(λ, μ) times the average variability of the arrival and service processes, even though intuitively the queue should add variability to the output;

(b) why the precise universal numerical factor 2/3 (equivalently the 1/3 reduction in the variability parameter) arises in the limit K → ∞ for a wide class of GI/G/1/K critical queues.

The required answer is a conceptual account that identifies the underlying mechanism producing the constant 2/3, not merely a computational proof of the corresponding asymptotic formula.
status_search_result: The BRAVO effect remains an active research topic. While the 2/3 asymptotic factor has been rigorously proved for various critical queueing models (M/M/1/K, GI/G/1/K, many-server QED systems) and recent work has connected it to phase transitions, oscillating cumulants, busy-period analysis, and heavy-traffic limits, no source identified provides a single, fully intuitive conceptual explanation of why the universal 2/3 constant appears. paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: Does the existence-and-uniqueness theory for the continuity equation and the associated regular Lagrangian flow extend from BV- and LD-type assumptions to vector fields in BD, where BD is the space of functions u such that the symmetric distributional derivative Du + tDu is representable by a measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be an open set and $T>0$. Recall the following function spaces of weakly differentiable vector fields $b:(0,T)\times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$:

- $BV$: vector fields whose distributional gradient $Db$ is representable by a (matrix-valued) finite Radon measure.
- $LD$ (functions of locally bounded deformation): vector fields whose symmetric distributional gradient $\tfrac{1}{2}(Db + (Db)^{T})$ lies in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$.
- $BD$ (functions of bounded deformation): vector fields $b$ such that the symmetric distributional derivative $Eb := \tfrac{1}{2}(Db + (Db)^{T})$ is representable by a finite Radon measure with values in the symmetric $d\times d$ matrices.

For a Borel vector field $b$ with bounded divergence, a regular Lagrangian flow is a Borel map $X:[0,T]\times \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for $\mathcal{L}^d$-a.e. $x$, $t\mapsto X(t,x)$ is an absolutely continuous integral solution of $\dot{X}(t,x) = b(t,X(t,x))$ with $X(0,x)=x$, and such that $X(t,\cdot)_{\#}\mathcal{L}^d \le C\,\mathcal{L}^d$ uniformly in $t\in[0,T]$. The associated continuity equation is
$$\partial_t \rho + \mathrm{div}(b\,\rho) = 0, \qquad \rho(0,\cdot)=\rho_0.$$

The DiPerna–Lions–Ambrosio theory establishes existence and uniqueness of the regular Lagrangian flow and well-posedness of the continuity equation in the class of bounded densities under $BV$ regularity of $b$ (with bounded divergence), as well as under $LD$-type assumptions.

Question: Does this existence-and-uniqueness theory for the continuity equation and for the associated regular Lagrangian flow extend to vector fields $b$ in $BD$ with bounded divergence? That is, for every $b \in L^{1}((0,T); BD(\Omega))$ with $\mathrm{div}\, b \in L^{\infty}$ and suitable growth/boundedness assumptions, do there exist a unique regular Lagrangian flow associated with $b$ and a unique bounded weak solution of the continuity equation with prescribed bounded initial datum?
category_tag: Regular Lagrangian flows for nonsmooth vector fields
status_search_result: A web search for results on well-posedness of the continuity equation and regular Lagrangian flow for vector fields of bounded deformation (BD) returned only results for the BV, LD, Sobolev, and metric-measure-space settings; no paper resolving the BD case was found. The extension to BD vector fields appears to remain an open problem.

paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: Let ν be a regular measure on P(R^d), meaning that its expectation Eν is bounded above by C·L^d for some constant C. Can there exist a ν-regular Lagrangian flow μ in P(R^d) that is not induced by any L^d-regular Lagrangian flow X in R^d via the formula μ(t,μ)=∫_{R^d} δ_{X(t,x)} dμ(x)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 1$ and let $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the space of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$, equipped with its natural Polish topology. Let $\mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ denote the set of nonnegative finite Borel measures on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. For $\nu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d))$, define its expectation $\mathbb{E}\nu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by
$$\mathbb{E}\nu(A) := \int_{\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \mu(A)\, d\nu(\mu), \qquad A \subset \mathbb{R}^d \text{ Borel}.$$
Call $\nu$ regular if $\mathbb{E}\nu \le C \mathcal{L}^d$ for some constant $C \ge 0$, where $\mathcal{L}^d$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$.

Fix a Borel time-dependent vector field $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$. An $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow (RLF) for $b$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a Borel map $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that:
(i) for $\mathcal{L}^d$-a.e. $x$, $t\mapsto X(t,x)$ is an absolutely continuous integral solution of $\dot\gamma(t)=b(t,\gamma(t))$ with $\gamma(0)=x$; and
(ii) there is $L\ge 0$ with $X(t,\cdot)_\#\mathcal{L}^d \le L\,\mathcal{L}^d$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.

Lift $b$ to a vector field $B$ on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (in the sense used in continuity-equation theory on Wasserstein space). A $\nu$-regular Lagrangian flow for $B$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is a Borel map $\boldsymbol{\mu}:[0,T]\times\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that:
(i') for $\nu$-a.e. $\mu$, $t\mapsto\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\mu)$ is an integral curve of $B$ starting at $\mu$; and
(ii') $\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\cdot)_\#\nu$ is regular with a uniform bound in $t$.

Given an $\mathcal{L}^d$-RLF $X$, one induces a flow on $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by
$$\boldsymbol{\mu}(t,\mu) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\delta_{X(t,x)}\,d\mu(x). \qquad (*)$$

Question: Does there exist a regular $\nu$ and a $\nu$-regular Lagrangian flow $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that is not of the form $(*)$ for any $\mathcal{L}^d$-regular Lagrangian flow $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$?
status_search_result: The question concerns existence of genuinely "higher-level" regular Lagrangian flows on the space of probability measures that are not lifts of classical RLFs on $\mathbb{R}^d$. It is posed as a speculative open problem in surveys on flows of weakly differentiable vector fields, and no resolution appears in the literature available via search.

For a positive integer m, let H_m = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/m denote the m-th harmonic number. For an integer k ≥ 2, evaluate in closed form the k-fold series
   T_k = Σ_{n_1=1}^∞ Σ_{n_2=1}^∞ ··· Σ_{n_k=1}^∞ (-1)^{n_1+n_2+...+n_k} · (H_{n_1} H_{n_2} ··· H_{n_k}) / (n_1 n_2 ··· n_k (n_1 + n_2 + ··· + n_k)),

paper_title: Time and Norm Optimal Controls: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: Consider the self-adjoint setting discussed in the paper: A is a self-adjoint infinitesimal generator in a separable Hilbert space, H_α = D((μI - A)^α), and a control is called regular when its multiplier z belongs to Z(T) and strongly regular when z belongs to E*. Is it true in this self-adjoint setting that whenever an optimal control reaches a target ȳ satisfying ȳ ∈ D(A), the associated multiplier must actually satisfy z ∈ E*? Equivalently, does regularity imply strong regularity in the borderline case α = 1 of the smoothness relation between the target and the costate?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space and let A: D(A) ⊂ H → H be a self-adjoint infinitesimal generator of a strongly continuous semigroup {S(t)}_{t≥0} on H. Fix μ ∈ ℝ such that μI − A is positive and self-adjoint, and for α ≥ 0 define the scale of Hilbert spaces H_α = D((μI − A)^α) endowed with the graph norm ‖x‖_α = ‖(μI − A)^α x‖. Set H_{−α} to be the completion of H with respect to ‖x‖_{−α} = ‖(μI − A)^{−α} x‖, so that (H_α)* ≅ H_{−α}.

Consider the linear control system
   y'(t) = A y(t) + B u(t),  t ∈ [0, T],   y(0) = y_0,
with admissible controls u ∈ L^∞(0, T; U) (U a Hilbert space) and a bounded control operator B: U → H. For a fixed target ȳ ∈ H, an admissible control u is called norm/time optimal if it achieves ȳ at time T while minimizing the corresponding cost. To any optimal control u there is associated, via the Pontryagin maximum principle, a "multiplier" (costate) z, characterised through the dual semigroup; this z lies a priori in a space of distributions on [0,T] taking values in an extrapolation space.

Let Z(T) denote the space of admissible multipliers (those z for which the maximum principle pairing ⟨B^* S(T−t)^* z, u(t)⟩ is well defined for all admissible u), and let E* ⊂ Z(T) denote the subspace of "strongly regular" multipliers (those z for which the costate trajectory t ↦ S(T−t)^* z takes values in the dual H_{−1}^* ≅ H_1, equivalently z is associated to an element in the natural energy space).

Call an optimal control regular if its multiplier z belongs to Z(T), and strongly regular if z ∈ E*.

Question. Suppose A is self-adjoint as above. If an optimal control reaches a target ȳ with ȳ ∈ D(A), must its associated multiplier z satisfy z ∈ E*? Equivalently, in the borderline case α = 1 of the smoothness correspondence between target and costate, does regularity imply strong regularity?
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this borderline α = 1 implication (regular ⇒ strongly regular under self-adjoint A with target in D(A)) was located in standard searches; it is described as an open problem in the surrounding literature on time- and norm-optimal control, and no later work clearly settling it was identified.

original_question: For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S_- be the backward shift on z(N0) and let r(S_-|z) be its spectral radius. Determine whether the spectrum of S_- is always exactly the closed disk {lambda in C : |lambda| <= r(S_-|z)}.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let z(N0) be a shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let L^{APP}_z be the operator ideal consisting of all bounded operators S between Banach spaces for which the dyadic approximation-number sequence (a_{2^k}(S)) belongs to z(N0). Theorem 1.19 constructs traces on L^{APP}_z from (1/2)S_+-invariant linear forms φ on z(N0) by choosing a z-representation S=∑_{k>=0} S_k and setting φ_z(S)=φ((2^{-k} trace(S_k))_k). Show that every trace on L^{APP}_z is of this form, so that L^{APP}_z carries no traces other than those produced in Theorem 1.19.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. The forward dyadic shift is the linear map $S_+\colon \ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)\to\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ defined by $(S_+ x)_k = x_{k-1}$ for $k\ge 1$ and $(S_+ x)_0=0$. A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called a shift-monotone sequence ideal if it is solid (i.e.\ $|y_k|\le |x_k|$ for all $k$ and $x\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ imply $y\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$) and satisfies $S_+ x\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ whenever $x\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

For a bounded linear operator $S\colon X\to Y$ between Banach spaces, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(S)=\inf\{\,\|S-A\|: A\colon X\to Y, \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\,\},\qquad n\ge 1.$$
Define the operator ideal
$$\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}=\bigl\{\,S\in\mathfrak{L}(X,Y):\ X,Y\text{ Banach},\ (a_{2^k}(S))_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\bigr\}.$$
A $z$-representation of $S\in\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ is a series $S=\sum_{k\ge 0} S_k$ converging in operator norm with $\mathrm{rank}(S_k)\le 2^k$ and such that $(\|S_k\|)_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$; every $S\in\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ admits such a representation.

A trace on $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,X)$ for all Banach spaces $X$ such that $\tau(BA)=\tau(AB)$ whenever the products make sense and lie in $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$, and $\tau$ is normalized on rank-one operators by the usual trace.

Construction of traces. Let $\varphi\colon z(\mathbb{N}_0)\to\mathbb{C}$ be a linear form that is invariant under the operator $\tfrac{1}{2}S_+$, i.e.\ $\varphi(\tfrac{1}{2}S_+ x)=\varphi(x)$ for all $x\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. For $S\in\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ and a $z$-representation $S=\sum_{k\ge 0} S_k$, define
$$\varphi_z(S)=\varphi\bigl((2^{-k}\,\mathrm{trace}(S_k))_{k\ge 0}\bigr),$$
where $\mathrm{trace}(S_k)$ denotes the ordinary trace of the finite-rank operator $S_k$. This expression is independent of the chosen $z$-representation and yields a trace on $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$.

Problem. Show that for every shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, every trace $\tau$ on the operator ideal $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ arises from some $\tfrac{1}{2}S_+$-invariant linear form $\varphi$ on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ by the construction $\tau=\varphi_z$ above. Equivalently, prove that no traces on $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ exist other than those obtained in this way.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in Pietsch's program on traces on Banach-space operator ideals. Web search returns the survey itself and related works (Pietsch; Levitina–Pietsch–Sukochev–Zanin), which resolve some companion problems (e.g., completeness) but no source indicates a resolution of this particular classification of traces on $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ in the Banach-space setting. The Hilbert-space analogue is known, but the general Banach-space statement appears to remain open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: An operator ideal A is called traceless if it admits no nonzero trace. Show that every norm-closed operator ideal is traceless.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces, and let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the Banach space of bounded linear operators from a Banach space $X$ to a Banach space $Y$. An operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is an assignment to each pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$ of a linear subspace $\mathcal{A}(X,Y) \subseteq \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) every finite-rank operator belongs to $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$;
(ii) for $S \in \mathcal{L}(X_0,X)$, $T \in \mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, $R \in \mathcal{L}(Y,Y_0)$ one has $RTS \in \mathcal{A}(X_0,Y_0)$.
The ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is called norm-closed if for every pair $(X,Y)$ the component $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$ is closed in $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ with respect to the operator norm.

A trace on $\mathcal{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X : \mathcal{A}(X,X) \to \mathbb{C}$ (one for each Banach space $X$) such that:
(a) $\tau_X(yx) = \tau_Y(xy)$ for all $x \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ and $y \in \mathcal{A}(Y,X)$ (with $yx \in \mathcal{A}(X,X)$ and $xy \in \mathcal{A}(Y,Y)$);
(b) $\tau_X$ extends the usual trace on finite-rank operators on $X$, i.e. $\tau_X(a \otimes x^*) = \langle x^*, a\rangle$ for all $a \in X$, $x^* \in X^*$.

The ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is called traceless if the only trace on $\mathcal{A}$ is the zero functional family (equivalently, no nonzero trace exists on $\mathcal{A}$).

Prove that every norm-closed operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces is traceless.

Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r. Theorem 1.21 constructs a trace φ_{r,\infty}(·|A) on A^{APP}_{r,\infty}. Determine whether this trace is spectral, meaning that for each operator in the ideal its value can be reconstructed from the operator's eigenvalue sequence.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between (arbitrary) Banach spaces, and let $\mathfrak{A}$ be a quasi-Banach operator ideal, i.e. a subclass $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak{A}}$ making each component $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ a quasi-Banach space and satisfying the usual ideal property $\|BTA\|_{\mathfrak{A}}\le \|B\|\,\|T\|_{\mathfrak{A}}\,\|A\|$.

For an operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ define the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|: F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}\,F<n\},\qquad n=1,2,\dots$$
For $0<r<\infty$ define the Lorentz-type approximation ideal
$$\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}=\{T\in\mathcal{L}: \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} a_n(T)<\infty\}.$$

Say that a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is of exact trace type $1/r$ (with $0<r<\infty$) in the sense required for the construction of the trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})$: there exists a continuous trace on $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ obtained by an averaging/limit procedure applied to the approximation numbers and the trace structure on finite-rank operators of $\mathfrak{A}$, yielding a linear functional
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})\colon\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}\to\mathbb{C}$$
that vanishes on commutators $ST-TS$ whenever both $S,T$ make sense in the ideal.

A trace $\varphi$ on an operator ideal $\mathfrak{I}\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ is called spectral if its value on every $T\in\mathfrak{I}$ depends only on the eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_n(T))$ of $T$ (counted with algebraic multiplicities and arranged so that $|\lambda_1(T)|\ge|\lambda_2(T)|\ge\cdots$); equivalently, there exists a symmetric functional $\Lambda$ on the corresponding space of eigenvalue sequences such that $\varphi(T)=\Lambda(\lambda_n(T))$ for every $T\in\mathfrak{I}$.

Problem. For every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ of exact trace type $1/r$, decide whether the trace
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})$$
on $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is spectral.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem about whether a specific trace constructed on the approximation Lorentz-type ideal $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is spectral. While there are general results characterizing spectral traces on Hilbert-space operator ideals (e.g. Sukochev–Zanin "Which traces are spectral?"), no resolution of the spectrality of $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid\mathfrak{A})$ for general Banach operator ideals of exact trace type $1/r$ was located.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: For 1 <= r <= 2, let P_{r,2} denote the ideal of (r,2)-summing operators. Determine whether the trace φ_{r,\infty}(·|P_{r,2}) on (P_{r,2})^{APP}_{r,\infty} constructed in Theorem 2.4 is spectral.
self_contained_problem:
Let $1\le r\le 2$. An operator $T:X\to Y$ between Banach spaces is called $(r,2)$-summing if there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for every finite family $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$,
$$\Big(\sum_{k=1}^n\|Tx_k\|^r\Big)^{1/r}\le C\,\sup_{\|x^*\|\le 1}\Big(\sum_{k=1}^n |x^*(x_k)|^2\Big)^{1/2}.$$
The class of all such operators forms a Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak P_{r,2}$, equipped with its natural norm $\pi_{r,2}$.

For an operator $T:X\to X$ on a Banach space $X$, let $a_n(T)$ denote its $n$-th approximation number,
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-A\|:A:X\to X,\ \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\}.$$
For $0<p<\infty$ and $0<q\le\infty$, the approximation component of $\mathfrak P_{r,2}$ of type $(p,q)$ is
$$(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{p,q}=\{T\in\mathfrak P_{r,2}:(a_n(T))_{n\ge 1}\in\ell_{p,q}\},$$
where $\ell_{p,q}$ is the Lorentz sequence space. In particular,
$$(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}=\{T\in\mathfrak P_{r,2}:\sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r}a_n(T)<\infty\}.$$

Assume that on the component $(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ (acting on Banach spaces) there exists a continuous linear trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\,|\mathfrak P_{r,2})$ (a linear functional satisfying $\varphi(ST)=\varphi(TS)$ whenever both compositions lie in the component, and reducing to the usual finite-rank trace on finite-rank operators).

Recall that a trace $\tau$ defined on an operator ideal component is called spectral if for every operator $T$ in its domain,
$$\tau(T)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \lambda_n(T),$$
where $(\lambda_n(T))_{n\ge 1}$ denotes the eigenvalue sequence of $T$ (counted with algebraic multiplicities and arranged in non-increasing order of absolute values).

Question: Is the trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\,|\mathfrak P_{r,2})$ on $(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ spectral?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. Web searches did not turn up a published resolution; available literature on summing operators, eigenvalue estimates and singular traces discusses related Lidskii-type results but no specific answer concerning the spectrality of the trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\cdot|\mathfrak P_{r,2})$ on the approximation component $(\mathfrak P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ for $1\le r\le 2$.

original_question: For 1 <= r < \infty, compare the two operator ideals (P_{r,2})^{APP}_{r,\infty} and (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty}, where P_{r,2} is the ideal of (r,2)-summing operators and L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty} is the Weyl-number generated ideal. Show that these two ideals coincide.
self_contained_problem:
Let $1 \le r < \infty$. Work in the category of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. Recall the following definitions.

(a) The ideal $P_{r,2}$ of $(r,2)$-summing operators consists of all operators $T : X \to Y$ such that there is a constant $C \ge 0$ with
$$\Big(\sum_{k=1}^n \|T x_k\|^r\Big)^{1/r} \le C \sup\Big\{\Big(\sum_{k=1}^n |\langle x_k, x^*\rangle|^2\Big)^{1/2} : x^* \in X^*,\ \|x^*\| \le 1\Big\}$$
for every finite family $x_1,\dots,x_n \in X$.

(b) For an operator $T : X \to Y$ and $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th Weyl number $x_n(T)$ is defined by
$$x_n(T) = \sup\{ a_n(T A) : A : \ell_2 \to X,\ \|A\| \le 1\},$$
where $a_n(\cdot)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number. The Weyl-number generated Lorentz-type ideal $L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}$ consists of those operators $T$ for which
$$\sup_{n \ge 1} n^{1/r} x_n(T) < \infty.$$

(c) The $n$-th approximation number of $T : X \to Y$ is
$$a_n(T) = \inf\{ \|T - F\| : F : X \to Y,\ \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}.$$
Given a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal A$, define its approximation-Lorentz hull $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ as the class of all operators $T$ such that there exists a sequence $(T_k)$ with $T_k \in \mathcal A$ for which $\sup_{k \ge 1} k^{1/r} a_k(T - T_{k-1}) < \infty$ in an appropriate sense (the standard $(r,\infty)$-Lorentz approximation procedure applied to $\mathcal A$).

Prove that the two operator ideals
$$(P_{r,2})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty} \quad \text{and} \quad (L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$$
coincide.

original_question: For 1 <= r < \infty, determine whether the trace φ_{r,\infty}(·|L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty}) on (L^{WEYL}_{r,\infty})^{APP}_{r,\infty} constructed in Theorem 2.8 is spectral.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let X be a complex Banach space and L(X) the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on X. For T ∈ L(X), the n-th Weyl number is
  x_n(T) = inf{ a_n(T A) : A : ℓ_2 → X, ‖A‖ ≤ 1 },
where a_n denotes the n-th approximation number. For 1 ≤ r < ∞, the Weyl operator ideal of Lorentz type L^{WEYL}_{r,∞} consists of all operators T (acting between arbitrary Banach spaces) such that
  ‖T‖_{L^{WEYL}_{r,∞}} = sup_{n≥1} n^{1/r} x_n(T) < ∞.
For an operator ideal I and parameters (p,q), one denotes by I^{APP}_{p,q} the sub-ideal of all T ∈ I that additionally belong to the approximation-number Lorentz ideal L^{APP}_{p,q}, i.e. sup_{n≥1} n^{1/p} a_n(T) < ∞ when q = ∞.

  φ_{r,∞}( · | L^{WEYL}_{r,∞} ) : (L^{WEYL}_{r,∞})^{APP}_{r,∞}(X) → ℂ,
defined on the component over each Banach space X, that is constructed from the Weyl ideal L^{WEYL}_{r,∞} (via a Dixmier-type / extended-limit procedure on its quasi-Banach component).

A trace φ on a two-sided operator ideal I (defined for every Banach space) is called spectral if for every Banach space X and every T ∈ I(X),
  φ(T) = Σ_{n} λ_n(T),
where (λ_n(T)) is the eigenvalue sequence of T counted with algebraic multiplicities (the series being absolutely convergent for T in the relevant ideal).

original_question: For every shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let L^{APP}_z be the ideal defined from dyadic approximation numbers and let L^{ENT}_z be the ideal defined from dyadic entropy numbers. Show that L^{APP}_z is contained in L^{ENT}_z for all shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. For an operator $T:X\to Y$ between Banach spaces, define:

- The $n$-th approximation number $a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T-A\| : A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\}$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
- The $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number $e_n(T) = \inf\{\varepsilon>0 : T(B_X)\ \text{can be covered by}\ 2^{n-1}\ \text{balls of radius}\ \varepsilon\ \text{in}\ Y\}$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

Set the dyadic versions $a_n^{\mathrm{dy}}(T) = a_{2^{n}}(T)$ and $e_n^{\mathrm{dy}}(T) = e_{2^{n}}(T)$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$.

Sequence ideals. Let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the linear space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called a sequence ideal if it is solid (i.e. $|s_n|\le|t_n|$ for all $n$ and $(t_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ imply $(s_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$). It is called shift-monotone if it is closed under both the left and right shift operators: $(s_0,s_1,s_2,\dots)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ if and only if $(s_1,s_2,\dots)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and $(0,s_0,s_1,\dots)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ for all $(s_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

Operator ideals generated by sequence ideals. For a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the operator classes
$$L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z} = \{\,T\in\mathcal{L} : (a_n^{\mathrm{dy}}(T))_{n\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\},$$
$$L^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{z} = \{\,T\in\mathcal{L} : (e_n^{\mathrm{dy}}(T))_{n\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\}.$$

Problem. Prove that $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}\subseteq L^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{z}$ for every shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a list of open questions on traces and operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. Web searches did not surface a published proof or counterexample establishing the inclusion $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\subseteq L^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ for arbitrary shift-monotone sequence ideals; related work (e.g., comparisons of entropy and approximation numbers) addresses specific scales but not the full general statement. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces, and for a bounded linear operator $S\colon X\to Y$ let $a_n(S)$ denote its $n$-th approximation number, defined by

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
context_brief: Banach spaces with few approximable operators.
original_question: Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X for which the set app(X) of approximation-number profiles realized by approximable operators on X is strictly smaller than the full cone c_0^*(N) of nonincreasing null sequences. In other words, find Banach spaces that have few approximable operators, and ideally make app(X) as small as possible.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. For a bounded linear operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, define the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T) := \inf\{\|T - F\| : F \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \operatorname{rank}(F) < n\}, \qquad n = 1,2,\dots .$$
The sequence $(a_n(T))_{n\ge 1}$ is nonincreasing, and $T$ is called approximable if it is the operator-norm limit of finite-rank operators on $X$, equivalently $a_n(T) \to 0$. Let $c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$ denote the cone of all nonincreasing sequences of nonnegative real numbers tending to $0$, and define
$$\operatorname{app}(X) := \{(a_n(T))_{n\ge 1} : T \in \mathcal{L}(X)\ \text{is approximable}\} \subseteq c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N}).$$
For a general infinite-dimensional Banach space one has $\operatorname{app}(X) = c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$. The problem is to find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ for which the inclusion $\operatorname{app}(X) \subsetneq c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$ is strict, and, more ambitiously, to construct $X$ for which the cone $\operatorname{app}(X)$ is as small as possible (ideally close to a minimal nontrivial subcone of $c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$).
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. No solution or substantive partial result identifying infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ with $\operatorname{app}(X)$ strictly smaller than $c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$ was found in the literature search. Related work on operator ideals and approximation properties exists, but does not resolve this question.

context_brief: Restriction of the strange trace to \ell_2.
original_question: Let X_K be the Argyros-Haydon C_0-trivial Banach space used in the paper's construction of the singular trace τ_Z on the quasi-Banach operator ideal N(2/3,Z). Describe the restriction of τ_Z to the component N(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2), and determine in particular whether this restriction might vanish identically on all of N(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2).

Setup. Let $X_K$ denote an Argyros–Haydon Banach space: an infinite-dimensional separable Banach space with a Schauder basis on which every bounded linear operator has the form $\lambda I + S$ with $\lambda$ a scalar and $S$ a compact operator (a $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Banach space).

For $0<r<\infty$ and a Banach space $Y$, recall the quasi-Banach ideal $\mathfrak{N}^{(r)}$ of $r$-nuclear operators: an operator $T:Y\to Z$ between Banach spaces belongs to $\mathfrak{N}^{(r)}(Y,Z)$ iff it admits a representation
$$T=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} y_n^*\otimes z_n,\quad y_n^*\in Y^*,\ z_n\in Z,\quad \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\|y_n^*\|^r\|z_n\|^r<\infty,$$
with the natural quasi-norm. Fix $r=2/3$.

Let $\mathfrak{Z}$ be the operator ideal whose components $\mathfrak{Z}(Y,Z)$ are characterized as follows: $T\in\mathfrak{Z}(Y,Z)$ iff $T$ factors through some $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Banach space (e.g. through an Argyros–Haydon space). Assume the existence of a non-zero singular trace $\tau_{\mathfrak{Z}}$ on $\mathfrak{N}^{(2/3)}_{\mathfrak{Z}}$, that is, a linear functional defined on every component $\mathfrak{N}^{(2/3)}_{\mathfrak{Z}}(Y,Y)$ which is invariant under cyclic commutation: $\tau_{\mathfrak{Z}}(AB)=\tau_{\mathfrak{Z}}(BA)$ for compatible operators.

Restriction to $\ell_2$. Consider the component
$$\mathfrak{N}^{(2/3)}_{X_K}(\ell_2):=\{\,T\in\mathfrak{N}^{(2/3)}(\ell_2,\ell_2)\ :\ T\text{ factors through }X_K\,\}.$$

Problem.
(a) Describe explicitly the restriction of $\tau_{\mathfrak{Z}}$ to $\mathfrak{N}^{(2/3)}_{X_K}(\ell_2)$.

(b) In particular, determine whether $\tau_{\mathfrak{Z}}\equiv 0$ on the whole of $\mathfrak{N}^{(2/3)}_{X_K}(\ell_2)$.

context_brief: New operator ideals with nonzero traces.
original_question: Find operator ideals, different from the classes already discussed earlier in the paper, that support non-vanishing traces.
self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is an assignment, to every pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$, of a linear subspace $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)\subseteq \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) all finite-rank operators belong to $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, and
(ii) if $T\in\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, $A\in\mathcal{L}(Y_0,X)$, $B\in\mathcal{L}(Y,X_0)$, then $BTA\in\mathcal{A}(Y_0,X_0)$.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X:\mathcal{A}(X,X)\to\mathbb{C}$ (one for each Banach space $X$) which is
(a) tracial: $\tau_Y(ST)=\tau_X(TS)$ whenever $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, $S\in\mathcal{A}(Y,X)$ (so that $TS\in\mathcal{A}(X,X)$ and $ST\in\mathcal{A}(Y,Y)$),
(b) normalized on rank-one operators: $\tau_X(x'\otimes x)=\langle x,x'\rangle$ for $x\in X$, $x'\in X^*$.
The trace is called non-vanishing (nonzero) if $\tau_X\not\equiv 0$ for some $X$.

Known examples of operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces that admit nonzero traces include the ideal of nuclear operators (on spaces with the approximation property, where the nuclear trace is well-defined and nonzero), the ideal of $2$-summing (and more generally absolutely $p$-summing) operators in suitable settings, ideals defined via approximation numbers / entropy numbers / eigenvalue sequences in appropriate Lorentz-type scales, and certain ideals constructed via dyadic decomposition methods on Banach spaces.

Problem. Exhibit an operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ on the class of all Banach spaces, distinct from the classical examples listed above, that supports a nonzero (continuous) trace. Equivalently, construct new operator ideals over Banach spaces together with a non-vanishing trace functional, or prove that every operator ideal over the class of all Banach spaces admitting a nonzero trace falls within the already-known families.
category_tag: Traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces
status_search_result: The problem is part of Pietsch's collection of open problems on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces. Surveys and follow-up work (e.g., Pietsch's series on traces and related linear forms on sequence ideals, and Oberwolfach reports on s-numbers and operator ideals) describe these as problems Pietsch was unable to solve, and no resolution providing genuinely new ideals with nonzero traces beyond the known families appears in the literature.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
context_brief: Distinguish two equivalent quasi-norms on L^{APP}_z.
original_question: Find a shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) and an operator S in L^{APP}_z(X,Y) for some Banach spaces X,Y such that the two equivalent quasi-norms on L^{APP}_z introduced in Theorem 1.4, namely ||S|L^{APP}_z|| based on the dyadic approximation numbers and |||S|L^{APP}_z||| based on z-representations, are not actually equal on that operator.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ that is solid (if $|a_n|\le|b_n|$ for all $n$ and $(b_n)\in z$, then $(a_n)\in z$) and equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\,|z\|$ making it a quasi-Banach sequence space in which the unit vectors $e_n$ are bounded. Such a sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if the dyadic block-shift operators are bounded, i.e. there is a constant $c\ge 1$ such that for every $(\xi_n)\in z$ one has $\|(\xi_{2n})|z\|\le c\,\|(\xi_n)|z\|$ and $\|(\xi_{n})|z\|\le c\,\|(\xi_{n/2})|z\|$ in the appropriate sense (so that passage between sequences indexed by $n$ and by dyadic blocks $2^k\le n<2^{k+1}$ is bounded).

For Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bounded linear operator $S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, the $n$-th approximation number is 
$$a_n(S)=\inf\{\|S-A\|: A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}\,A<n\},\qquad n\ge 1,$$
and the dyadic approximation numbers are $a^{(d)}_k(S)=a_{2^k}(S)$ for $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$.

Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the approximation operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ as the class of operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ such that the dyadic approximation sequence $(a^{(d)}_k(S))_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, with quasi-norm
$$\|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|:=\bigl\|(a^{(d)}_k(S))_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\big|\,z\bigr\|.$$

A $z$-representation of $S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ is a series representation $S=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} S_k$ converging in operator norm, where each $S_k\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ has finite rank $\mathrm{rank}\,S_k<2^k$, such that the sequence $(\|S_k\|)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. Define
$$|\!|\!|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|\!|\!|:=\inf\bigl\|(\|S_k\|)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\big|\,z\bigr\|,$$
where the infimum is taken over all $z$-representations of $S$. It is known that $\|\cdot\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|$ and $|\!|\!|\cdot\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|\!|\!|$ are equivalent quasi-norms on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$.

Problem. Exhibit a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, Banach spaces $X,Y$, and an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for which the two equivalent quasi-norms above are not equal, i.e.
$$\|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|\ \neq\ |\!|\!|S\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|\!|\!|.$$
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a published list of open problems on traces of operator ideals (zbMATH 7709580). No subsequent resolution was identified in available sources, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Two Open Problems for Absolutely Convergent Dirichlet Series
context_brief: Analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 for S^0(Λ)
original_question: Let S^0(Λ) denote the class of Dirichlet series absolutely convergent in the half-plane {z∈ℂ: Re z<0}. Develop for S^0(Λ) an analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 from the paper. Concretely, determine hypotheses under which one can prove for F∈S^0(Λ) a no-exceptional-set upper estimate of the same kind as the S_ψ(Λ) estimates in Theorem A or Proposition 1, namely bounds comparing M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)| to the maximal term μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n} through expressions such as μ(x,F)h(ln μ(x,F)) or the stronger Proposition 1 type bound μ(x,F)h(xd(x)).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_n<\lambda_{n+1}\to\infty$. For a real number $a$, let $\Pi_a=\{z=\sigma+it\in\mathbb{C}:\sigma<a\}$ and let $S_a(\Lambda)$ denote the class of Dirichlet series 
$$F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n e^{z\lambda_n}$$
which converge absolutely in $\Pi_a$. For such $F$, define the maximum modulus and the maximal term
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|, \qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\ge 0}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}.$$
Let $L$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $\psi$ on $[0,\infty)$ which are nondecreasing to $+\infty$, and let $L_0\subset L$ consist of those $\psi$ for which $\psi(x)/x\to 0$. For $\psi\in L$, set
$$S_\psi(\Lambda)=\{F\in S_0(\Lambda):\ \ln\mu(x,F)\le \psi(x)\ \text{for all sufficiently large } x<0\ \text{(in the appropriate variable)}\}$$
and consider $S^0(\Lambda)$, the class of Dirichlet series of the above form that converge absolutely in the half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} z<0\}$.

Two known results for the classes $S_\psi(\Lambda)$ assert:

(A) Under appropriate growth conditions on $\psi\in L$ and $h\in L_0$ relating $\Lambda$ and $\psi$, one has the equivalence: for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exists $x_0$ such that for all $x\ge x_0$,
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(\ln\mu(x,F)).$$

(B) Under analogous conditions, one has the stronger statement: for every $d\in L_0$ and every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exists $x_0$ such that for all $x\ge x_0$,
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(x\,d(x)).$$

The problem is: formulate and prove an analogue of (A) or (B) for the class $S^0(\Lambda)$. Specifically, identify hypotheses on $\Lambda$ and on auxiliary functions $h$ (and possibly $d$) under which, for every $F\in S^0(\Lambda)$, a no-exceptional-set upper bound of the form
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(\ln\mu(x,F)) \quad\text{or}\quad M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(x\,d(x))$$
holds for all $x$ sufficiently close to $0$ from the left (i.e. as $x\to 0^-$).
status_search_result: A web search for analogues of the Theorem A / Proposition 1 maximum-modulus vs. maximal-term estimates for the class of Dirichlet series absolutely convergent in the left half-plane $\{\operatorname{Re} z<0\}$ did not turn up a definitive resolution. No paper explicitly stating an analogue for $S^0(\Lambda)$ was located, so the current status of the problem is unclear from accessible sources.

paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
original_question: Let G and H be finite simple graphs with at least three vertices. If the multiset of vertex-deleted subgraphs of G is identical to the multiset of vertex-deleted subgraphs of H, must G and H be isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
Let G and H be finite simple graphs, each having at least three vertices. For a graph X with vertex set V(X), define the deck of X to be the multiset D(X) = {{X - v : v ∈ V(X)}}, where X - v denotes the subgraph obtained from X by deleting the vertex v together with all edges incident to v, and where vertex-deleted subgraphs are considered up to isomorphism.

Prove or disprove: if D(G) = D(H) as multisets of isomorphism classes of graphs, then G and H are isomorphic.
status_search_result: This is the Reconstruction Conjecture of Kelly and Ulam (1941/1942), which remains a famous open problem in graph theory. It has been verified for many graph classes (e.g., trees, regular graphs, disconnected graphs, maximal planar graphs) and for all graphs up to 11 vertices, but no proof or counterexample is known in general.
