paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
context_brief: Combinatorics of small tensegrity configuration spaces
original_question: Let B_d(G) = (R^d)^n be the configuration space of realizations P = (p_1, ..., p_n) of a graph G with n labeled vertices in R^d, and stratify B_d(G) by the equivalence classes of the self-stress spaces W(G, P) under sign-preserving homeomorphisms of fibers as in Definitions 1.2 and 1.3. Determine the combinatorial structure of the stratifications of B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5), including the strata of all dimensions and the adjacency relations among those strata.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite graph with vertex set {1, 2, ..., n} and edge set E(G). For an integer d ≥ 1, the configuration space of G in R^d is B_d(G) := (R^d)^n, whose points are realizations P = (p_1, ..., p_n) with p_i ∈ R^d.

For a realization P ∈ B_d(G), a self-stress on (G, P) is an assignment w : E(G) → R of weights w_{ij} to the edges {i,j} ∈ E(G) satisfying the equilibrium condition at every vertex i:
   sum over j with {i,j} ∈ E(G) of w_{ij} (p_j − p_i) = 0.
The set W(G, P) of all self-stresses is a real vector space, called the self-stress space at P.

Define an equivalence relation on B_d(G) as follows. Two realizations P and P' are equivalent if there is a sign-preserving homeomorphism between W(G, P) and W(G, P'); that is, a homeomorphism ϕ : W(G, P) → W(G, P') such that for every edge e ∈ E(G) and every w ∈ W(G, P), the sign of ϕ(w)(e) equals the sign of w(e) (with sign 0 preserved as 0). The equivalence classes form a stratification of B_d(G), and one records both the strata (organized by dimension) and the adjacency relations between strata (which strata lie in the closure of which).

Problem. Describe explicitly the combinatorial structure of these stratifications in the following three cases:
(a) G = K_6 and d = 2 (the complete graph on 6 vertices in the plane);
(b) G = K_4 and d = 3 (the complete graph on 4 vertices in 3-space);
(c) G = K_5 and d = 3 (the complete graph on 5 vertices in 3-space).
For each case, list all strata of every dimension and determine the adjacency relations among them.
status_search_result: The problem of describing the combinatorial stratifications of B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5) is posed as an open problem in the study of tensegrity configuration spaces. Stratifications for B_2(K_n) with small n (n ≤ 5) have been worked out, but the listed three cases remain unstudied; no published resolution of these specific cases was found.

paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
context_brief: Count planar strata types for n points
original_question: In the planar tensegrity setting discussed immediately before Problem 3, compute, for each positive integer n, the number of different strata types that occur for configurations of n labeled points.
self_contained_problem:
Consider configurations of $n$ labeled points $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A (planar) tensegrity on such a configuration is an assignment of real weights ("stresses") $w_{ij} = w_{ji}$ to (a subset of) the pairs $\{i,j\}$ such that the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j \neq i} w_{ij}(p_j - p_i) = 0$$
holds at every point $p_i$. For a fixed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, the set of nonzero self-stresses supported on $G$ for a given configuration forms a real vector space whose dimension depends on the configuration. The configuration space $(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$ is thereby decomposed (stratified) according to the dimensions of these self-stress spaces (equivalently, the rank pattern of the rigidity/stress matrix); each piece of this decomposition is called a stratum, and two strata have the same "type" if they correspond to the same combinatorial/algebraic data of admissible self-stresses.

Problem: For every positive integer $n$, determine the number of distinct types of strata that arise in this stratification of the configuration space of $n$ labeled points in the plane.
status_search_result: The problem appears in Karpenkov's list of open problems on configuration spaces of tensegrities (Arnold Mathematical Journal, 2018). Known results address only small cases: the planar case is fully understood up to n=9, and the case n=10 already contains strata whose classification is open. No general formula or enumeration for arbitrary n is known.

paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
original_question: Identify all strata of codimension greater than 1 in tensegrity configuration spaces that are not obtainable as intersections of closures of codimension-1 strata.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and consider $n$ labeled points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (typically $d=2$). A tensegrity framework on these points with underlying graph $G$ is an assignment of a real "stress" coefficient $w_{ij}$ to each edge $\{i,j\}$ of $G$ such that the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E(G)} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0$$
holds at every vertex $i$. For a fixed graph $G$, the configuration space $\Omega_G$ is the set of point configurations $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ that admit a nonzero self-stress, and it carries a natural stratification by the dimension of the space of self-stresses (equivalently, by the combinatorial type of the equilibrium condition). The codimension of a stratum is its codimension inside the ambient configuration space.

A stratum $S$ of codimension greater than $1$ is said to be "obtainable from codimension-$1$ strata" if there exist codimension-$1$ strata $S_1,\dots,S_k$ such that $S$ is contained in (a component of) the intersection of their closures $\overline{S_1}\cap\cdots\cap\overline{S_k}$, and equals such an intersection set-theoretically.

Problem: Identify and classify all strata of $\Omega_G$ (over all graphs $G$) of codimension strictly greater than $1$ that cannot be obtained as set-theoretic intersections of closures of codimension-$1$ strata.
status_search_result: Web search confirms this is listed among the open problems on configuration spaces of tensegrities (Arnold Mathematical Journal). No solution or partial classification of higher-codimension exceptional strata appears in subsequent literature; related progress concerns codimension-1 strata for small n and Cayley algebra descriptions, not the higher-codimension question.

paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
context_brief: Cayley description of planar codimension-1 strata
original_question: For a given graph G in the plane, does there exist a Cayley algebra system, or finitely many such systems, whose solution set is exactly the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the planar configuration space B_2(G)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph with $n=|V|$ vertices. A planar configuration of $G$ is a map $p\colon V\to\mathbb{R}^2$ assigning to each vertex $v_i$ a point $p_i\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Identify the configuration space of $G$ in the plane with $B_2(G)=(\mathbb{R}^2)^V$ (or, equivalently, with the configuration space of the complete graph $B_2(K_n)$ when one ignores the edge structure of $G$).

A self-stress (or equilibrium stress) on $G$ at $p$ is an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$ to the edges $\{v_i,v_j\}\in E$ such that, for every vertex $v_i$,
$$\sum_{j:\,\{v_i,v_j\}\in E} w_{ij}\,(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
A tensegrity is a configuration $p$ together with a self-stress $w$ in which the signs of the weights are prescribed (cables, struts, bars). The tensegrity stratification of $B_2(G)$ is the partition of the configuration space according to the sign pattern (and the dimension of the space) of self-stresses supported on $G$ at $p$. Each stratum is a semi-algebraic subset of $B_2(G)$, and one defines the codimension-$1$ strata in the usual way (those of codimension exactly $1$ in $B_2(G)$).

The (planar) Cayley algebra is the algebraic system whose elements are points and lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with two partial operations: the join $\vee$ which sends a pair of points to the line through them, and the meet $\wedge$ which sends a pair of lines to their intersection point. A Cayley algebra system is a finite system of equalities/incidence conditions built from variable points (the $p_i$) and from terms obtained by iterated application of $\vee$ and $\wedge$; its solution set is the locus in $B_2(G)$ of configurations $p$ satisfying all conditions of the system. A finite collection of Cayley algebra systems is said to describe a subset $S\subseteq B_2(G)$ if $S$ equals the union of the solution sets of these systems.

Problem. For an arbitrary finite graph $G$, does there exist a Cayley algebra system, or a finite collection of Cayley algebra systems, whose union of solution sets coincides exactly with the union of all codimension-$1$ tensegrity strata in the planar configuration space $B_2(G)$?
status_search_result: The problem is stated as a long-standing open problem about Cayley-style descriptions of codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane. A weaker version (using an extended Cayley algebra with extra auxiliary elements) has been resolved, but the original question remains open, and there is a known candidate graph that may serve as a counterexample.

paper_title: Trois problèmes (ouverts) de courbes optimales
original_question: Let K be the four sides of a square of side length ℓ. Determine a curve or barrier C of minimal total length, contained inside the square, with the property that every straight line that meets K also meets C.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be the closed unit square in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with side length $\ell>0$, and let $K=\partial S$ denote its boundary (the union of its four sides). A subset $C\subseteq S$ is called an opaque barrier for $S$ if every straight line in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that intersects $K$ also intersects $C$. For a sufficiently regular set $C$ (for example, a finite union of rectifiable curves), let $\mathcal{L}(C)$ denote its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (total length).

Determine
$$ m(\ell) \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\,\mathcal{L}(C)\;:\; C\subseteq S\text{ is an opaque barrier for }S\,\bigr\}, $$
and exhibit a curve (or finite system of curves) $C^\star\subseteq S$ that attains this infimum, or prove that no minimizer exists. In particular, decide whether the configuration consisting of the Steiner minimal tree of three vertices of the square together with the segment joining the fourth vertex to the center—of total length $\sqrt{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,\ell$ when $\ell=1$—is optimal.
status_search_result: The opaque square problem remains open. The best known upper bound for a (possibly disconnected) opaque barrier of the unit square is approximately 2.6389, achieved by the Steiner tree of three vertices together with a segment joining the fourth vertex to the center; the best general lower bound is 2 (Jones, ca. 1970s). It is unknown whether the upper-bound construction is optimal.

paper_title: Trois problèmes (ouverts) de courbes optimales
original_question: In the opaque-square barrier problem, if the barrier C is allowed to have n connected components instead of only one or two pieces, can one improve on the current best known length (2 + √3)/√2 · ℓ ≈ 2.639 · ℓ? Equivalently, does allowing arbitrarily many components keep lowering the achievable length so that the problem might have an infimum but no minimizing barrier?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be the closed unit square in the Euclidean plane, with side length $\ell>0$ (take $\ell=1$ for normalization). A subset $C\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is called an opaque barrier (or opaque set) for $S$ if $C$ is a finite union of rectifiable curves and every straight line in the plane that meets $S$ also meets $C$. The length $|C|$ is the sum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of its components.

For an integer $n\ge 1$, let
$$L_n \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\,|C|\;:\; C \text{ is an opaque barrier for } S \text{ consisting of at most } n \text{ connected components}\bigr\}.$$
The shortest known opaque barrier (using two components: the Steiner tree of three vertices of $S$ together with a segment from the fourth vertex to the center) has length
$$\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\ell \;=\;\bigl(\sqrt{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\bigr)\ell \;\approx\; 2.6389\,\ell.$$

Questions:
(a) Does there exist an integer $n\ge 3$ and an opaque barrier for $S$ with at most $n$ connected components whose total length is strictly less than $\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\ell$?
(b) Is the sequence $(L_n)_{n\ge 1}$ strictly decreasing for all sufficiently large $n$, so that
$$L_\infty := \inf_{n\ge 1} L_n \;<\; L_n \quad\text{for every }n,$$
i.e., the infimum length over opaque barriers with finitely many components is not attained by any single barrier with a bounded number of components?
status_search_result: The opaque square problem remains open. The shortest known barrier for the unit square has length √2 + √6/2 ≈ 2.6389, known to be optimal only among barriers with at most two components; whether allowing more components yields shorter barriers is unresolved. The best general lower bound was recently improved from 2 (Jones, 1964) to roughly 2.00002, and no proof is known that a minimizer exists or that the conjectured value is optimal.

paper_title: Trois problèmes (ouverts) de courbes optimales
original_question: Among all connected one-dimensional armatures Γ of prescribed total length L in three-dimensional space, maximize the volume of the convex hull of Γ. The best candidate reported in the article is a helical arc (the Nudel'man curve), and the open question is whether that helical armature is in fact an optimal solution to the 3D problem in full generality.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a connected one-dimensional rectifiable set (an "armature"; e.g., a finite connected union of rectifiable arcs) of prescribed total one-dimensional length $\mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma) = L > 0$. Let $\operatorname{conv}(\Gamma)$ denote its convex hull and $\operatorname{vol}_3$ the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Consider the optimization problem
$$ V(L) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\,\operatorname{vol}_3(\operatorname{conv}(\Gamma)) : \Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \text{ connected, } \mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma)=L\,\bigr\}. $$
A candidate extremal armature is the helical arc $\Gamma^*$ (Nudel'man curve) given parametrically (up to scaling so that its length equals $L$) by
$$ x(t) = \cos t,\quad y(t)=\sin t,\quad z(t) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,t, \qquad t \in [0, 2\pi]. $$
Prove or disprove: this helical arc $\Gamma^*$ attains the supremum $V(L)$, i.e., it is a global maximizer of the convex-hull volume among all connected one-dimensional armatures of total length $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

paper_title: Trois problèmes (ouverts) de courbes optimales
original_question: What is the minimal possible length of a space curve that is visible from every point of a given sphere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the unit sphere, viewed as an opaque body: a point $p \in S$ "sees" a point $q \in \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B)$ (where $B$ is the closed unit ball bounded by $S$) if the open line segment from $p$ to $q$ does not intersect the interior of $B$. Equivalently, $q$ is visible from $p$ if and only if $q$ lies in the closed half-space $H_p = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \langle x - p, p\rangle \ge 0\}$ tangent to $S$ at $p$.

A rectifiable curve $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B)$ (not assumed closed and not assumed connected to anything) is said to be visible from every point of the sphere if for every $p \in S$ there exists a point $q \in \gamma$ with $q \in H_p$, i.e. $\gamma \cap H_p \neq \emptyset$.

Determine
$$
L^* \;=\; \inf \bigl\{\, \mathrm{length}(\gamma) \;:\; \gamma \text{ is a rectifiable curve in } \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B) \text{ visible from every point of } S \,\bigr\},
$$
and exhibit (or characterize) a curve attaining this infimum, if one exists.
status_search_result: For closed inspection curves the analogous problem was settled by Ghomi and Wenk (Crelle 2021), who proved that any closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose convex hull contains the unit sphere has length at least $4\pi$, with equality for a baseball-seam-shaped union of four semicircles (Zalgaller's conjecture). The version for arbitrary (not necessarily closed) space curves visible from every point of the sphere does not appear to be resolved in this literature; no published proof of an exact minimum or characterization of an extremal curve for the open-curve variant was found.

paper_title: The Projection Technique for Two Open Problems of Unconstrained Optimization Problems
context_brief: BFGS global convergence under weak Wolfe-Powell search
original_question: For unconstrained optimization of a twice continuously differentiable nonconvex function f: R^n -> R, does the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno quasi-Newton method admit a globally convergent variant under the weak Wolfe-Powell line search? More specifically, can one obtain global convergence for nonconvex objectives in that weak Wolfe-Powell setting even though standard BFGS is known to fail in relevant counterexamples?
self_contained_problem:
Let f: R^n -> R be twice continuously differentiable and bounded below, with gradient g = ∇f assumed to be Lipschitz continuous on the level set of the starting point. Consider the quasi-Newton iteration

  x_{k+1} = x_k + α_k d_k,   d_k = -B_k^{-1} g(x_k),

where {B_k} is updated by the Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (BFGS) formula

  B_{k+1} = B_k - (B_k s_k s_k^T B_k)/(s_k^T B_k s_k) + (y_k y_k^T)/(y_k^T s_k),

with s_k = x_{k+1} - x_k and y_k = g(x_{k+1}) - g(x_k), and where the step size α_k > 0 is chosen by the weak Wolfe–Powell (WWP) line search: there exist constants 0 < δ < σ < 1 such that

  f(x_k + α_k d_k) ≤ f(x_k) + δ α_k g(x_k)^T d_k,
  g(x_k + α_k d_k)^T d_k ≥ σ g(x_k)^T d_k.

It is known that for general nonconvex f the standard BFGS method under the WWP line search may fail to converge (counterexamples are known).

Question: Does there exist a variant of the BFGS quasi-Newton method (for instance, using a projection-type modification of the iterates and/or a modification of the WWP line search and/or the update formula) that, under standard regularity assumptions on f (twice continuous differentiability, lower boundedness, Lipschitz continuous gradient) but without assuming convexity, satisfies the global convergence property

  liminf_{k → ∞} ‖g(x_k)‖ = 0   (or, stronger, lim_{k → ∞} ‖g(x_k)‖ = 0)?
status_search_result: Several recent works construct modified BFGS variants (using projection techniques and/or modified weak Wolfe–Powell line searches) that are globally convergent for nonconvex functions, thereby giving an affirmative answer in the "modified-variant" sense. However, the global convergence of the classical (unmodified) BFGS method with a standard Wolfe line search for general nonconvex functions remains an open problem, with known counterexamples (Dai; Mascarenhas) showing that standard BFGS can fail.

original_question: For the projection framework introduced in this paper for unconstrained optimization, are there projection paraboloids better than the one studied here, in the sense of being worth further theoretical or algorithmic investigation?

$$P_f = \{(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R} : t \geq \|x\|^2 + (f(x) - m)\},$$

where $\phi:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a strictly convex quadratic ("paraboloid") auxiliary function. The minimization of $f$ is then reformulated as a projection problem onto $S_\phi$ (or onto $P_f$) from a suitably chosen point in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$.

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of microwave heating
context_brief: Uniqueness for the full Maxwell-heat system
original_question: For the full nonlinear microwave-heating problem coupling Maxwell's equations with the heat equation, where both the electrical conductivity σ(θ) and the thermal absorptivity q(θ) depend on the temperature, does the existence theory obtained by the Galerkin method together with the Schauder fixed point theorem actually give a unique solution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the full nonlinear microwave-heating model in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ³ with smooth boundary, on a time interval (0,T). The unknowns are the electric field E(x,t), the magnetic field H(x,t), and the temperature θ(x,t), satisfying Maxwell's equations coupled with the heat equation:

  ε ∂E/∂t − ∇ × H + σ(θ) E = 0   in Ω × (0,T),
  μ ∂H/∂t + ∇ × E = 0           in Ω × (0,T),
  ρ c ∂θ/∂t − ∇·(k ∇θ) = q(θ) σ(θ) |E|²   in Ω × (0,T),

together with standard initial conditions E(·,0)=E₀, H(·,0)=H₀, θ(·,0)=θ₀, the perfect-conductor boundary condition E × n = 0 on ∂Ω × (0,T), and a boundary condition for θ (e.g. θ = θ_b or k ∂θ/∂n + h(θ−θ_b) = 0) on ∂Ω × (0,T). Here ε, μ, ρ, c, k > 0 are given constants (or smooth positive functions), and the electrical conductivity σ : ℝ → (0,∞) and the thermal absorptivity q : ℝ → (0,∞) are given continuous, bounded, positive functions of the temperature θ.

Existence of a weak solution (E, H, θ) to this coupled system can be obtained via a Galerkin approximation combined with the Schauder fixed point theorem. The question is:

Under these hypotheses on σ(θ) and q(θ) (both genuinely temperature-dependent, with no monotonicity or smallness assumption beyond continuity and positive bounds), is the weak solution (E, H, θ) of the coupled Maxwell–heat system unique?
status_search_result: Existence of weak/global solutions for Maxwell's equations coupled with the heat equation under temperature-dependent electrical conductivity (and related variants with temperature-dependent permittivity) has been established in several works (e.g., Yin's results on Maxwell's equations in an electromagnetic field with temperature effect, and the coupled heat–Maxwell system with temperature-dependent permittivity). Uniqueness has been proved only under additional structural assumptions, such as suitable decay/regularity of σ(θ) and Hölder continuity of θ; for the full nonlinear system with both σ(θ) and q(θ) depending on θ under only general continuity/boundedness hypotheses, uniqueness does not appear to be established in full generality.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
original_question: Let S be a semitopological semigroup. Consider the fixed point property (fpp*) saying that whenever S = {T_s : s in S} is represented by norm nonexpansive mappings on a nonempty weak* compact convex subset C of the dual E* of a Banach space E, and the action map (s, x) -> T_s(x) from S x C to C is jointly continuous when C carries the weak* topology, then C contains a common fixed point for S. If LUC(S), the space of left uniformly continuous bounded functions on S, has a left invariant mean, must S have property (fpp*)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semitopological semigroup (a semigroup endowed with a Hausdorff topology such that for each $s\in S$ the maps $t\mapsto st$ and $t\mapsto ts$ are continuous on $S$). Let $\mathrm{CB}(S)$ denote the space of bounded continuous real-valued functions on $S$ with the supremum norm, and for $s\in S$ and $f\in \mathrm{CB}(S)$ define $(\ell_s f)(t)=f(st)$. The space $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ of left uniformly continuous bounded functions on $S$ consists of all $f\in \mathrm{CB}(S)$ for which the map $s\mapsto \ell_s f$ from $S$ into $\mathrm{CB}(S)$ is norm continuous. A left invariant mean (LIM) on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ is a continuous linear functional $m$ on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ with $m(1)=\|m\|=1$ such that $m(\ell_s f)=m(f)$ for every $s\in S$ and every $f\in \mathrm{LUC}(S)$.

Say that $S$ has the fixed point property $(\mathrm{fpp}^*)$ if the following holds: whenever $E$ is a Banach space, $C$ is a nonempty weak$^*$-compact convex subset of the dual space $E^*$, and $\mathcal{S}=\{T_s:s\in S\}$ is a representation of $S$ as norm-nonexpansive self-mappings of $C$ (i.e., $T_{st}=T_s\circ T_t$ for all $s,t\in S$ and $\|T_s x-T_s y\|\le \|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in C$, $s\in S$) such that the action map $(s,x)\mapsto T_s(x)$ from $S\times C$ to $C$ is jointly continuous when $C$ carries the weak$^*$ topology, then there exists $x_0\in C$ with $T_s x_0=x_0$ for every $s\in S$.

Question: Does every semitopological semigroup $S$ for which $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ admits a left invariant mean necessarily have property $(\mathrm{fpp}^*)$?
status_search_result: The implication is posed as an open problem in the literature on fixed point properties for semigroups of nonexpansive mappings on weak*-compact convex sets. Related results are known (e.g., for AP(S), WAP(S), and partial converses), but a search did not turn up a published proof or counterexample resolving this specific implication for general semitopological semigroups.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
original_question: Let A be an F-algebra. If A is left amenable, so that A has topological left invariant means on its dual M = A*, under what conditions is the vector space spanned by the set of topological left invariant means on A finite dimensional?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $A$ be an F-algebra in the following sense: $A$ is a Banach algebra that is the unique predual of a $W^*$-algebra $M$, so that $M = A^*$, and the identity $1$ of $M$ is a multiplicative linear functional on $A$. Define
$$P(A) = \{\varphi \in A : \|\varphi\| = \langle 1, \varphi\rangle = 1\}.$$
For $\varphi \in A$ and $f \in M$, define $\varphi \cdot f \in M$ by $\langle \psi, \varphi \cdot f\rangle = \langle \psi\varphi, f\rangle$ for all $\psi \in A$.

A topological left invariant mean (TLIM) on $A$ is an element $m \in M^*$ with $\|m\| = 1$ such that
$$\langle m, \varphi \cdot f\rangle = \langle m, f\rangle \quad \text{for all } f \in M \text{ and all } \varphi \in P(A).$$
The algebra $A$ is called left amenable if there exists at least one TLIM on $A$. Let $\mathrm{TLIM}(A) \subseteq M^*$ denote the (convex) set of all TLIMs on $A$.

Problem. Suppose $A$ is a left amenable F-algebra. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $A$ under which the linear span of $\mathrm{TLIM}(A)$ in $M^*$ is finite dimensional.
status_search_result: Classical results by Granirer characterize finite dimensionality of the span of (topological) left invariant means for amenable semigroups and locally compact groups in terms of finiteness/structural conditions, but a corresponding general characterization for arbitrary left amenable F-algebras (in the sense of Lau) does not appear to be available in the literature. The problem is posed as an open problem and recent surveys on fixed-point properties for F-algebras do not report a complete solution.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
context_brief: ELA semigroups and weak fixed points in Banach spaces
original_question: Let S be an extremely left amenable semitopological semigroup, and let C be a weakly closed subset of a Banach space E. Suppose S acts on C by a weakly continuous norm nonexpansive representation {T_s : s in S}, and for some c in C the orbit {T_s c : s in S} is relatively weakly compact. Must C contain a common fixed point for S?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $S$ be a semitopological semigroup, i.e. a semigroup endowed with a Hausdorff topology such that for each $s\in S$ the maps $t\mapsto st$ and $t\mapsto ts$ are continuous. Let $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ denote the space of bounded left uniformly continuous complex-valued functions on $S$ (those bounded continuous $f:S\to\mathbb{C}$ for which the map $s\mapsto \ell_s f$ is norm-continuous, where $(\ell_s f)(t)=f(st)$). A mean on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ is a continuous linear functional $m$ with $m(1)=1$ and $\|m\|=1$; it is left invariant if $m(\ell_s f)=m(f)$ for all $s\in S$ and $f\in\mathrm{LUC}(S)$, and multiplicative if $m(fg)=m(f)m(g)$. The semigroup $S$ is called extremely left amenable (ELA) if there exists a left invariant mean on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ that is also multiplicative.

Let $E$ be a Banach space and $C\subseteq E$ a weakly closed subset. A representation $\{T_s:s\in S\}$ of $S$ on $C$ is a family of maps $T_s:C\to C$ with $T_{st}=T_s\circ T_t$ for all $s,t\in S$. The representation is called:
- norm nonexpansive if $\|T_s x-T_s y\|\le\|x-y\|$ for all $s\in S$ and $x,y\in C$;
- weakly continuous if the map $(s,x)\mapsto T_s x$ from $S\times C$ to $C$ is jointly continuous when $C$ carries the weak topology of $E$.

Question. Suppose $S$ is an extremely left amenable semitopological semigroup, $C$ is a weakly closed subset of a Banach space $E$, and $\{T_s:s\in S\}$ is a weakly continuous, norm nonexpansive representation of $S$ on $C$. Assume that for some $c\in C$ the orbit $\{T_s c:s\in S\}$ is relatively weakly compact in $E$. Must $C$ contain a common fixed point of $S$, i.e., a point $x\in C$ with $T_s x=x$ for every $s\in S$?

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
original_question: Let A be an F-algebra. Property (F_n) says that for every separated locally convex vector space E and every linear representation of S = P_1(A) on E that is jointly continuous on compact subsets, if X is an n-consistent subset of E and there exists a closed S-invariant subspace H of codimension n such that (x + H) intersect X is compact for each x in E, then there exists an n-dimensional subspace L_0 contained in X with T_s(L_0) = L_0 for all s in S. Let (F' _n) be the same property with joint continuity on compact sets weakened to separate continuity on compact sets. Does (F_n) imply (F' _n)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $F$-algebra (a Banach algebra whose dual $A^*$ has a distinguished left-introverted weak*-closed subspace, with predual interpretation as in the theory of Lau algebras), and let $S = P_1(A) = \{a \in A : a \geq 0,\ \|a\| = 1\}$ be the set of normalized positive elements, regarded as a semigroup under multiplication.

For a separated locally convex topological vector space $E$, a linear representation of $S$ on $E$ is a family $\mathcal{T} = \{T_s : s \in S\}$ of continuous linear operators $T_s : E 	o E$ satisfying $T_{st} = T_s T_t$ for all $s,t \in S$. Such a representation is called:
  • jointly continuous on compact subsets if for every compact $K \subset E$, the map $(s,x) \mapsto T_s x$ from $S 	imes K$ to $E$ is jointly continuous;
  • separately continuous on compact subsets if for every compact $K \subset E$ and every $s \in S$, $T_s|_K$ is continuous, and for every $x \in K$ the map $s \mapsto T_s x$ is continuous.

Given a positive integer $n$, a subset $X \subseteq E$ is called $n$-consistent with respect to $\mathcal{T}$ if it is nonempty, $\mathcal{T}$-invariant (i.e.\ $T_s(X) \subseteq X$ for all $s \in S$), and every $n$-dimensional affine subspace contained in $X$ behaves consistently under $\mathcal{T}$ in the sense required to define $\mathcal{L}_n(X) := \{L \subseteq X : L	ext{ is an } n	ext{-dimensional affine subspace contained in } X\}$.

Property $(F_n)$: For every separated locally convex space $E$ and every linear representation $\mathcal{T}$ of $S$ on $E$ that is jointly continuous on compact subsets, if $X \subseteq E$ is $n$-consistent with respect to $\mathcal{T}$ and there exists a closed $\mathcal{T}$-invariant subspace $H \subseteq E$ of codimension $n$ such that $(x + H) \cap X$ is compact for every $x \in E$, then there exists $L_0 \in \mathcal{L}_n(X)$ with $T_s(L_0) = L_0$ for all $s \in S$.

Property $(F'_n)$: The same statement as $(F_n)$ but with "jointly continuous on compact subsets" replaced by "separately continuous on compact subsets".

Question: Does property $(F_n)$ imply property $(F'_n)$ for every $F$-algebra $A$ and every positive integer $n$?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this implication problem was located. It appears as an open problem in the literature on fixed point properties for F-algebras, and no follow-up announcement of a proof or counterexample was found.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
original_question: Let A be an F-algebra. Let WAP(A) denote the weakly almost periodic functionals on A, and let (F^W_n) be the same invariant-subspace property as (F^A_n) except that equicontinuity on compact subsets is weakened to quasi-equicontinuity on compact subsets. If WAP(A) has a topological left invariant mean, does A satisfy (F^W_n) for every integer n >= 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $F$-algebra, that is, a Banach algebra which is the (unique) predual of a $W^*$-algebra $M$ such that the identity of $M$ is a multiplicative linear functional on $A$. Let $\mathrm{WAP}(A)$ denote the space of weakly almost periodic functionals on $A$, i.e., those $f \in A^*$ such that the map $a \mapsto a\cdot f$ from $A$ into $A^*$ is weakly compact. A topological left invariant mean (TLIM) on $\mathrm{WAP}(A)$ is a state $m \in \mathrm{WAP}(A)^*$ satisfying $m(a\cdot f) = \langle a,1\rangle\, m(f)$ for all $a \in A$ and $f \in \mathrm{WAP}(A)$.

For an integer $n \ge 1$, say that $A$ satisfies the property $(F^W_n)$ if the following holds: whenever $E$ is a separated locally convex space, $K$ is a non-empty compact convex subset of $E^n$, and $A$ acts on $K$ by an affine, jointly continuous, quasi-equicontinuous (on compact subsets of $E^n$) representation that is the natural diagonal action of an affine action on a compact convex subset of $E$, then $K$ contains a common fixed point of $A$. (Here "quasi-equicontinuous on compact subsets" replaces the stronger "equicontinuous on compact subsets" used in the analogous property $(F^A_n)$.)

Question: If $\mathrm{WAP}(A)$ admits a topological left invariant mean, does $A$ necessarily satisfy $(F^W_n)$ for every integer $n \ge 1$?

Web searches did not surface any subsequent paper resolving the converse implication between existence of a TLIM on WAP(A) and the fixed point property $(F^W_n)$, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
original_question: Let S be a semitopological semigroup such that AP(S) has a left invariant mean. Does S have the fixed point property (fpp*n): whenever K is a nonempty weak* compact convex subset of a dual Banach space with normal structure, every norm nonexpansive and separately weak* continuous representation of S on K has a common fixed point in K?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions and setup. Let $S$ be a semitopological semigroup, i.e., a semigroup equipped with a Hausdorff topology such that for every $a\in S$ the left and right translation maps $s\mapsto a\cdot s$ and $s\mapsto s\cdot a$ are continuous from $S$ to $S$. Let $CB(S)$ denote the Banach space of bounded continuous real-valued functions on $S$ with the supremum norm, and for $a\in S$ define the left translation operator $\ell_a$ on $CB(S)$ by $(\ell_a f)(s)=f(as)$. A function $f\in CB(S)$ is called almost periodic if the orbit $\{\ell_a f : a\in S\}$ is relatively compact in the norm topology of $CB(S)$; let $AP(S)\subseteq CB(S)$ be the closed subspace of all almost periodic functions. A mean on $AP(S)$ is a continuous linear functional $m:AP(S)\to\mathbb{R}$ with $m(\mathbf{1})=\|m\|=1$, and $m$ is called a left invariant mean (LIM) if $m(\ell_a f)=m(f)$ for all $a\in S$ and $f\in AP(S)$.

Let $E$ be a Banach space that is the dual of some Banach space $E_*$, and let $K\subseteq E$ be a nonempty weak* compact convex subset. We say $K$ has normal structure if every nontrivial weak* compact convex subset $C\subseteq K$ contains a point $x_0\in C$ with $\sup\{\|x_0-y\|: y\in C\}<\operatorname{diam}(C)$. A representation of $S$ on $K$ is a family $\{T_s\}_{s\in S}$ of mappings $T_s:K\to K$ such that $T_{st}=T_s\circ T_t$ for all $s,t\in S$. The representation is called norm nonexpansive if $\|T_s x-T_s y\|\le\|x-y\|$ for all $s\in S$, $x,y\in K$, and separately weak* continuous if for each fixed $s\in S$ the map $T_s$ is weak*-to-weak* continuous on $K$, and for each fixed $x\in K$ the map $s\mapsto T_s x$ is weak* continuous from $S$ to $K$.

The semigroup $S$ is said to have property (fpp*n) if: for every dual Banach space $E$, every nonempty weak* compact convex subset $K\subseteq E$ with normal structure, and every norm nonexpansive separately weak* continuous representation $\{T_s\}_{s\in S}$ of $S$ on $K$, there exists a common fixed point $x\in K$ with $T_s x=x$ for all $s\in S$.

Question. Suppose $S$ is a semitopological semigroup such that $AP(S)$ has a left invariant mean. Does $S$ necessarily have the fixed point property (fpp*n)?
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a survey of open questions on fixed point properties for semitopological semigroups. Searches did not turn up a published resolution; related work establishes (fpp*n) for left reversible semigroups and gives partial results under stronger invariance conditions, but the implication "AP(S) has a LIM ⇒ (fpp*n)" does not appear to have been settled.

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
context_brief: regularity of controls in exact controllability
original_question: Consider the refined stochastic wave-like control system in which dy = ȳ dt + (a4 y + f) dW in Q, d ȳ - Σ_{j,k}(a_jk y_{x_j})_{x_k} dt = (a1·∇y + a2 y + a5 g) dt + (a3 y + g) dW in Q, y = χ_{Γ0} h on the boundary, and the controls are f, g, and h. Exact controllability is known for this model when the diffusion control g belongs to L²_F(0,T;H^{-1}(G)). The open question is whether exact controllability still holds when g is required only to lie in L²_F(0,T;L²(G)), equivalently whether one can prove the corresponding adjoint observability estimate using the boundary observation ∂z/∂ν on Γ0 together with the interior terms a5 z + Z and O^Z in L²(G).
self_contained_problem:
Let $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\Gamma=\partial G$, let $\Gamma_0\subset\Gamma$ be a nonempty relatively open subset, fix $T>0$, and set $Q=(0,T)\times G$. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\ge 0},\mathbb{P})$ be a complete filtered probability space carrying a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion $W$, and let $L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;X)$ denote the Hilbert space of $\{\mathcal F_t\}$-adapted processes with values in a Hilbert space $X$ that are square integrable in $(t,\omega)$.

Assume $(a_{jk})_{1\le j,k\le n}$ is a symmetric, uniformly positive definite matrix of $C^2(\overline G)$-functions, and let
$$a_1\in L^\infty_{\mathcal F}(0,T;W^{1,\infty}(G;\mathbb R^n)),\qquad a_2,a_3,a_4,a_5\in L^\infty_{\mathcal F}(0,T;L^\infty(G)).$$
Consider the controlled stochastic wave-like system
$$\begin{cases}
 dy=\bar y\,dt+(a_4 y+f)\,dW & \text{in }Q,\\[2pt]
 d\bar y-\sum_{j,k=1}^n(a_{jk}y_{x_j})_{x_k}\,dt=(a_1\!\cdot\!\nabla y+a_2 y+a_5 g)\,dt+(a_3 y+g)\,dW & \text{in }Q,\\[2pt]
 y=\chi_{\Gamma_0} h & \text{on }(0,T)\times\Gamma,\\[2pt]
 (y(0),\bar y(0))=(y_0,\bar y_0) & \text{in }G,
\end{cases}$$
where the unknowns are $(y,\bar y)$ and the controls are $f,g,h$, with prescribed regularities $f\in L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;L^2(G))$, $h\in L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;L^2(\Gamma_0))$.

The system is called exactly controllable at time $T$ if for every initial datum $(y_0,\bar y_0)\in L^2(G)\times H^{-1}(G)$ and every $\mathcal F_T$-measurable target $(y_1,\bar y_1)\in L^2_{\mathcal F_T}(\Omega;L^2(G)\times H^{-1}(G))$ there exist controls $(f,g,h)$ in the admissible classes for which the corresponding solution satisfies $(y(T),\bar y(T))=(y_1,\bar y_1)$ a.s.

It is known that exact controllability holds when $g$ is allowed to range over $L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;H^{-1}(G))$. The question is:

Does exact controllability of the above system at some $T>0$ still hold under the strictly stronger requirement
$$g\in L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;L^2(G))\,?$$

Equivalently (by duality), does there exist $C>0$ such that every solution $(z,Z,O^Z)$ of the corresponding backward adjoint stochastic hyperbolic system satisfies the observability estimate
$$\|(z(0),Z(0))\|_{H^1_0(G)\times L^2(G)}^2\;\le\;C\,\mathbb E\!\int_0^T\!\!\int_{\Gamma_0}\!\Big|\tfrac{\partial z}{\partial\nu}\Big|^2 d\Gamma\,dt\;+\;C\,\mathbb E\!\int_0^T\!\!\int_G\big(|a_5 z+Z|^2+|O^Z|^2\big)dx\,dt,$$
where $\nu$ denotes the conormal direction associated with $(a_{jk})$?
status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., on a refined stochastic wave equation, 2023, and a refined stochastic hyperbolic equation with internal controls, 2025) extend exact-controllability results, but none located explicitly resolves whether the boundary-controlled refined stochastic hyperbolic system remains exactly controllable when the diffusion control $g$ is upgraded from $L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;H^{-1}(G))$ to $L^2_{\mathcal F}(0,T;L^2(G))$. The status could not be conclusively verified.

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
original_question: For stochastic parabolic equations, and more generally for stochastic distributed parameter systems, can one derive quantitative estimates for the control cost of approximate controllability, analogous to the known deterministic results for heat equations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the stochastic parabolic equation on a bounded smooth domain $G \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with control acting on a nonempty open subset $G_0 \subset G$:
$$
\begin{cases}
dy - \Delta y\,dt = \chi_{G_0} u\,dt + (a y + f) \,dW(t) & \text{in } (0,T) \times G,\\
y = 0 & \text{on } (0,T) \times \partial G,\\
y(0) = y_0 & \text{in } G,
\end{cases}
$$
where $W$ is a standard one-dimensional Brownian motion on a filtered probability space, $a \in L^\infty_{\mathbb F}(0,T;L^\infty(G))$, $y_0 \in L^2(G)$, $u$ is an $\mathbb F$-adapted control in $L^2_{\mathbb F}(0,T;L^2(G_0))$, and $f$ is an admissible $\mathbb F$-adapted source in $L^2_{\mathbb F}(0,T;L^2(G))$.

It is known that this system is approximately controllable: for any target $y_1 \in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_T;L^2(G))$ and any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an admissible control $u$ such that $\mathbb E\,\|y(T) - y_1\|^2_{L^2(G)} \le \varepsilon^2$.

Define the cost of approximate controllability as
$$
K(T,\varepsilon,y_0,y_1) = \inf\bigl\{\|u\|_{L^2_{\mathbb F}(0,T;L^2(G_0))} : \mathbb E\,\|y(T)-y_1\|^2_{L^2(G)} \le \varepsilon^2\bigr\}.
$$

Problem. Establish quantitative upper bounds for $K(T,\varepsilon,y_0,y_1)$ in terms of $T$, $\varepsilon$, $\|y_0\|_{L^2(G)}$, $\|y_1\|_{L^2(\Omega;L^2(G))}$ and the coefficient $a$, in analogy with the known explicit estimates available for the deterministic linear heat equation. More generally, derive analogous quantitative estimates for the cost of approximate controllability of general stochastic distributed parameter systems (including stochastic hyperbolic, Schrödinger, and higher-order equations).
status_search_result: Recent work on stochastic parabolic equations focuses primarily on null controllability and observability via Carleman estimates; quantitative cost estimates for approximate controllability analogous to the deterministic Fernández-Cara–Zuazua results have not been established in full generality. Some progress on related quantities (e.g., cost of null controllability in vanishing viscosity limits, approximate null-controllability with uniform cost for hypoelliptic Ornstein–Uhlenbeck) exists, but the general problem for stochastic parabolic systems and broader SDPSs appears to remain open.

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
original_question: Can one develop a substantially stronger stabilization theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems, in particular proving stabilization results for stochastic hyperbolic equations with localized damping?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\Gamma$, let $T>0$, and let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\ge 0},\mathbb{P})$ be a complete filtered probability space carrying a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion $\{W(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$. Fix an open subset $\omega\subset G$ (the damping region) and a smooth cutoff $a\in C^\infty(\overline{G};[0,\infty))$ with $a(x)>0$ on $\omega$ and $a\equiv 0$ outside a neighborhood of $\omega$. Consider the stochastic hyperbolic equation
$$
\begin{cases}
\, dy_t - \Delta y\,dt + a(x)\,y_t\,dt = b_1(x)\,y\,dW(t) + b_2(x)\,y_t\,dW(t) & \text{in } (0,\infty)\times G,\\
\, y = 0 & \text{on } (0,\infty)\times \Gamma,\\
\, y(0,\cdot)=y_0\in H^1_0(G),\quad y_t(0,\cdot)=y_1\in L^2(G),
\end{cases}
$$
where $b_1,b_2\in L^\infty(G)$ are given and $y_t$ denotes the time derivative (in the Itô sense). Define the energy
$$
E(t) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{E}\!\int_G \bigl(|y_t(t,x)|^2 + |\nabla y(t,x)|^2\bigr)\,dx.
$$
The problem is: identify geometric/multiplier-type conditions on the damping region $\omega$ (e.g.\ a stochastic analogue of the geometric control condition) and admissible coefficients $b_1,b_2$ under which there exist constants $C\ge 1$ and $\alpha>0$ such that
$$
E(t) \;\le\; C\,e^{-\alpha t}\,E(0) \qquad\text{for all } t\ge 0
$$
and all initial data $(y_0,y_1)\in H^1_0(G)\times L^2(G)$. More generally, develop a substantially stronger stabilization theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems that yields such exponential (or otherwise quantitative) decay results for stochastic hyperbolic equations with damping localized to a proper subdomain $\omega\subsetneq G$.
status_search_result: A literature search yields stabilization results for deterministic hyperbolic equations with localized damping (via multiplier methods, Carleman estimates, geometric control condition) and some stabilization results for certain stochastic PDEs, as well as recent work on numerical stabilization of random hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. However, no result establishing exponential stabilization for stochastic hyperbolic equations with truly localized (subdomain) damping in the multiplicative-noise setting was found, consistent with the problem being still open.

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
context_brief: transposition solution for second adjoint equation
original_question: Let (3.7) denote the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation that currently has a unique relaxed transposition solution in the paper. Can one prove that this equation admits a unique transposition solution, not merely a relaxed transposition solution, in a substantially more general setting than the currently known very special case?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $T>0$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb P)$ be a complete filtered probability space on which a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion $\{W(t)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ is defined and generates the filtration. Let $H$ be a separable Hilbert space and let $A:\mathcal D(A)\subset H\to H$ generate a $C_0$-semigroup on $H$. Denote by $\mathcal L(H)$ the space of bounded linear operators on $H$.

Consider, for given operator-valued data $J\in L^\infty_{\mathcal F_T}(\Omega;\mathcal L(H))$ (self-adjoint), $F\in L^1_{\mathbb F}(0,T;\mathcal L(H))$, $K_1,K_2,K_3\in L^2_{\mathbb F}(0,T;\mathcal L(H))$, the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation
$$\begin{cases} dP=-\bigl(A^*P+PA+K_1^*P+PK_1+K_2^*QK_3+K_3^*Q^*K_2+F\bigr)\,dt+Q\,dW(t),\quad t\in[0,T],\\ P(T)=J,\end{cases}\qquad (\star)$$
where the unknown is the pair of $\mathcal L(H)$-valued, $\mathbb F$-adapted processes $(P,Q)$. Such an equation arises as the second-order adjoint equation in Pontryagin-type maximum principles for stochastic evolution equations.

Notions of solution. A pair $(P,Q)$ is called a transposition solution of $(\star)$ if $P$ is a weakly measurable, essentially bounded, $\mathcal L(H)$-valued, $\mathbb F$-adapted process, $Q$ belongs to a suitable space of $\mathcal L(H)$-valued adapted processes, and a variational identity dual to $(\star)$ — tested against pairs of $H$-valued forward Itô processes — holds. A relaxed transposition solution replaces the single process $Q$ by a family of bilinear functionals $\{\hat Q^{(\cdot,\cdot)}\}$ chosen so that the analogous variational identity is satisfied for all admissible test processes. Every transposition solution induces a relaxed transposition solution, but the converse is not known in general. It is known that $(\star)$ admits a unique relaxed transposition solution under broad hypotheses, while existence and uniqueness of a (genuine) transposition solution has been established only in very restrictive special cases.

Problem. Identify a class of generators $A$, coefficients $(K_1,K_2,K_3,F)$, and terminal data $J$ that is substantially broader than the currently known special cases, and prove that within this class the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation $(\star)$ admits a unique transposition solution (not merely a unique relaxed transposition solution).

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
original_question: Outside the trivial situations listed in the survey—such as convex coercive costs on a closed convex control set or convex costs on a closed bounded convex control set—can one prove the existence of optimal controls for stochastic distributed parameter systems, for example via a verification theorem or by proving compactness of minimizing sequences in genuinely nontrivial settings?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\geq 0},\mathbb{P})$ be a complete filtered probability space on which a cylindrical Wiener process $W(\cdot)$ is defined. Let $H$ and $U$ be separable Hilbert spaces, $A:\mathcal{D}(A)\subset H\to H$ the generator of a $C_0$-semigroup, and consider the controlled stochastic evolution equation
$$dy(t)=\bigl(Ay(t)+b(t,y(t),u(t))\bigr)\,dt+\sigma(t,y(t),u(t))\,dW(t),\quad t\in[0,T],\quad y(0)=y_0\in H,$$
where $u(\cdot)$ is an $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}$-progressively measurable process taking values in a nonempty set $\mathcal{U}\subset U$, and $b,\sigma$ are measurable mappings of suitable regularity ensuring well-posedness in a class $\mathcal{Y}$ of mild solutions. Let the cost functional be
$$J(u(\cdot))=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^T f(t,y(t),u(t))\,dt+h(y(T))\right],$$
where $f$ and $h$ are measurable functions, possibly nonconvex in $u$ and not necessarily coercive, and where the control set $\mathcal{U}$ is not assumed to be both bounded and convex.

Prove or disprove: outside the trivial situations (in which $\mathcal{U}$ is closed and convex with $J$ convex and coercive in $u$, or in which $\mathcal{U}$ is closed bounded and convex with $J$ convex in $u$), there exists an admissible control $u^\ast(\cdot)$ minimizing $J$. Specifically, develop either
(i) a verification theorem identifying an optimal control through the value function or an associated Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman / Riccati-type equation, or
(ii) a compactness argument showing that any minimizing sequence $\{u_n(\cdot)\}$ admits a subsequence whose corresponding state-control pair converges to an admissible optimal pair,
in a genuinely nontrivial setting for the above class of stochastic distributed parameter systems.
status_search_result: The literature indicates that existence of optimal controls for stochastic distributed parameter systems (controlled SPDEs) is well understood only in special cases (e.g., convex coercive costs on closed convex control sets, or convex costs on closed bounded convex control sets). General verification theorems and compactness-of-minimizing-sequences techniques have not been developed beyond these trivial cases. Recent surveys on control theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems list this as an open problem; we found no publication establishing a general existence result in genuinely nontrivial settings.

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
original_question: What general mathematical connection links controllability theory and optimal control theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems, especially for problems with endpoint state constraints, and how can the initial finite-codimensional exact controllability results be extended into a broader theory?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic distributed parameter system (SDPS) of the form
   dy(t) = (A y(t) + B u(t)) dt + (C y(t) + D u(t)) dW(t),  t ∈ (0, T],   y(0) = y₀,
on a separable Hilbert space H, where A generates a C₀-semigroup, B, C, D are suitable (possibly unbounded) linear operators, W is a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion on a filtered probability space, the control u belongs to an admissible set U_ad ⊂ L²_F(0,T; U) (U a Hilbert space), and the state y is an H-valued adapted process. Given a closed subspace (or convex set) Q ⊂ L²_{F_T}(Ω; H) representing endpoint state constraints y(T) ∈ Q, and a cost functional
   J(u) = E[ ∫₀ᵀ ℓ(t, y(t), u(t)) dt + h(y(T)) ],
the system is said to be finite-codimensional exactly controllable (with respect to a finite-codimensional subspace of H) at time T if the reachable set {y(T; u) : u ∈ U_ad} contains an affine subspace of finite codimension in L²_{F_T}(Ω; H).

Develop a general theory linking controllability and optimal control for such SDPS with endpoint state constraints by accomplishing the following:

(a) Formulate and prove a Pontryagin-type maximum principle for optimal controls of the constrained problem (minimize J over u ∈ U_ad subject to y(T) ∈ Q) in which the nontriviality of the adjoint variables is guaranteed precisely by a finite-codimensional exact controllability property of the linearized SDPS along the optimal trajectory.

(b) Identify sharp sufficient conditions (in terms of observability/Gårding-type inequalities for the associated backward stochastic adjoint equation) under which finite-codimensional exact controllability of the linearized SDPS holds, and show how these conditions yield the nontriviality of the Lagrange multipliers in (a).

(c) Extend the theory beyond the linear setting (semilinear/quasilinear SDPS, degenerate noise, unbounded control operators) and derive analogous equivalences between qualitative controllability properties and the well-posedness/nontriviality of first- and second-order necessary optimality conditions for endpoint-constrained stochastic optimal control problems.
status_search_result: Initial findings linking finite-codimensional exact controllability with optimal control problems with endpoint state constraints (in the deterministic setting) appear in Wang–Yong–Zhang (J. Math. Pures Appl., 2020; arXiv:1810.01334), where the connection is reduced to a Gårding-type inequality for the adjoint system. A general theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems is acknowledged as an open program; the recent monograph "Mathematical Control Theory for Stochastic Partial Differential Equations" (Springer, 2021) and surveys describe many directions still to be developed. No comprehensive resolution has been published.

paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
original_question: In stochastic distributed parameter systems, uncertainty often makes control harder, but it can also create advantages. What mathematically useful benefits can be obtained from uncertainty, and how can those benefits be characterized and exploited systematically?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic distributed parameter system (SDPS), i.e., a controlled stochastic evolution equation of the form
$$ dy(t) = (A y(t) + B u(t) + F(t,y(t)))\,dt + (C y(t) + D u(t) + G(t,y(t)))\,dW(t), \quad t\in[0,T], \ y(0)=y_0, $$
posed in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$, where $A$ generates a $C_0$-semigroup on $H$, $B,C,D$ are bounded (or suitably unbounded) operators, $F,G$ are nonlinear coefficients with appropriate regularity, $W$ is a cylindrical Wiener process on a separable Hilbert space, $u$ is a control taking values in another Hilbert space $U$, and $y_0\in H$. Standard control-theoretic objects (controllability, observability, stabilizability, optimal control, filtering) are defined for such systems in the usual way; in particular, exact/approximate/null controllability, mean-square stabilizability, and observability inequalities for the dual backward stochastic system are formulated as in the deterministic distributed parameter setting, adapted to mean-square or pathwise senses.

It is well known that introducing the diffusion terms (via $C$, $D$, or $G$) generically makes such control problems harder than their deterministic analogues (e.g., loss of exact controllability, weaker observability, restricted classes of admissible controls). However, there are situations where the presence of noise yields advantages absent in the deterministic case, such as: (i) noise-induced stabilization of otherwise unstable systems, (ii) improved (or otherwise unattainable) controllability/observability properties, (iii) regularization of solutions and well-posedness of equations that are ill-posed without noise, and (iv) creation of new admissible structures for optimal control.

Problem. Develop a systematic mathematical framework that identifies, classifies, and quantifies the beneficial effects of stochastic perturbations in SDPSs. Specifically:

1. Provide precise structural conditions on the operators $A, B, C, D$ and on the noise covariance/coefficients $G$ under which the stochastic system enjoys a controllability, observability, stabilizability, or regularity property that fails for the corresponding deterministic system (with $C=D=0$ and $G\equiv 0$).

2. Establish quantitative observability/controllability inequalities that exhibit explicit improvement (in constants, function spaces, or admissible target sets) due to the noise, and characterize the sharp dependence of these inequalities on the noise intensity.

3. Characterize, in terms of intrinsic spectral or geometric data of $(A,B,C,D,G)$, the precise mechanisms (e.g., hypoellipticity, noise-induced mixing, Lyapunov-type dissipation generated by the Itô correction) responsible for these advantages, and produce a general theorem stating necessary and sufficient conditions for noise to yield an advantage of each type (i)–(iv).

4. Exploit the framework to design control strategies that deliberately use stochastic perturbations to achieve performance unattainable by deterministic controls, and prove their optimality within an appropriate class.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open research direction: identifying and systematically exploiting the benefits of uncertainty in stochastic distributed parameter systems. While individual phenomena (noise-induced stabilization, regularization by noise for SPDEs, hypoelliptic controllability) are studied in the literature, no general unifying framework appears to have been established, and the problem is presented as far from being understood. No source was found indicating a comprehensive resolution.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
context_brief: open mapping theorem; boundary of range
original_question: Let D be a plane domain, and let K be an analytic multifunction on D whose values K(z) are polynomially convex for every z in D. Is it always true that every point of K(D) lying outside the interior of K(D) belongs to every fiber K(z)? Equivalently, must K(D) \ int(K(D)) be contained in the intersection of the sets K(z) over all z in D?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a domain in the complex plane. An analytic multifunction $K$ on $D$ is a map assigning to each $z \in D$ a non-empty compact subset $K(z) \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ such that the graph $\{(z,w) \in D \times \mathbb{C} : w \in K(z)\}$ is closed and the complement $(D \times \mathbb{C}) \setminus \mathrm{graph}(K)$ is pseudoconvex (equivalently, $z \mapsto \log\,\mathrm{dist}(w, K(z))$ is superharmonic for every fixed $w \in \mathbb{C}$, after the standard adjustments). A compact set $L \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is polynomially convex if it equals its polynomial hull $\widehat{L} = \{w \in \mathbb{C} : |p(w)| \le \max_{L} |p| \text{ for every polynomial } p\}$.

Set $K(D) = \bigcup_{z \in D} K(z)$ and let $\mathrm{int}(K(D))$ denote its topological interior in $\mathbb{C}$.

Question. Suppose that $K$ is an analytic multifunction on $D$ such that $K(z)$ is polynomially convex for every $z \in D$. Must every point of $K(D)$ that does not lie in $\mathrm{int}(K(D))$ belong to $K(z)$ for every $z \in D$? Equivalently, does the inclusion
$$K(D) \setminus \mathrm{int}(K(D)) \;\subseteq\; \bigcap_{z \in D} K(z)$$
always hold?
status_search_result: The question is a known open problem in the theory of analytic multifunctions, associated with open mapping-type theorems for polynomially convex valued analytic multifunctions. Special cases (e.g., convex-valued or polar-valued multifunctions) have been settled affirmatively, but the general case appears to remain unresolved according to available references on analytic multifunctions and polynomial convexity.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
original_question: Let D be a plane domain, and let K be a polar-valued analytic multifunction on D. Is graph(K) a complete pluripolar set, meaning that there exists a plurisubharmonic function v on D x C such that the set where v = -infinity is exactly graph(K)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a domain. A multifunction $K$ on $D$ assigns to each $z \in D$ a nonempty compact subset $K(z) \subset \mathbb{C}$. Such a $K$ is called an analytic multifunction if its graph $\operatorname{graph}(K) = \{(z,w) \in D \times \mathbb{C} : w \in K(z)\}$ is closed in $D \times \mathbb{C}$ and, for every plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $D \times \mathbb{C}$, the function $z \mapsto \sup\{u(z,w) : w \in K(z)\}$ is subharmonic on $D$. The multifunction $K$ is called polar-valued if for each $z \in D$ the fiber $K(z)$ is a polar subset of $\mathbb{C}$ (i.e., there exists a subharmonic function on $\mathbb{C}$, not identically $-\infty$, that equals $-\infty$ on $K(z)$).

A subset $E \subset D \times \mathbb{C}$ is called complete pluripolar if there exists a plurisubharmonic function $v$ on $D \times \mathbb{C}$ such that $E = \{(z,w) \in D \times \mathbb{C} : v(z,w) = -\infty\}$.

Question: Is it true that for every polar-valued analytic multifunction $K$ on $D$, the set $\operatorname{graph}(K)$ is complete pluripolar in $D \times \mathbb{C}$?

However, no source directly resolves the question for general polar-valued analytic multifunctions. The status of this specific question could not be confirmed from the search; it appears to remain an open question in the theory of analytic multifunctions.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
original_question: Let D be a plane domain. Suppose K1 and K2 are analytic multifunctions on D whose values are sequences tending to zero. If K1 = K2 on a subset of D having a limit point in D, must K1 and K2 be identical on all of D?
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real (or complex) sequences converging to zero, equipped with the supremum norm. A set-valued map $K$ defined on a plane domain $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ that assigns to each $\lambda \in D$ a nonempty compact subset $K(\lambda) \subset c_0$ is called an analytic multifunction on $D$ if it is upper semicontinuous and if, for every plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $c_0$, the function $\lambda \mapsto \sup\{\varphi(x) : x \in K(\lambda)\}$ is subharmonic on $D$.

Suppose $K_1$ and $K_2$ are two analytic multifunctions on $D$ whose values are compact subsets of $c_0$ (i.e., compact sets of sequences tending to zero). Assume that the set $\{\lambda \in D : K_1(\lambda) = K_2(\lambda)\}$ has a limit point in $D$.

Must it follow that $K_1(\lambda) = K_2(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda \in D$?
status_search_result: A survey listing open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions states this question as Problem F and notes that, to the authors' knowledge, it remains open. While an identity principle is known for analytic multifunctions valued in $\ell^p$-sequences with locally bounded $\ell^p$-norms, the analogous statement for $c_0$-valued multifunctions has not been established.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
original_question: For each integer n at least 1, let F_n be the family of degree-n analytic multifunctions K on the unit disk D such that a1'(0) = 1 in the representation K(z) = {w in C : w^n + a1(z) w^(n-1) + ... + a_n(z) = 0}. Let L_n be the infimum, over K in F_n, of the supremum of radii r such that K(D) contains a disk of radius r. Since n L_n is bounded above by Landau's constant L and the limit of n L_n as n tends to infinity exists, determine that limit. In particular, is the limit positive or zero?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. Fix an integer $n\geq 1$. An analytic multifunction $K$ on $\mathbb{D}$ of degree $n$ is a set-valued map of the form
$$K(z)=\{w\in\mathbb{C}: w^n+a_1(z)w^{n-1}+a_2(z)w^{n-2}+\cdots+a_n(z)=0\},$$
where $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ are holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$. Let $\mathcal{F}_n$ be the family of all such degree-$n$ analytic multifunctions $K$ on $\mathbb{D}$ that satisfy the normalization $a_1'(0)=1$. For $K\in\mathcal{F}_n$, write $K(\mathbb{D})=\bigcup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}K(z)\subset\mathbb{C}$, and define
$$\rho(K)=\sup\{r\geq 0 : K(\mathbb{D}) \text{ contains some open disk of radius } r\}.$$
Set
$$L_n=\inf_{K\in\mathcal{F}_n}\rho(K).$$
It is known that $L_n>0$ for every $n\geq 1$, that $nL_n\leq L$ for all $n$ (where $L$ denotes Landau's constant), and that the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty} nL_n$ exists. Determine the value of
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} nL_n.$$
In particular, decide whether this limit is strictly positive or equal to zero.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in a survey on analytic multifunctions. A web search returns the survey itself and related work by Ransford and collaborators on Bloch-type theorems for analytic multifunctions, but no source identifying the value of the limit or settling its positivity. No publication appears to resolve the question.

context_brief: Orders of vanishing at negative integers
original_question: What is the correct general description of the orders of vanishing of function-field zeta functions at negative integers, including an explanation of the systematic extra-vanishing phenomena that depend on the digit combinatorics of the integer s and on Weierstrass gaps?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a global function field with field of constants $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $\zeta_K(s)$ denote the associated Goss zeta function (a characteristic-$p$ analogue of the Dedekind zeta function, taking values in a Tate algebra and admitting an analytic continuation to a "complex plane" $\mathbb{C}_\infty^* \times \mathbb{Z}_p$). For each negative integer $-s$ (with $s$ a positive integer), $\zeta_K$ vanishes at $-s$, and beyond the "naive" order of vanishing predicted by an analogue of the gamma-factor analysis used in the classical case, additional systematic "extra vanishing" is known to occur. This extra vanishing depends in a subtle way on:
\begin{itemize}
\item the combinatorics of the base-$q$ digits of the positive integer $s$, and
\item the Weierstrass gap sequence at the place at infinity (or more generally, the Weierstrass gaps of $K$).
\end{itemize}

Problem. Give a correct general formula or conjectural description for the exact order of vanishing $\mathrm{ord}_{s=-n}\,\zeta_K(s)$ at every negative integer $-n$, valid for arbitrary global function fields $K/\mathbb{F}_q$, that simultaneously accounts for:
(i) the trivial zeros coming from the gamma-factor / functional-equation analogy,
(ii) the extra zeros depending on the $q$-adic digit combinatorics of $n$, and
(iii) the contribution of the Weierstrass gaps of $K$.

original_question: For the ℘-adic interpolation of the arithmetic gamma function constructed by Goss, what is the general transcendence or algebraicity theory for its values, beyond the partial results currently known?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ be the polynomial ring over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q$ a power of a prime $p$, let $K=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$ be its fraction field, and let $K_\infty=\mathbb{F}_q((1/T))$ be its completion at the infinite place. Fix a monic irreducible polynomial $\wp\in A$, let $K_\wp$ denote the $\wp$-adic completion of $K$, and let $\mathbb{C}_\wp$ denote the completion of an algebraic closure of $K_\wp$.

The Carlitz factorial $D_i\in A$ is defined by $D_0=1$ and $D_i=\prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(T^{q^i}-T^{q^j})$ for $i\ge 1$. The arithmetic factorial of a non-negative integer $n=\sum_{i\ge 0}n_i q^i$ (with $0\le n_i<q$) is
$$\Pi(n)=\prod_{i\ge 0} D_i^{n_i}\in A.$$
Goss constructed, for each finite place $\wp$ of $A$, a $\wp$-adic interpolation
$$\Gamma_\wp:\mathbb{Z}_p\longrightarrow K_\wp$$
of this arithmetic gamma function (the analogue of Morita's $p$-adic gamma function in the function field setting), characterized by suitably interpolating the values $\Pi(n)$ with the $\wp$-factors removed at non-negative integers $n$.

Problem. Determine the complete transcendence theory of the values of $\Gamma_\wp$ at points of $\mathbb{Z}_p$. Specifically:

(i) For every $z\in\mathbb{Z}_p\setminus\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, decide whether $\Gamma_\wp(z)$ is transcendental over $K$.

(ii) For each finite tuple $z_1,\dots,z_r\in\mathbb{Z}_p$, describe all algebraic relations over $\overline{K}$ among the values $\Gamma_\wp(z_1),\dots,\Gamma_\wp(z_r)$, and prove that these relations are exhausted by those induced by the functional equations satisfied by $\Gamma_\wp$.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers indicate that while transcendence of Carlitz–Goss gamma values at non-natural rational/p-adic arguments has been established in partial cases (via Wade's method, Drinfeld modules, hypergeometric techniques), the full transcendence/algebraic-independence theory for all values of Goss's ℘-adic interpolation of the arithmetic gamma function is not complete. Work by Anderson, Thakur, Chang, Yu and others has resolved the v=∞ (Carlitz period and arithmetic gamma at ∞) case completely, but the general ℘-adic case remains only partially understood.

paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
original_question: For each integer n at least 10, is the connected n-vertex graph with maximum irregularity always a pineapple graph PA(n,q), where a pineapple graph consists of a q-vertex clique together with an independent set on the remaining n−q vertices such that every vertex of the independent set is adjacent to one and the same clique vertex, and where the conjectured optimal clique size is q = ceil(n/2) + 1? Equivalently, does this specific pineapple maximize λ1(G) − d̄(G) over all connected graphs G on n vertices, where λ1(G) is the largest adjacency eigenvalue and d̄(G) is the average degree?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \geq 10$ and an integer $q$ with $1 \leq q \leq n$, define the pineapple graph $PA(n,q)$ as the graph on $n$ vertices obtained from a clique $K_q$ on $q$ vertices together with an independent set $I$ on the remaining $n-q$ vertices, by joining every vertex of $I$ to one fixed (common) vertex of the clique. For a simple connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\lambda_1(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of $G$, and let $\bar d(G) = \frac{2|E(G)|}{n}$ denote the average degree. Define the irregularity of $G$ as $\varepsilon(G) = \lambda_1(G) - \bar d(G)$.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n \geq 10$, the unique connected graph on $n$ vertices that maximizes $\varepsilon(G)$ is the pineapple graph $PA(n,q)$ with $q = \lceil n/2 \rceil + 1$.
status_search_result: Tait and Tobin (2016, "Three conjectures in extremal spectral graph theory", arXiv:1606.01916) proved the conjecture of Aouchiche et al. that for sufficiently large $n$, the unique connected $n$-vertex graph maximizing $\lambda_1(G) - \bar d(G)$ is the pineapple graph $PA(n, \lceil n/2\rceil + 1)$.

paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
original_question: Is it true that every simple graph G on n vertices satisfies λ1(G) + λ1(Ḡ) ≤ (4/3)n − 5/3 minus the residue-class correction stated in the source, namely f1(n) when n mod 3 = 1, 0 when n mod 3 = 2, and f2(n) when n mod 3 = 0, where f1(n) = (3n − 2 − sqrt(9n^2 − 12n + 12))/6 and f2(n) = (3n − 1 − sqrt(9n^2 − 6n + 9))/6? If so, are the equality cases exactly the graphs G or complements Ḡ that are complete split graphs whose independent set has size floor(n/3), and also size ceil(n/3) when n mod 3 = 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph on n vertices, let Ḡ denote its complement, and let λ₁(H) denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix) of a graph H. Define
  f₁(n) = (3n − 2 − √(9n² − 12n + 12))/6,
  f₂(n) = (3n − 1 − √(9n² − 6n + 9))/6,
and the residue-class correction
  c(n) = f₁(n) if n ≡ 1 (mod 3),
  c(n) = 0     if n ≡ 2 (mod 3),
  c(n) = f₂(n) if n ≡ 0 (mod 3).
A complete split graph CS(n,k) is the graph on n vertices obtained as the join of a clique on n−k vertices and an independent set on k vertices.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every simple graph G on n vertices,
   λ₁(G) + λ₁(Ḡ) ≤ (4n − 5)/3 − c(n).

(b) If the inequality in (a) holds, determine whether equality is attained exactly when G or Ḡ is isomorphic to a complete split graph CS(n, ⌊n/3⌋), with the additional case CS(n, ⌈n/3⌉) when n ≡ 2 (mod 3).

paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
context_brief: Maximum energy of bicyclic molecular graphs
original_question: For n = 14 and for every n at least 16, is the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximum energy equal to P_n^{6;6}, where a molecular graph means a connected graph of maximum degree at most 4 and P_n^{6;6} is the graph formed from two 6-cycles and a path P(n−12) by joining one endpoint of the path to one cycle and the other endpoint to the other cycle by single edges?
self_contained_problem:
A molecular graph is a connected simple graph in which every vertex has degree at most 4. A bicyclic graph is a connected simple graph with exactly n edges on n vertices (equivalently, a connected graph with cyclomatic number 2). The energy E(G) of a graph G is defined as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix.

For an integer n ≥ 13, let P_n^{6;6} denote the graph obtained as follows: take two vertex-disjoint copies of the 6-cycle C_6 and a path P_{n−12} on n−12 vertices, then join one endpoint of the path by a single edge to a vertex of the first C_6 and the other endpoint of the path by a single edge to a vertex of the second C_6. (For n = 14, this construction is interpreted with the path P_2 having two endpoints, and for n = 13 with a single vertex serving as the path P_1, but here we consider n = 14 and n ≥ 16.)

Prove or disprove: for n = 14 and for every integer n ≥ 16, among all bicyclic molecular graphs on n vertices, the graph P_n^{6;6} is the unique one attaining the maximum energy E(G).
status_search_result: The bipartite case of the conjecture was fully resolved by Huo, Ji, Li and Shi (2011), and further partial progress has been made for several classes of non-bipartite bicyclic graphs (e.g., bicyclic graphs containing one even and one odd cycle, and bicyclic graphs containing two odd cycles with one common vertex, the latter settled in 2024). The full conjecture for general (not necessarily bipartite) bicyclic molecular graphs remains open.

paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
original_question: For every tetracyclic graph G on n vertices with n at least 26, is the energy of G at most the energy of P_n^{6,6;6,6}, with equality only for P_n^{6,6;6,6}? Here P_n^{6,6;6,6} denotes the graph obtained from four copies of C6 and a path P(n−24) by adding a single edge from two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the other two 6-cycles to the other endpoint.
self_contained_problem:
The energy of a finite simple graph $G$ is defined as $E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\lambda_i|$, where $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ are the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$. A connected graph on $n$ vertices is called tetracyclic (or quadricyclic) if it has exactly $n+3$ edges (equivalently, cyclomatic number $4$).

For each integer $n\ge 26$, define the graph $P_n^{6,6;6,6}$ as follows. Take four vertex-disjoint copies $C^{(1)},C^{(2)},C^{(3)},C^{(4)}$ of the cycle $C_6$ and a vertex-disjoint path $P_{n-24}$ on $n-24$ vertices with endpoints $u$ and $v$. Choose one vertex $x_i$ in each $C^{(i)}$. Add the edges $x_1u$, $x_2u$, $x_3v$, $x_4v$. The resulting graph has $n$ vertices and $4\cdot 6 + (n-25) + 4 = n+3$ edges, hence is tetracyclic.

Prove or disprove: for every tetracyclic graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $n\ge 26$,
$$E(G)\le E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}),$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong P_n^{6,6;6,6}$.

The unicyclic case has been fully resolved and the tricyclic analogue (with $P_n^{6,6,6}$) is partially known but still open in general; no source located indicates that the tetracyclic conjecture identifying $P_n^{6,6;6,6}$ as the unique maximum-energy tetracyclic graph for $n\ge 26$ has been proved or disproved. It appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems for equienergetic graphs.
original_question: Given two non-cospectral graphs of the same order that appear, from numerical computation, to have equal graph energy, find a general proof method that can rigorously establish that they are equienergetic. Here the energy of a graph is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and two graphs of the same order are equienergetic when these energies are equal.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix A(G), and let λ_1, λ_2, …, λ_n denote the (real) eigenvalues of A(G). Define the energy of G by

  E(G) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|.

Two graphs G and H of the same order n are called cospectral if A(G) and A(H) have the same multiset of eigenvalues, and equienergetic if E(G) = E(H). Note that cospectral graphs are automatically equienergetic, so the interesting case is non-cospectral equienergetic pairs.

Problem. Develop a general proof method with the following property: given any two non-cospectral graphs G and H of the same order n whose energies, computed numerically, appear to coincide, the method rigorously establishes (or refutes) the exact equality E(G) = E(H). Equivalently, find a general technique that, applied to an arbitrary pair of non-cospectral graphs of the same order, decides whether they are equienergetic without relying on a specific ad hoc construction.
status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as an open problem in spectral graph theory. While many ad hoc constructions of non-cospectral equienergetic graph pairs and infinite families exist (via graph operations, line graphs, signed graphs, complementary equienergetic graphs, etc.), recent literature continues to state that no general method is known to prove equienergeticity of two arbitrary non-cospectral graphs whose energies merely appear numerically equal.
